# Spam likely overview
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/telephony/call_efficiency_overview

Why phone numbers get marked "Spam Likely" by carriers and how Retell verified phone numbers and branded call services raise pickup rates on outbound calls.

![Spam Likely](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/_FxJdxv7mQoPqyGs/images/vp.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_FxJdxv7mQoPqyGs\&q=85\&s=deb425180734b50c28afc089f080c0ae)

Spam Likely

![Apply for branded call](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/zL2HeUqUnagEN9eK/images/b_1.PNG?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=zL2HeUqUnagEN9eK\&q=85\&s=0eab2bc57f4ac8831f0ab29267cfc421)

Branded Call

Phone carriers may mark certain phone numbers as "Spam Likely". This lowers your outbound call pickup rate, and can sometimes lead telephony providers to ban your number or account.

## Check whether your number is marked as spam likely

Check your outbound call log for calls that failed to connect with SIP error code 608. That code means the call was rejected for being marked as spam likely. Not every spam-likely rejection returns error code 608, though.

A few external services can help you check whether your number is marked as spam likely. Results aren't exact, since each carrier has its own rules and database, but you can use them as a reference:

* [Nomorobo](https://www.nomorobo.com/): use the app or API to check your number against its database.
* [IPQualityScore](https://www.ipqualityscore.com/phone-number-validator): check your phone number's reputation score.

## Actions you can take

Retell provides two services to improve your call pickup rate:

1. **[Verified phone number](/build/telephony/verified-phone)**: Retell will register your number with the phone carrier, which will not be marked as spam by carriers.
2. **[Branded call](/build/telephony/branded-call)**: Callee will see your number as your business name, instead of the generic Retell number.

Both services require a verified [business profile](/build/telephony/business-profile) first. If an application is rejected, see [how to handle a rejection](/build/telephony/branded-call-rejection). To stop a service later, see [stop caller ID service](/build/telephony/delete-service).

## iOS 26 call screening

iPhones on iOS 26 may deploy a [call screening feature](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/screen-and-block-calls-iphe4b3f7823/ios). At the start of the call, Siri asks unknown numbers to provide their name and reason for calling.
To pass this screen, update your agent prompt to respond clearly. For example:

```
## FAQ
Q: Hi, if you record your name and reason for calling, I'll see if this person is available
A: In one sentence, introduce yourself and explain why you are calling. <wait for response>
```

![iOS Call Screen](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/nRxhsVoMBWNZU20m/images/iOS_call_screen.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=nRxhsVoMBWNZU20m\&q=85\&s=4662d60d9f84b23883335985f4841845)

iOS Call Screen


# Stop caller ID service
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/telephony/delete-service

Stop active Retell caller-ID services — branded calls and verified phone numbers — without interrupting your underlying telephony or live agent calls.

You can stop an active caller ID service at any time. These services — [branded calls](/build/telephony/branded-call) and [verified phone numbers](/build/telephony/verified-phone) — are add-ons layered on top of your underlying telephony. **Stopping them does not interrupt calls.** Your agents will continue making and receiving calls; only the associated caller ID enhancement or number verification will be removed.

![Delete service](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/rxvYffEkEJPRL1KD/images/delete_service.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=rxvYffEkEJPRL1KD\&q=85\&s=1ab297f0299ad72e27b8966f4530ea4d)

## What gets removed

* **Branded Calls** — your branded caller ID will no longer appear on the recipient's screen. Calls will still connect, but will present as a standard unbranded call.
* **Verified Phone Numbers** — your number's spam remediation registration is removed. The number may begin appearing as "Spam Risk" or "Scam Likely" on recipient devices until re-registered.

## Billing

### Branded Calls

Billing continues until the end of your current billing cycle. You will retain branded caller ID display for the remainder of the paid period even after initiating the stop.

### Verified Phone Numbers

Billing stops immediately upon service deletion. You will only be charged for the portion of the billing cycle the service was active.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you plan to [re-register a verified phone number](/build/telephony/verified-phone) in the future, be aware that the re-registration process can take time. Your number may be flagged as spam in the interim.


# Set & parse custom SIP headers
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/telephony/sip-headers

Use custom SIP headers in Retell to pass metadata on inbound and outbound calls, transfers, and agent hangups, with dynamic values from the conversation.

Use custom SIP headers to pass metadata between your systems and Retell on a call — for example, forwarding an account ID or a caller reference from your [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony) platform so the agent can use it during the conversation.

> [!NOTE]
>
> SIP headers are available for phone calls only. Retell receives SIP headers on inbound calls, and sets them on outbound calls, transfers, and agent hangups.

Many SIP parsers and middleboxes assume 1024 bytes is a reasonable maximum for a header line, and may reject or truncate longer headers unless configured to allow more.

## Parse custom SIP headers for inbound calls

For inbound calls, custom SIP headers (those starting with `X-` or `x-`) are received and extracted automatically into `call.custom_sip_headers`. They are also added to your [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables), where you access them by stripping the `X-` or `x-` prefix. No configuration is needed.

For example, if this is the SIP header received for an inbound call:

```json theme={"dark"}
{
  "X-test-header": "something",
  "X-another-header": "something else",
  "from": "1234567890",
  "to": "0987654321"
}
```

Then here's your `call.custom_sip_headers` field, and they will be added to your dynamic variables.

```json theme={"dark"}
{
  "test-header": "something",
  "another-header": "something else"
}
```

If you have already specified dynamic variables with the same name for this inbound call, it will override the value received from the SIP header.

## Set custom SIP headers for outbound calls

![Outbound call dialog with a custom SIP header key and value being added.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/rxvYffEkEJPRL1KD/images/deploy/phone-call/outbound-call.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=rxvYffEkEJPRL1KD\&q=85\&s=a19d395e5d5d2005d6f3937c6aa35055)

For outbound calls, you can add custom SIP headers as needed. Each must start with `X-`.

## Set custom SIP headers for call transfers

For call transfers, header names must start with `X-` or `x-`, or be `User-to-User` or `Diversion` (case-insensitive). You can use a dynamic variable for the header value to pass information extracted from the call to the receiving party.

> [!WARNING]
>
> For cold transfer with transferee number, it will use SIP REFER to transfer the call. Different telephony providers may or may NOT honor the custom SIP headers in the REFER request. Twilio, for example, does not honor the custom SIP headers in the REFER request, so the SIP headers you set in the transfer call tool will not work for cold transfer with transferee number when using Twilio.

If you are using:

* Conversation flow agents, check out [call transfer node](/build/conversation-flow/call-transfer-node#configure-transfer) for more details.
* Single / multi agent, check out [call transfer function](/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call) for more details.

## Set custom SIP headers when ending a call

Use end-call headers to pass a call outcome or reference ID to your SIP system when the agent hangs up through an [End Call tool](/build/single-multi-prompt/end-call) or [end node](/build/conversation-flow/end-node). These headers are optional; none are configured by default.

For example, after booking an appointment, send `X-Call-Outcome` with the value `booked` and `X-Appointment-ID` with the value `{{appointment_id}}`. Set the `appointment_id` [dynamic variable](/build/dynamic-variables) during the conversation before ending the call. Retell resolves the value when the tool or node executes.

**1. Open the end-call settings**

For a single- or multi-prompt agent, add or edit the **End Call** tool. In a conversation flow, select an end node and open its settings. You can also configure headers on an End Call tool attached to a [subagent node](/build/conversation-flow/subagent-node).

**2. Add header names and values**

Under **Custom SIP Headers**, click **Add** for each key/value pair. Use a literal header name beginning with `X-` or `x-`, and a static string or dynamic variable for its value.

**3. Save the headers**

Save the End Call tool. End-node headers save when you leave the edited field. To stop sending a header, remove its row; remove all rows to clear the configuration.

![End Call dialog with Custom SIP Headers outlined in blue, showing the X-Ticket-ID header with the ticket_id dynamic variable as its value.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/xnGtpZfvieBKNmwD/images/end-call-sip-headers.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=xnGtpZfvieBKNmwD\&q=85\&s=999cc5b92ffb208e9c65b70e01573504)

Use a dynamic variable to send the ticket ID when the agent ends the call.

### Which header names are allowed?

End-call header names must start with `X-` or `x-`. Unlike transfer headers, `User-to-User` and `Diversion` are not allowed. Standard headers such as `Reason` are also rejected.

The dashboard blocks saving a row with a value but no name, an unsupported name, or a duplicate name. Names are compared without case, so `X-Ticket` and `x-ticket` count as duplicates. Correct the name or remove the duplicate row, then save again.

These settings apply when the configured tool or node ends a phone call. They do not apply to chat or to a caller hanging up first.

# Transcription modes
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/transcription-mode

Configure Retell AI transcription modes for speed or accuracy, choose a custom speech recognition provider, and override settings in conversation flow nodes.

Transcription Mode controls how Retell turns the caller's speech into text. Choose an agent-wide default, then override it in individual conversation or subagent nodes when a step needs different transcription settings.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Transcription modes apply to cascading voice agents, which use a separate speech recognition provider. They do not apply to chat agents or speech-to-speech models.

## Which mode should I use?

* **Optimize for speed**: Use for responsive conversation. This is the default when no mode is configured.
* **Optimize for accuracy**: Try this when collecting details such as account numbers or dates, or when transcripts cut off before the caller finishes.
* **Custom Settings**: Choose a [speech recognition provider](/build/asr-providers) and tune its endpointing for your use case.

The presets use provider configurations chosen for the agent's languages. Their latency difference depends on the language and provider; accuracy mode does not add a fixed delay. Hover over **(Provider Config)** beside a preset to see its current provider and endpointing in a tooltip. It isn't clickable.

For example, an appointment-booking flow can use speed mode globally and accuracy mode only in the node that collects a date of birth. Later nodes without an override use the global mode again.

## Set the agent default

Open **Realtime transcription settings** in the agent editor and find **Transcription Mode**. For a conversation flow, select **Global settings** first. Choose a preset or configure [Custom Settings](#custom-settings).

![Global settings with Transcription Mode highlighted: Optimize for speed is selected, with Optimize for accuracy and Custom Settings also available.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/9F0TkPfPICAMToGX/images/transcription-global-modes.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=9F0TkPfPICAMToGX\&q=85\&s=db31a731cf5ff56cca7fe7a59c3ba37f)

Choose the agent default under Realtime transcription settings. Optimize for speed is selected here.

## Override transcription for a node

[Conversation nodes](/build/conversation-flow/conversation-node) and [subagent nodes](/build/conversation-flow/subagent-node) support their own transcription mode.

![Node settings with the Transcription Mode override enabled and highlighted. Optimize for accuracy is selected; speed and Custom Settings are also available.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/PVVZlJBBrM_spnAP/images/transcription-node-override.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=PVVZlJBBrM_spnAP\&q=85\&s=3273cbc675d101574cd68321de49db47)

Enable Transcription Mode in Node settings, then choose a mode. Optimize for accuracy is selected here.

**1. Open the node settings**

Select the node on the canvas, then select **Node settings** in the right panel. Expand the **Node settings** section if it is collapsed.

**2. Enable the transcription override**

Under **Node-level overrides**, turn on **Transcription Mode**. It starts with the agent's current global mode. For a custom global mode, it also starts with the global provider and endpointing, where supported.

**3. Choose the node's mode**

Select **Optimize for speed**, **Optimize for accuracy**, or **Custom Settings**. The setting applies while this node is active. On transition, Retell restores the agent default and applies the next node's override, if any.

**4. Test the relevant part of the flow**

Use a [web test](/test/test-web) to check the transcript and response timing for that step. Turn off the node's **Transcription Mode** override to inherit the global setting again.

An enabled override keeps its own values when you change the global mode. Turn it off if the node should follow future global changes.

To change which names or terms the transcriber favors, configure a [node boosted-keyword override](/reliability/wrong-transcript#override-boosted-keywords-for-a-node). It works independently of the transcription mode.

## Custom settings

Select **Custom Settings**, then choose a **Provider** that supports all of the agent's selected languages. For providers with an **Endpointing** control, adjust how long the transcriber waits to finalize speech. A longer window can help callers who pause while reading numbers, but can also delay the agent's response.

![Node transcription override with Custom Settings selected, Deepgram as the provider, and the Endpointing slider set to 1000ms, highlighted in blue.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/PVVZlJBBrM_spnAP/images/transcription-node-custom.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=PVVZlJBBrM_spnAP\&q=85\&s=af72249d7ad2f369ed9f9809e3c96881)

Custom Settings exposes the provider and endpointing controls. This node uses Deepgram with 1,000 ms endpointing.

**Endpointing** is separate from [Response Wait time](/build/conversation-flow/global-setting#configure-speech-settings), which adds a minimum wait before the agent responds. Check both settings when troubleshooting slow replies.

The dashboard offers these endpointing controls, in milliseconds (as of October 2026):

| Provider | Slider range | Default when no value is configured |
| - | - | - |
| Deepgram | 100–10,000 ms | 1,000 ms |
| Azure | 100–10,000 ms | 1,000 ms |
| Soniox | 500–3,000 ms | 1,500 ms |
| AssemblyAI | 100–3,000 ms | 1,500 ms |

When changing providers, the dashboard preserves the existing endpointing value where it fits the new provider's range. These are dashboard slider bounds; API validation limits can differ.

The selected provider is tried first. Retell can still use fallback providers if it becomes unavailable. See [provider selection and fallback](/build/asr-providers#how-retell-picks-a-provider).

## FAQ

> [accordion] Why is Custom Settings unavailable for my node?
>
> The dashboard needs to load language support and find a provider that supports every selected language. If loading fails, use **Retry loading language support**. If no provider covers the combination, choose a preset or change the [agent languages](/agent/multilingual). If the global mode is custom and no compatible provider is available, change the global mode to a preset before enabling the node override.

> [accordion] Does a node override change the whole agent?
>
> No. It applies while that node is active. Other nodes inherit the global mode unless they have their own override. Turning off an override removes its node-specific mode and custom configuration.


# Set up TTS fallback
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/tts-fallback

Configure TTS fallback voices so Retell agents keep speaking during a TTS provider outage — required when using custom or third-party provider voices.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you are using a [platform voice](/build/platform-voices) or a standard Retell voice from the voice library, fallback is handled automatically — no additional setup is required. The steps below apply only if you are using a custom or third-party provider voice.

There might be cases where the TTS provider is having outages or temporary issues, but the agents need to keep talking to the user on call. Thus fallback and retries here are necessary. Fallback will use a different voice provider.

Currently if no specific TTS fallback is set up, the agent will use the default fallback plan that's being set up:

* it will use the same gender voice as the original voice (if the original voice has a gender field)
* it will follow a default plan, to fall back to the next voice in the list, and if that voice is also not available, it will fall back to the next voice in the list.
* even if the original voice is back online, the agent will still continue to use the fallback to minimize the change of voice during the call.

## Set up your own TTS fallback

You can set up your own fallback plan, so that it sounds similar, and the user would not notice the change.

Open **Security & fallback settings** in the agent editor. For a conversation flow, select **Global settings** first. Under **Fallback Voice ID**, you can add multiple fallback voices, each needs to be using a different TTS provider, and it cannot be using the same provider as the original voice.

![Fallback Voice ID with Automatic fallback selected and both radio options disabled for this agent voice.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k/images/agent-settings-fallback.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k\&q=85\&s=bcd55d8684f0775b5d121e33eedba8d4)

Fallback Voice ID controls provider fallback where supported.


# Capture DTMF input from user
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/user-dtmf

Capture DTMF keypad input from callers in Retell agents — accept PINs, menu choices, and numeric entries, and configure completion timing and digit counts.

The user can provide information via DTMF (phone keypad presses) instead of voice. For example, entering a PIN is easier to press on the keypad than to say aloud in public.

DTMF input is captured by default and factored into the agent's responses. To use it, prompt the agent to ask for the information via DTMF.

## When to use it

Reach for DTMF capture whenever a caller needs to enter something more reliably or privately than by voice:

* Collecting a PIN, account number, or verification code.
* Confirming a menu choice ("Press 1 to confirm, 2 to reschedule").
* Capturing numeric input in a noisy environment where speech recognition is unreliable.

To capture voicemail or IVR responses on outbound calls instead, see [handle voicemail and IVR](/build/handle-voicemail).

## DTMF input completion options

The agent supports three methods for determining when DTMF input is complete:

* **Digit limit (`user_dtmf_options.digit_limit`)**\
  The maximum number of digits the user can enter per turn (1–50). Once this limit is reached, input is considered complete and the agent responds immediately.

* **Termination key (`user_dtmf_options.termination_key`)**\
  A single key that signals the end of input. Acceptable values are any digit (`0`–`9`), the pound/hash symbol (`#`), or the asterisk (`*`).

* **Timeout (`user_dtmf_options.timeout_ms`)**\
  The time in milliseconds to wait after the last digit before timing out (1000–15000). The timer resets with each new digit.

You can find these options under **Call settings**.

![User Keypad Input Detection enabled, with a 2.5-second timeout and Termination Key and Digit Limit switches off.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k/images/agent-settings-keypad.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k\&q=85\&s=1618495963b23d7f53563ce44d3efb69)

User Keypad Input Detection controls when the agent responds to digits.

Here's an example prompt:

```
Please enter your PIN number using the keypad. You can finish by pressing the pound key.
```

And the transcript would look like this:

![Call transcript showing the caller's DTMF keypad entry captured as digits.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/_FxJdxv7mQoPqyGs/images/user_dtmf.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_FxJdxv7mQoPqyGs\&q=85\&s=9fbafc57ee80673ede884dfbbe096301)

## FAQ

> [accordion] Which DTMF format does Retell capture?
>
> Retell captures RFC 2833 DTMF (keypad tones sent as RTP events) by default. If digits aren't being recognized, you can confirm how they were sent by [analyzing the call's PCAP file](/reliability/debug-calls-pcap#extract-and-inspect-dtmf-events) in Wireshark.

> [accordion] What happens if I set more than one completion option?
>
> Whichever condition is met first completes the input. For example, the agent stops collecting as soon as the digit limit is reached, the termination key is pressed, or the timeout elapses after the last digit.

> [accordion] Digits the caller pressed aren't showing up. What should I check?
>
> Confirm the agent prompted for keypad input, then inspect the PCAP for a DTMF payload-type mismatch between the SDP and the RTP packets. See [debug SIP calls using PCAP files](/reliability/debug-calls-pcap#extract-and-inspect-dtmf-events).


# Choose a custom provider
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/build/voice

Add custom voices to your Retell agent — search community voices or train a voice clone for a unique, brand-specific sound.

If you find the existing voice doesn't meet your needs, you can add a custom voice. There's a limit of 100 custom voices per account. If you need more, please contact us via the [Customer Support Portal](https://support.retellai.com/) or [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com).

> [!TIP]
>
> Start with [Platform Voices](/build/platform-voices) — Retell's built-in voices with automatic TTS fallback. Add a custom voice only if none of them fit.

## Add Custom Voice

Open the voice selector, go to **Custom Providers**, pick a provider (MiniMax, Cartesia, Fish Audio, Inworld, or ElevenLabs), then click **Add custom voice**. On the **Community Voices** tab, search by voice name or voice ID to add a publicly available community voice.

![Add Custom Voice dialog on the Community Voices tab for ElevenLabs, with a Voice Name search field](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/WSVXueUGaVojnhAq/images/add-custom-voice-elevenlabs-community.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=WSVXueUGaVojnhAq\&q=85\&s=b706395f76733dcdcf947301b3f78ad0)

## Add Voice Clone

The recommended way to clone a voice is from the **Platform Voices** tab: click **Add voice clone**, which creates a [platform voice](/build/platform-voices) clone (automatic TTS fallback, same as built-in platform voices). You can also train a clone through a custom provider's **Voice Clone** tab using the steps below.

**1. Open Add custom voice**

Open the voice selector, select **Custom Providers**, choose your provider, then click **Add custom voice**.

![Select Voice dialog on the Custom Providers tab showing MiniMax, Cartesia, Fish Audio, Inworld, and ElevenLabs, with the Add custom voice button](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/bGyCVCcHUoMm65YS/images/voice-select-custom-providers.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=bGyCVCcHUoMm65YS\&q=85\&s=56f68718b8091c79f8f44f5b504ed5b6)

**2. Train Your Voice Clone**

Open the **Voice Clone** tab, enter a voice name, upload your audio clip, confirm the consent checkbox, then click **Save**.

![Add Custom Voice dialog on the Voice Clone tab for ElevenLabs, with Voice Name, upload audio clip, and consent checkbox](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/WSVXueUGaVojnhAq/images/add-custom-voice-elevenlabs-clone.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=WSVXueUGaVojnhAq\&q=85\&s=5e4c46bc82aa2716a4add6401d0be0c4)

### What to say in the recordings

Cloning captures how the voice sounds, not what it says, so you don't need to read a specific script. Any natural speech works. For the best result:

* Speak in the tone, pace, and energy you want the agent to use on calls. The clone reproduces the delivery it hears.
* Use continuous, conversational speech rather than isolated words or long pauses.
* Record a single speaker with no background noise, music, or echo.
* Avoid heavily edited or compressed audio. A clean microphone recording works better than audio captured from a phone or video call.

### File limits

File limits depend on the voice provider you clone with. Inworld voice cloning accepts up to 3 files and 16 MB of audio in total, while Cartesia, MiniMax, and platform clones take a single file. ElevenLabs clones accept up to 25 files via the [Clone Voice API](/api-references/clone-voice). In the dashboard upload field, ElevenLabs accepts audio and video formats up to 10 MB per clip.

> [accordion] Import an existing voice with a share link
>
> Some custom providers (currently ElevenLabs) show an **Import Professional Voices** tab under **Add custom voice**. Paste the voice's share link from the provider, enter a voice name, then click **Save**. Only professional voice clones that are shareable by link can be imported.
>
> ![Add Custom Voice dialog on the Import Professional Voices tab, with Share Link and Voice Name fields](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/WSVXueUGaVojnhAq/images/add-custom-voice-elevenlabs-import-professional.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=WSVXueUGaVojnhAq\&q=85\&s=892570bf99bdeaa93d02cf3ea00a9dac)


# Review QA results
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/ai-qa

Review AI QA results with Retell AI Conductor. Inspect cohort trends and individual evaluations, compare findings with call transcripts, and identify fixes.

Conductor can inspect AI QA cohorts, aggregate results, and individual call evaluations. Ask it to explain a trend or examine the calls behind a low score.

## When to use it

Use Conductor to investigate a drop in resolution rate, understand why a call failed a criterion, or compare a QA finding with the actual conversation.

For example: "Which calls in this cohort failed the appointment-confirmation criterion, and what happened in them?"

## Investigate QA results

**1. Choose a cohort**

Open a cohort and Conductor, or use **Add context** (+) → **AI QA** to attach one. You can also ask Conductor to find a cohort by name.

**2. Start with the overall results**

Ask about aggregate results and trends, then ask for the individual scored calls behind them.

**3. Check an evaluation**

Ask why a call received its score and have Conductor compare the evaluation with the transcript before proposing an agent change.

Conductor can return a navigation card with **View** to open the cohort and continue the conversation there. See [Open pages from replies](/conductor/overview#open-pages-from-conductor-replies).

## Why can one call have different QA results?

A call can belong to several cohorts with different evaluation criteria. Specify the cohort when asking Conductor to explain a score.

## Change the agent or the evaluation criteria

If the transcript shows an agent problem, ask Conductor to propose a fix and [review the changes](/conductor/build-and-refine#review-and-apply-changes).

Conductor’s QA tools inspect results; they do not create cohorts or edit their criteria. If the criteria do not reflect your intended outcome, update them using [Define resolution criteria](/ai-qa/define-resolution-criteria). See [AI QA overview](/ai-qa/overview) for setup and sampling.


# Build analytics dashboards
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/analytics-dashboards

Build analytics dashboards with Retell AI Conductor. Describe the metrics you need, add chart context, and review proposed changes before applying them.

Ask Conductor to build an analytics dashboard or improve one you already use. Describe what you want to measure, then review its proposed changes before applying them.

## When to use it

Use Conductor when you know the question you want a dashboard to answer and need help choosing or configuring charts. You can also ask it to explain an existing chart or suggest improvements to a dashboard.

For example, an appointment-booking team could ask: "Help me build a call dashboard showing call volume, success rate, and average duration by week. Break it down by agent."

## Not sure where to start?

Open a new Conductor conversation on **Analytics** and choose a starter suggestion. It fills the message box so you can edit it before sending:

* **Build a dashboard** — describe what you want to measure and why.
* **Add useful charts** — choose charts that support your dashboard’s goals.
* **Improve this dashboard** — review the current dashboard and suggest improvements.

![Conductor on Analytics showing Build a dashboard, Add useful charts, and Improve this dashboard.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-analytics-suggestions.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=fdb081fa275c0a8cfa9b394b57924fe5)

Starter suggestions for building and improving analytics dashboards.

## Build or improve a dashboard

**1. Open Analytics and Conductor**

Go to **Analytics**, select the dashboard you want to work on, and open **Conductor**.

**2. Describe your goal**

Ask for a new dashboard, a dashboard name change, or charts to add, update, or remove. Include whether you want call or chat data, the metrics, the time range, and any filters or breakdowns.

For example: "Add a chart showing unsuccessful calls over the last four weeks, broken down by disconnection reason."

**3. Review the proposal**

Review the proposed dashboard and chart changes. Accept the changes you want, reject the others, then submit your review in Conductor.

![Full Analytics page with five charts, global date range, Filter and Breakdown controls, and Conductor's pending review. The proposed Call Success Rate chart change appears beside the unchanged charts.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-analytics-dashboard-proposal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=9682d02d8cb0cb8a08f7ec6906fbbe07)

A dashboard proposal with the Call Success Rate chart change.

![Analytics dashboard showing a proposed Call Success Rate chart update beside Conductor's Review changes card, with the reject and accept controls.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-analytics-review.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=1f7595d454678f710218abdbfa55bafa)

Review a proposed chart update and accept or reject it before submitting.

Click a proposed change to find the affected chart or setting. Where available, use **View original** and **View proposed** to compare versions. Use **Undo** to change a decision before submitting.

If the proposal belongs to another dashboard, click **Open this dashboard** to review it there. Finish the pending review before manually editing charts or dashboard settings.

See [Analytics dashboard](/features/analytics-dashboard) for available metrics, chart types, filters, and breakdowns.

## Change global filters and breakdowns

Ask Conductor to change **global filters and breakdowns** when you want the change to apply across the dashboard. Global filters limit which calls or chats appear in every chart; global breakdowns group the results across charts, such as by agent or agent version.

For example:

* "Filter this entire dashboard to inbound calls."
* "Break down every chart on this dashboard by agent."
* "Remove the global agent breakdown from this dashboard."

Conductor includes these changes in its dashboard proposal. Review the proposed **Filter** and **Breakdown** settings in the dashboard header, accept or reject them, then submit your review.

![Analytics header previewing Type: Inbound and an Agent breakdown with the product's native proposal outlines.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-global-filters-proposal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=30e21ce80bb983c7b63c09bc386c34f5)

A proposed inbound-call filter and agent breakdown in the dashboard header.

![Conductor Review changes showing Dashboard filters and breakdown, with accept and reject controls and an unsubmitted review.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-global-filters-review.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=95c5ac752ecc545754e1de4323dee668)

Review global filters and breakdowns together before submitting.

If you only want to change one chart, name or attach that chart and say so. Chart-level filters are combined with the global filters, so both restrictions apply. See [Filters and breakdowns](/features/analytics-dashboard#filters-and-breakdowns) for the available fields.

Conductor can also return a [navigation link](/conductor/overview#open-pages-from-conductor-replies) to an analytics dashboard with filters and breakdowns included. Click **View** to open that selection and keep the conversation alongside it.

## Give Conductor chart context

With Conductor open on **Analytics**, click a chart to attach it as context, then ask your question. For example: "Explain what this chart measures and suggest a breakdown to help compare agents."

You can also use **Add context** (+): choose **Charts** for charts on the current dashboard, or **Analytics** to attach a dashboard. To attach several items, use **Multi-select**, select them, and click **Save**. Check the context chips before sending your message.

See [Give Conductor context](/conductor/overview#give-conductor-context) for other resources you can attach.

## View charts in chat

Conductor can show a chart directly in its reply so you can inspect the result without first adding it to a dashboard. Ask for a metric and time range, such as "Show call counts over the last three months."

The chart shows a snapshot of the results returned with that reply, rather than refreshing as dashboard data changes. You can keep discussing it in chat or save it to a dashboard.

![Conductor conversation displaying a Call Counts bar chart for the last three months, with the Add to this dashboard button below the chart.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-analytics-chat-chart.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=60a5bfcea369ac8b6408f913bd4b4969)

A Call Counts chart in a Conductor reply, with Add to this dashboard below the chart.

When Conductor returns a chart in its reply, click **Add to this dashboard** to save it to the dashboard currently open in Analytics. From another page, click **Use in Analytics** first.

The chart and dashboard must use the same data source: call charts belong on call dashboards, and chat charts on chat dashboards. Adding a chart requires analytics edit access. Finish any pending Conductor review before adding it.


# Build and refine agents
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/build-and-refine

Build and refine agents with Retell AI Conductor. Describe an edit, compare the current and proposed settings, and accept changes before testing your agent.

Ask Conductor to change your agent’s prompts, settings, or conversation flow in plain language. It proposes edits for you to review before applying them.

Use it for a targeted change, such as shortening an appointment-booking greeting, or to improve an agent based on [unsuccessful calls or chats](/conductor/test-and-improve).

## Create or inspect an agent

To generate a first version from your requirements, follow [Create an agent with Conductor](/conductor/create-agent). For an existing agent, ask Conductor to explain its configuration, compare versions, or compare it with another agent attached through [Add context](/conductor/overview#give-conductor-context).

For example: "Compare these two appointment-booking agents and explain how they handle unavailable slots."

## Send your first message

**1. Open Conductor**

Click **Conductor** in the agent builder toolbar.

**2. Describe the change**

Type your request in the message box. [Attach a node, call, chat, or other resource](/conductor/overview#give-conductor-context) when the request concerns a specific item.

**3. Send your request**

Press **Enter** or click the send button.

Conductor explains what it is doing, then replies or proposes changes to your agent.

![An unsent request to clarify the template patient-screening greeting, with the send button.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-first-message.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=e0cd5b6cddb258fa87be6b8af5f28938)

Describe the change you want before sending your message.

## Not sure where to start?

When you open a new conversation, Conductor shows **starter suggestions**. Click one to fill the message box, edit the request if needed, then send it:

* **Review this agent** — review the current agent configuration.
* **Improve using failures** — find improvements from unsuccessful interactions.
* **Suggest edge case tests** — identify scenarios to test.

![Conductor starter suggestions for the Patient Screening template agent: Review this agent, Improve using failures, and Suggest edge case tests.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-suggestions.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=d298b2f320d47bd6af1181e3a969ffb2)

Starter suggestions in a new conversation with Patient Screening (from template).

## Examples of what to ask

> [accordion] Editing how your agent talks
>
> * "Make the greeting shorter and friendlier."
> * "Ask for the caller's full name before anything else."
> * "If the caller sounds upset, apologize and offer to transfer to a human."

> [accordion] Adding or changing steps
>
> * "Add a step that collects the caller's email and confirms the spelling."
> * "After booking, ask if they'd like a text reminder."
> * "Add a path for callers who only want store hours."

> [accordion] Fixing problems
>
> * "Callers say the agent talks over them — can you fix that?"
> * "The agent keeps repeating the menu. Help me stop that."

## Configure functions and tools

Ask Conductor to add or update the functions your agent uses, including their configuration and the instructions for when to call them. For a custom function, provide the endpoint details, expected inputs, and the response the agent should handle.

For example: "Add a check_availability function that takes an appointment date. Ask for the date before calling it, and offer another date if no slots are available."

For conversation-flow agents, ask Conductor to connect the function to a [Function node](/build/conversation-flow/function-node) and define the transitions after it returns. For prompt agents, describe when to call the function and how to use its result in the response.

Review proposed function changes along with the agent’s other edits before submitting. If a function behaves unexpectedly, [attach a call or chat](/conductor/call-and-chat-history) and ask Conductor to inspect its arguments, result, and surrounding conversation.

See [Function calling](/build/add-function-calling) for supported functions and [Testing with Conductor](/test/testing-with-conductor) for mocking function responses in simulations.

## Tips for great results

* **Be specific.** "Ask for the appointment date and time" works better than "collect info."
* **One goal at a time.** Smaller requests are easier to review and get right.
* **Give context.** Name the specific step, call, or chat, or better yet, [attach it](/conductor/overview#give-conductor-context).
* **Iterate.** If a suggestion isn't quite right, tell Conductor what to adjust and it will revise.

## Stopping a response

If Conductor is working and you want to stop it, click the **Stop** button in the message box. You can then send a new message.

## Review and apply changes

Conductor lists its proposed agent edits in **Review changes** and previews them on the affected settings or nodes. Review each change before applying it.

![Conductor response proposing a shorter greeting for the template agent, with Review changes controls below the response.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k/images/conductor/conductor-template-review.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k\&q=85\&s=d0e659d3b254667ec2379908c7e39e8a)

A greeting proposal in Patient Screening (from template), with the changed node in view.

### Compare the current and proposed values

Select a change in the review panel to find the affected setting or node. The inline preview shows the proposed edit in context. Where available, use **View original** and **View proposed** to switch between versions. Text diffs mark removed content with strikethrough and added content in green.

Click the change description, such as **Node updated**, to open its **JSON diff** and inspect the exact values.

![JSON diff for the template agent's Greetings node, showing the original greeting and the shorter proposed greeting above the Node updated control.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-template-review-diff.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=d00c48c76d3173cca37374dc4664a1f9)

Open Node updated to inspect the greeting's JSON diff.

### Choose what to apply

Use **Accept change** (✓) or **Reject change** (×) for each edit. For proposals with several edits, the bulk accept and reject controls let you decide on all remaining changes together. Use **Undo** to revise a decision before submitting.

Click **Submit** to apply the accepted changes and send your review back to Conductor. To request a revision, write feedback in **Anything I should do differently?** and submit. Any changes you have not accepted are rejected when you submit.

Finish the review before sending your next prompt. If a change fails to apply, check Conductor's response before continuing. After applying agent changes, [test the updated behavior](/conductor/test-and-improve).

### Review on the correct agent

If a proposal belongs to another agent or version, click **Open this agent** in the proposal before reviewing it. If the agent is already open on another tab within the builder, click **Switch to Agent tab**.


# Review calls and chats
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/call-and-chat-history

Investigate calls and chats with Retell AI Conductor. Filter conversations, inspect transcripts and tool calls, and compare failures to improve your agent.

Ask Conductor to find and investigate calls or chats, compare their outcomes, and suggest agent improvements. You can describe the conversations you want or select them directly from history.

## When to use it

Use Conductor when a conversation failed, a customer did not get an answer, or you want to understand a pattern across several sessions.

For example: "Review chats where the customer’s question went unanswered and suggest improvements."

## Find and review conversations

**1. Choose the conversations**

Open **Call History** or **Chat History**, click **Select**, and check the rows. Open Conductor to see the selected conversations as context chips. You can also use **Add context** (+), provide a session ID, or describe a set of conversations.

![Call History with two checked rows and a 2 selected count.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-history-multi-select.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=3916891c6d4525de82e288a5c4f2cf21)

Select the history rows you want Conductor to investigate.

**2. Describe the problem**

Ask what went wrong or what the selected conversations have in common. Include the outcome you expected, such as confirming a booking or answering a delivery question.

**3. Inspect the evidence**

Ask Conductor to examine transcripts, outcomes, analysis, tool calls, or node transitions. Use inline call or chat links in the reply to open individual session details.

![Conductor message box with two call context chips above the draft question What do these calls have in common?](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-history-context.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=d08da59423751b2ed0c2ef16ec376f29)

Two selected calls appear as context for a question about shared patterns.

For the selection steps, see [Select calls and chats from history](/conductor/overview#select-calls-and-chats-from-history).

## Open filtered results

Ask, "Show unsuccessful calls from last week," or "Find unsuccessful chats for this agent." Conductor can return a navigation card that opens **Call History** or **Chat History** with the requested filters. Check the filters after opening the results.

See [Call and chat history](/features/session-history) for the available filters and session details.

## Turn findings into improvements

Ask Conductor to propose a targeted fix, then [review the agent changes](/conductor/build-and-refine#review-and-apply-changes). For example: "Update the agent to explain the next step when the booking function returns no available slots."

Use [Testing](/conductor/test-and-improve) to check the change before deploying it. If the issue comes from a QA evaluation, [inspect the QA result](/conductor/ai-qa) alongside the transcript.


# Review contacts
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/contacts

Inspect contacts with Retell AI Conductor. Find records, review contact fields, and follow associated phone calls and SMS chats across your agents.

Conductor can find contacts, inspect their fields, and review their associated phone calls and SMS chats. Use it to understand a contact’s history across agents.

## When to use it

Use Conductor before following up with a contact or when investigating repeated unsuccessful conversations.

For example: "Review this contact’s recent conversations and summarize what still needs a follow-up."

## Review a contact

**1. Find the contact**

Use **Add context** (+) → **Contacts**, or ask Conductor to find a contact by name. If you have a contact ID or phone number, include it in the request.

**2. Ask about fields or history**

Ask about the contact’s fields, recent conversations, outcomes, or last interaction. You can also ask for contacts matching a custom field or last-contacted date.

**3. Inspect a conversation**

Ask Conductor to examine a specific call or chat from the contact’s history. Use the reply’s inline links to open the session details.

For more investigation options, see [Call and chat history](/conductor/call-and-chat-history).

## Which conversations belong to a contact?

Contacts are associated with phone calls and SMS chats by phone number, so their history can span multiple agents. Web calls and web chats have no phone number and do not belong to a contact.

## Can Conductor update contacts?

Conductor’s contact tools are read-only. Add contacts, edit fields, and manage CRM synchronization from the [Contacts page](/features/contacts).

A contact’s **Do not call** flag is information you can filter or sync; it does not itself block calls. Check the flag when planning outreach.


# Inspect knowledge bases
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/knowledge-base

Inspect knowledge bases with Retell AI Conductor. Find sources, check indexing status and errors, and see which knowledge bases your agents and nodes use.

Conductor can inspect your knowledge bases, their source metadata, and indexing status. Attach a knowledge base or name it in your request to find its sources and understand how it is configured.

## When to use it

Use Conductor to find an existing knowledge base, check why indexing has not finished, or identify the knowledge bases attached to an agent or node.

For example: "Which knowledge bases does my appointment-booking agent use, and have they finished indexing?"

## Inspect a knowledge base

**1. Choose the knowledge base**

Open Conductor and use **Add context** (+) → **Knowledge Base**. Select an item, or use **Multi-select** to attach several. You can also ask Conductor to find a knowledge base by name.

**2. Ask about its setup**

Ask for the source inventory, indexing status, reported errors, or refresh settings. For example: "List this knowledge base’s sources and explain any indexing errors."

**3. Check agent associations**

Attach the relevant agent or node and ask which knowledge bases it uses. To compare agents, attach both and ask how their knowledge-base configuration differs.

See [Give Conductor context](/conductor/overview#give-conductor-context) for selecting resources across your workspace.

## What can Conductor inspect?

Conductor can list knowledge bases and read their names, source metadata, indexing status, error messages, and refresh configuration. Source metadata includes information such as URLs, filenames, and titles.

A source count may be incomplete while indexing is in progress or has failed. Ask Conductor to check the status before interpreting a missing source as an empty knowledge base.

## Can Conductor read or change the source content?

Conductor’s knowledge-base tools cannot search or read indexed source contents, create a knowledge base, or add, replace, or delete its sources. Manage those changes on the [Knowledge Base page](/build/knowledge-base).

To discuss the contents of a specific document, [attach the file](/conductor/overview#attach-files) to your message. Attaching a knowledge base provides its configuration and source metadata.


# Retell AI Conductor overview
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/overview

Use Retell AI Conductor to build agents, improve analytics dashboards, investigate conversations, and open resources while keeping your work in context.

Conductor is Retell’s AI assistant for building agents, investigating conversations, and improving analytics dashboards. Ask for what you need in plain language, attach relevant context, and review proposed changes before applying them.

Use Conductor to build and test agents, inspect knowledge bases, investigate calls and chats, and analyze dashboards, QA results, or contacts. The [functionality guides](#where-to-go-next) cover each workflow.

![Conductor panel with suggested tasks and its message box.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/pODYYtXmCDaCiu-r/images/conductor/conductor-panel.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=pODYYtXmCDaCiu-r\&q=85\&s=8103b390c8301c23ad203e1a96f4731d)

Conductor open beside Patient Screening (from template).

## How to open Conductor

* **From an agent:** click **Conductor** in the agent builder toolbar.
* **From Analytics and other dashboard pages:** click **Ask Conductor** to open the panel alongside the page.
* **From Home:** start typing in the Conductor message box; no agent needs to be open.

Drag the panel’s left edge to adjust its width. You can also drag the floating **Ask Conductor** button along the bottom of the page to move it out of the way. Conductor stays available alongside open dialogs and detail panels.

Close the panel when you need more room; your conversation stays in history.

Starter suggestions change with the page you have open. Click a suggestion to fill the message box, edit it if needed, then send it.

## Work across dashboard pages

Conductor is available on every dashboard page and uses the current page as context. You can [attach other resources](#give-conductor-context) to compare agents or investigate conversations across your workspace.

Conductor’s replies can include navigation cards with a **View** button. Click **View** to open the resource and continue the same conversation there. For example, ask "Show unsuccessful calls from last week" to get a **Call History** link with those filters applied.

![A request to show unsuccessful calls from last week, followed by Conductor’s Call History navigation card filtered to September 7–13, 2026, with a View button.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-navigation-card.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=3ff55209f060c448e81b286f5c373861)

Click View to open the resource and continue your Conductor conversation there.

Cards can open agents and specific versions, filtered call or chat history, analytics dashboards with filters and breakdowns, or AI QA cohorts. Check the destination’s filters to confirm the selection.

Replies can also include **inline links** to individual calls, chats, and conversation-flow nodes. Click a call or chat link to open its details, or a node link to focus it in the agent builder, while keeping the conversation open.

## Give Conductor context

Attach resources or files when your request concerns a specific item. They appear as **context chips** above the message box. For example, attach two appointment-booking agents and ask how they handle rescheduling differently.

### How to attach context

**1. Open the resource selector**

Click **Add context** (+) in the Conductor message box.

**2. Choose resources**

Choose a category, such as **Agents** or **Call History**, then click an item to attach it.

To attach several items from a category, click **Multi-select**, check the items, and click **Save**. Repeat for other categories as needed.

**3. Review and send**

Check the context chips above the message box, type your request, and send it.

![Conductor Add context selector beside the message box, with Nodes selected, Greetings and Wrong User checked, and the Save button.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-attach-menu.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=048c3e135f432ae4392ebe3854cde627)

Choose several resources with Multi-select, then click Save.

Larger selections of the same resource type appear as a single chip with a count. Your sent messages keep their attachment chips, so you can see which context accompanied each request.

### What can you attach?

The available categories depend on your permissions and the page you have open.

| Category | What it provides | Availability |
| - | - | - |
| Agents | Agents to reference or compare. | Any page |
| Knowledge Base | [Source metadata and indexing status](/conductor/knowledge-base). | Any page |
| Call History / Chat History | Conversations to investigate. | Any page |
| Analytics | An [analytics dashboard](/conductor/analytics-dashboards) to discuss. | Any page |
| AI QA | A [cohort’s evaluation results](/conductor/ai-qa). | Any page |
| Contacts | A [contact and its conversation history](/conductor/contacts). | Any page |
| Nodes | Conversation-flow nodes. | Conversation-flow agent |
| Test Cases / Testing History | Saved test cases and test runs. | Agent page, except custom LLM agents |
| Charts | Individual charts. | Analytics dashboard |

With Conductor open in a conversation-flow agent, you can also click a node on the canvas to attach it.

For a targeted edit, attach the "Collect email" node and ask, "Make this step confirm the spelling back to the caller." To [investigate a failed test](/conductor/test-and-improve), attach its test case or run and ask what needs to change.

### Select text anywhere in the UI

Highlight text anywhere in the dashboard to give Conductor context about what you’re reading. For example, highlight **Voice & Language** in an agent’s settings and ask, "Explain how this setting affects my agent."

The selection appears as a character-count chip above the message box. Check that the chip appears before sending. If it says **Selection too large**, select a smaller passage.

![Conductor message box with 5 Nodes and 16 characters context chips above a question about the selected setting.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k/images/conductor/conductor-selected-context.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k\&q=85\&s=6d5066a40260b45363ff9f8b4d7cf29d)

Selecting Voice & Language adds a 16 characters chip to Conductor.

### Select calls and chats from history

On **Call History** or **Chat History**, click **Select**, check the conversations, and open Conductor. The selected rows appear as context chips. Ask, for example, "What do these conversations have in common?"

![Call History in selection mode with two checked web-call rows and a 2 selected count.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-history-multi-select.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=3916891c6d4525de82e288a5c4f2cf21)

Two calls selected from the Patient Screening template agent’s history.

See [Review calls and chats](/conductor/call-and-chat-history#find-and-review-conversations) for the full workflow.

### Attach files

Click the **paperclip** in the message box to upload files, or **drag and drop files** directly into the message box. You can also paste an image from your clipboard.

**Supported file types:** images (JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), documents (PDF, DOCX), text-based files (TXT, CSV, HTML, HTM, MD, RTF, JSON), and audio (WAV, MP3).

**Limits:** up to 10 files per message, each 50 MB or smaller (as of September 2026). Conductor identifies files it cannot attach because of their type, size, or the file-count limit.

## Review proposed changes

Conductor previews proposed agent and dashboard edits for your review. Compare the current and proposed values, accept or reject each change, then submit. See [agent change review](/conductor/build-and-refine#review-and-apply-changes) or [dashboard proposals](/conductor/analytics-dashboards#build-or-improve-a-dashboard) for the steps.

If a proposal belongs to another page, click **Open this agent** or **Open this dashboard** to review it there.

## Follow a guided walkthrough

Ask Conductor how to do or find something in the dashboard, such as "Show me where to change this agent’s voice." Conductor can start an interactive walkthrough that highlights the steps on the page. Follow the highlighted instructions to complete the task.

Depending on your question, Conductor may answer directly or ask for more detail before starting a walkthrough. If a walkthrough is unavailable or cannot start, it offers another way to help.

## Manage your conversations

Your conversation history is shared across dashboard pages, so you can reopen a chat and continue where you left off.

### Start a new conversation

Click **New chat** at the top of the panel when you switch tasks. The previous conversation stays in history.

![Conductor header with new chat, history, and close controls.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/3a75AO214qaM767u/images/conductor/conductor-header-actions.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3a75AO214qaM767u\&q=85\&s=e1db27ea0e735234220fbe3fb79a507b)

Start a new chat, reopen history, or close the panel from its header.

### Open your chat history

Click **History** to reopen a conversation. **Current Page** marks chats last used on the page you have open.

On Home, click **Search chats** in **Conductor History** to open [global search](/get-started/global-search) with **Conductor** selected. Search by title or message text, then select a result to reopen it. You can also open global search from **Search & create** in the sidebar or press **⌘K** / **Ctrl+K**, then choose **Conductor**.

Conductor restores your most recent chat when you reopen the panel. If its last message was sent elsewhere, **Last used on** links back to that page with the conversation open.

### Rename or delete a conversation

Open the conversation title menu and choose **Rename chat** or **Delete chat**. Enter a new title and press **Enter**, or confirm deletion when prompted. You can also hover over a history entry to open its rename/delete menu. Deletion cannot be undone.

### Give feedback

Click **Helpful** (👍) or **Not helpful** (👎) on a reply. After **Not helpful**, describe what you expected and click **Submit**, or choose **Skip** to leave only the rating. Click a selected thumb again to clear it, or choose the other thumb to change it.

> [accordion] Copy a conversation ID or link
>
> Open the conversation title menu and click **Copy chat ID** to identify it for support.
>
> When you open a resource through a reply’s navigation link, the destination URL includes the conversation. Copy that URL to revisit the same resource and chat, or share it with a teammate who has workspace access.

> [accordion] What happens to long conversations?
>
> Conductor automatically condenses earlier context in long conversations. You may briefly see **Condensed conversation context** in its activity. Continue in the same chat after condensation, or start a **New chat** for a different task.

## Pricing

Conductor includes a daily free message allowance. Workspace admins can enable pay-as-you-go and set a monthly spending limit. See [Pricing](/conductor/usage-and-billing) for allowances, reset times, and billing details.

# Test and improve agents
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/test-and-improve

Use Retell AI Conductor to investigate calls and chats, run simulation tests, and review results. Find issues and refine agent responses before deployment.

Use Conductor to investigate unsuccessful calls and chats, then test improvements with simulations against your agent. Test a proposed fix or an edge case, such as a wrong-number call, before using the updated agent with customers.

## Start from real conversations

Use [Call and chat history](/conductor/call-and-chat-history) to investigate unsuccessful sessions before deciding what to test. Turn the problem into a repeatable scenario, then check whether the proposed agent change resolves it.

## Test and refine edge cases

Edge cases are the unusual situations that trip agents up — an angry caller, a wrong number, someone who changes their mind. Ask Conductor to help you handle them:

* "What edge cases should I worry about for this agent?"
* "Make sure the agent handles a caller who refuses to give their name."

## Run simulations

Conductor can run **simulation tests** that play out a scenario against your agent and show how it responds. This lets you check changes without making real phone calls. See [Testing with Conductor](/test/testing-with-conductor) for creating test cases from calls, configuring mocks, and running a saved suite.

* "Run a simulation where the caller wants to reschedule an appointment."
* Attach a saved test case and say "Run this and tell me if it passes."

When a simulation finishes, Conductor shows the result so you can see how your agent behaved and decide what to refine next.

![Conductor Simulation Tests result showing Wrong number - caller not the patient passed, with one test completed and a reply explaining that the template agent apologized and ended the call.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F/images/conductor/conductor-simulation.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hUHAB8rIIpPsqz8F\&q=85\&s=1f9310b4a6cc2c6a8a37fbfafce576fa)

A wrong-number simulation passes for Patient Screening (from template).

## Manage test cases and runs

Ask Conductor to list or inspect saved test cases, update their scenarios or success criteria, or delete cases you no longer need. You can also ask it to run a batch, report the pass rate, and inspect individual run transcripts.

Use **Add context** (+) → **Test Cases** or **Testing History** on the agent page to attach the case or run you mean. See [Testing with Conductor](/test/testing-with-conductor) for personas, dynamic variables, function mocks, and batch workflows.

## A good loop to follow

**1. Make a change**

Ask Conductor to build or adjust something, then [accept the proposal](/conductor/build-and-refine#review-and-apply-changes).

**2. Test it**

Run a simulation or review a relevant call or chat to see how the change behaves.

**3. Refine**

Tell Conductor what to improve, and repeat until you're happy.

> [!NOTE]
>
> See the [testing guides](/test/test-overview) for the LLM Playground, simulation testing, and audio testing.


# Pricing
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/conductor/usage-and-billing

See how Conductor charges credits per message by model tier, how daily free credits reset, and how admins turn on pay-as-you-go with a monthly limit.

Each message you send to Conductor uses credits. Every user gets free credits each day, and a workspace admin can turn on **pay-as-you-go** to keep Conductor running after they run out.

## Model tiers

Each message costs a fixed number of credits based on its model tier. Conversation length and task complexity don't change the cost.

| Tier | Best for | Credits per message |
| - | - | - |
| **Fast** | Quick answers and FAQs | 0.5 |
| **Default** | Small edits and updates | 1 |
| **Advanced** | Big changes and new builds | 3 |

## Daily free credits

* Each user gets **30 free credits per day**.
* Each workspace shares a cap of **200 free credits per day** across all users.
* Free credits reset at **midnight PT** and don't roll over.

Once either cap is reached, more usage is paid. If pay-as-you-go is off, Conductor pauses until free credits reset.

## Pay-as-you-go

With pay-as-you-go on, usage past the free credits is billed to the workspace at **\$0.20 per credit**. Only workspace admins can turn it on, from the Conductor panel or [**Settings → Limits**](https://dashboard.retellai.com/settings/limits).

Admins choose a monthly limit:

* **Unlimited**: no cap on paid usage.
* **Fixed**: a monthly cap in USD. Once the workspace reaches it, Conductor pauses until an admin raises the limit or free credits reset.


# A/B Testing
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/ab-testing

Run Retell A/B tests by splitting inbound and outbound voice and chat traffic between agents to compare prompts, voices, and flows in production.

A/B testing lets you compare multiple agents or scripts by sending a percentage of traffic to each. You define a traffic split (for example, 80% to one agent and 20% to another) so you can test different prompts, voices, or flows without changing your main agent.

## Where A/B testing is available

A/B testing is supported for:

* **Inbound calls** — Calls received on a phone number
* **Outbound calls** — Calls made from a phone number
* **Inbound chats** — Incoming chat conversations
* **Outbound chats** — Chat sessions you initiate

## How it works

* **Multiple agents**: Bind or assign two or more agents to the same number or chat configuration.
* **Traffic split**: Set the percentage of traffic each agent receives (e.g., 80% / 20%). Traffic is distributed according to this split.
* **Use cases**: Test different scripts on marketing or support calls, try prompt or voice changes, or compare conversation flows in chat.

## Where to configure

**Phone numbers (calls):** On the phone number configuration page, the A/B Testing toggle appears next to the Call Agent field. Turn it on to bind multiple agents and set a traffic split. The screenshot below shows the control with A/B testing disabled.

![Phone number configuration showing Call Agent dropdown and A/B Testing toggle in the off position](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb/images/deploy/phone-call/ab-testing-disabled.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb\&q=85\&s=25946aa3ee6fa45200c2bde81cefc3cf)

A/B Testing control on the phone number configuration page (disabled)

After you turn the toggle on, you can add one or more agents and set the traffic percentage for each (for example, one agent at 100% or a split such as 80% / 20%).

![Call Agent section with A/B Testing on, showing one agent variant with 100% traffic and edit option](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb/images/deploy/phone-call/ab-testing-enabled.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb\&q=85\&s=af20d15125759a970ce2cd9a2a6d9fcb)

A/B Testing enabled: agent variants and traffic split

Click **Edit** to open the A/B Testing modal. There you choose which agents to use and set a weight (percentage) for each. You can add multiple agents and remove or adjust them; the weights must total 100%. Click **Deploy** to save.

![A/B Testing modal with Agent and Weight columns, two agents at 50% each, Add button and Deploy/Cancel actions](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb/images/deploy/phone-call/ab-testing-modal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb\&q=85\&s=5ce22efaa611769f780edd3e86f03303)

A/B Testing modal: configure agents and percentage weights

After you click **Deploy**, the configuration is active. The Call Agent section shows each agent and its traffic percentage (for example, a 50/50 split). You can click **Edit** anytime to change the agents or weights.

![Call Agent section with A/B Testing on, showing Agent A and Agent B each at 50% with Edit option](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb/images/deploy/phone-call/ab-testing-deployed.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=OUoENzk-DjeUQ4lb\&q=85\&s=63c0babd4cedf06ac8d12c075011d290)

A/B Testing after deploy: active traffic split

| Context | Configure in |
| - | - |
| **Inbound calls** | Number configuration: bind multiple agents to the number and set the traffic split. See [Receive calls](/deploy/inbound-call). |
| **Outbound calls** | Number configuration: bind multiple agents for outbound and set the traffic split. See [Outbound calls](/deploy/outbound-call). |
| **Chat (inbound & outbound)** | Chat agent or widget configuration where you assign the chat agent; enable A/B testing and set the traffic split. See [Create Chat Completion](/deploy/create-chat-completion) and [Chat widget](/deploy/chat-widget). |

## View analytics by agent version

After you deploy an A/B test, you can compare performance by specific agent versions in the Analytics dashboard.

1. Open **Analytics** in the Retell dashboard.
2. Set a date range that covers your experiment period.
3. In the filter bar, click **Agent** (or click **Filter** and add **Agent**).
4. In the left panel, select the agent(s) used in your A/B test.
5. In the right panel, select the specific version(s) you want to analyze (for example, `Version 3` vs `Version 4` of the same agent).
6. Click **Save** to apply the filter.

All charts on the page will update to the selected agent-version scope, so you can compare metrics (such as call success rate, duration, and latency) for each variant.

For more details on Analytics, see [Get analytics insight](/features/analytics-dashboard).

## A/B testing vs dynamic agent selection

> [tab] A/B testing
>
> Use when you want a **random percentage-based split**. Traffic is distributed according to the percentages you set, with no per-call or per-chat logic.

> [tab] Dynamic selection (webhook / API)
>
> Use when you want to **choose the agent per call or per chat** based on caller, context, or other data. For inbound calls, use the [Inbound Call Webhook](/features/inbound-call-webhook). For outbound calls or chats, pass the agent (or other overrides) in the API when you create the call or chat.


# Amazon Connect
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/amazon-connect

Amazon Connect is a cloud-based contact center service from AWS that lets you set up and manage customer support call centers quickly.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Customers with an enterprise or paid support plan can contact us via the [Customer Support Portal](https://support.retellai.com/) or [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com) for step-by-step guidance to connect with your Amazon Connect infrastructure.

Retell supports multiple integration patterns with Amazon Connect. Because every deployment differs, contact Retell support via the [Customer Support Portal](https://support.retellai.com/) or [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com) to discuss your Amazon Connect infrastructure and find the right integration approach.

Once connected, your number works for [inbound](/deploy/inbound-call) and [outbound](/deploy/outbound-call) calls like any Retell number. For how Retell connects to a third-party provider over SIP, see [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony).


# Avaya
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/avaya

A step-by-step guide to integrate Avaya Aura with Retell's SIP endpoints using Avaya SBCE as the border element to send and receive phone calls.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Customers with an enterprise or paid support plan can contact us via the [Customer Support Portal](https://support.retellai.com/) or [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com) for step-by-step guidance to connect with your Avaya infrastructure.

## Overview

This guide covers connecting **Avaya Aura** to Retell using **Avaya Session Border Controller for Enterprise (SBCE)** as the SIP border element between Retell and the Avaya core (Session Manager and Communication Manager).

**Architecture:**

```
Retell ↔ Avaya SBCE (B1 external) | (A1 internal) ↔ Session Manager ↔ Communication Manager
```

The SBCE handles topology hiding, codec interworking, and security policy between the external Retell SIP trunk and your internal Aura infrastructure. All configuration flows through **System Manager** (the central management UI for Aura).

For the general model of how Retell connects to a third-party provider over SIP, see [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony).

**Retell SIP details:**

* SIP server URI: `sip.retellai.com`
* IP ranges: `18.98.16.120/30` (all regions, signaling only), `143.223.88.0/21` (certain US traffic), `161.115.160.0/19` (certain US traffic)
* Recommended transport: TCP (also supports UDP and TLS/SRTP)
* Supported audio codecs: PCMU (G.711 µ-law), PCMA (G.711 A-law), G.722

**Official Avaya documentation references:**

* [Administering Avaya SBCE](https://documentation.avaya.com/bundle/AdministeringAvayaSBCERelease8/)
* [Administering Avaya Aura Session Manager](https://documentation.avaya.com/bundle/AdministeringSMRelease10/)
* [Administering Avaya Aura Communication Manager](https://documentation.avaya.com/bundle/AdministeringAuraCommunicationManager/)

***

**1. Firewall considerations**

The SBCE has two network interfaces:

* **A-side (external / untrusted)** — faces the internet / Retell.
* **B-side (internal / trusted)** — faces Session Manager and Communication Manager.

Apply the following rules on your perimeter firewall and on the SBCE's built-in packet filter.

**Allow inbound to SBCE A-side from Retell IP ranges:**

| CIDR Block | Coverage |
| - | - |
| `18.98.16.120/30` | All regions, signaling only |
| `143.223.88.0/21` | Certain US traffic |
| `161.115.160.0/19` | Certain US traffic |

**Ports to open on the SBCE A-side (from/to Retell):**

| Protocol | Port | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| TCP / UDP | 5060 | SIP signaling |
| TCP | 5061 | SIP over TLS (if using TLS transport) |
| UDP | 1024–65535 | RTP / SRTP media (configurable on SBCE) |

**Ports to open on the SBCE B-side (toward Session Manager):**

| Protocol | Port | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| TCP / UDP | 5060 | SIP signaling to Session Manager |
| TCP | 5061 | SIP/TLS to Session Manager (if TLS internally) |
| UDP | 1024–65535 | RTP media toward Communication Manager |

> [!NOTE]
>
> The SBCE's media port range is configurable under **SBCE** > **Global Profiles** > **Media Interface**. Match your firewall rules to whatever range you configure there.

**2. Enable SIP trunking on the Avaya system**

Before creating the trunk, verify SIP trunking is enabled across the Aura stack.

**On Communication Manager (via System Manager):**

1. Log in to **Avaya System Manager** (`https://<smgr-ip>/SMGR`).
2. Navigate to **Elements** > **Communication Manager** > select your CM instance > **System Parameters** > **Customer Options**.
3. Confirm **SIP Trunking** is set to **y** (enabled). If not, contact your Avaya partner to activate the license.
4. Confirm **Maximum Administered SIP Trunks** is set high enough to accommodate your expected [concurrent calls](/deploy/concurrency).

**On Session Manager:**

1. In System Manager, go to **Elements** > **Session Manager** > **System Status** > **Security Module Status**.
2. Verify the Session Manager instance shows **Registered** and the SIP signaling service is active.

**3. Configure the SBCE**

All SBCE configuration is done through the **Avaya SBCE EMS (Element Management System)** web UI (`https://<sbce-ip>/`). Refer to [Administering Avaya SBCE](https://documentation.avaya.com/bundle/AdministeringAvayaSBCERelease8/) for full field-level reference.

**1. Create Server Interworking Profiles**

Server Interworking Profiles define how the SBCE adapts SIP behavior for each side of the trunk. You need one for the internal Avaya side and one for the external Retell (service provider) side.

*Avaya-side profile:*

1. Go to **Configuration Profiles** > **Server Interworking** > **Add**.
2. Name it `Avaya`.
3. Configure:
   * **SIPS Required**: unchecked (not required for this trunk type)
   * **Hold Support**: `None`
   * **Record Route**: `Both Sides`
   * **Include Endpoint IP for Context Lookup**: checked
   * **Extensions**: `Avaya`
   * **Has Remote SBC**: checked
   * **DTMF Support**: `None`
4. Click **Finish**.

*Retell (service provider) side profile:*

1. Click **Add** again and name it `Service-Provider`.
2. Configure:
   * **SIPS Required**: unchecked
   * **Delayed SDP Handling**: checked
   * **Record Route**: `Both Sides`
   * **Include Endpoint IP for Context Lookup**: checked
   * **Extensions**: `Avaya`
   * **DTMF Support**: `None`
     \[!NOTE] If your provider requires RFC 2833 DTMF relay or inband DTMF, change this to `RFC 2833` or `Inband` respectively. Check your provider's application note on [Avaya DevConnect](https://devconnect.avaya.com) for the correct value.
3. Click **Finish**.

***

**2. Add SIP Servers**

SIP Servers represent the endpoints that the SBCE sends traffic to and receives traffic from.

*Retell (service provider) server:*

1. Go to **Configuration Profiles** > **Server Configuration** > **Add**.
2. Name it `Service-Provider`.
3. Configure:
   * **Server Type**: `Trunk Server`
   * **IP Address / FQDN**: `sip.retellai.com`
   * **Port**: `5060` (use `5061` if TLS)
   * **Transport**: `TCP` (recommended), `UDP`, or `TLS` — match what you configured on the Signaling Interface and what your firewall permits. TCP is preferred for reliability; use TLS if end-to-end encryption is required (see TLS step).
4. Click **Next**. Leave authentication blank (IP-based trunk, no credentials required).
5. On the **Heartbeat** tab:
   * Enable **SIP OPTIONS** ping, interval `30` seconds.
   * **From URI**: `sip@<sbce-b1-public-ip>` (your external interface's public IP).
   * **To URI**: `sip@sip.retellai.com`
6. Click **Next**. Leave **Registration** and **Ping** defaults.
7. Ensure **Enable Grooming** is unchecked (not applicable for non-TLS trunks; leave unchecked for TCP/UDP).
8. Set **Interworking Profile** to `Service-Provider`.
9. Click **Finish**.

*Avaya Session Manager server:*

1. Click **Add** and name it `Avaya`.
2. Configure:
   * **Server Type**: `Call Server`
