# Purchase phone number
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/purchase-number

Purchase Retell-managed US or Canada phone numbers directly in the dashboard — no telephony provider account required, ready for inbound and outbound calling.

Purchase a phone number from Retell directly in the dashboard or through the API. Retell manages these numbers, so you don't have to set up any telephony infrastructure. Numbers are provisioned through **Twilio**, **Telnyx** or **Bandwidth**; you choose the provider when you buy the number.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Currently we only support purchase of US and Canada numbers and support making calls to [15 countries](/deploy/international-call). If you are looking to use numbers from other countries, or to make calls to more countries, or to use your own telephony provider, check out [Custom Telephony guide](/deploy/custom-telephony).

> [!NOTE]
>
> You must [add a payment method](/accounts/add-payment) to your workspace before you can purchase a phone number.

### From the dashboard

Open the **Phone Numbers** page in the dashboard sidebar, click **Add number**, and choose **Buy new number** to purchase a number and bind agents to it. Pick the provider, the country and the number type (standard or toll-free). You can optionally search by area code.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/DR_2iGaVfXqP35L8/images/deploy/purchase-number/purchase-new.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=DR_2iGaVfXqP35L8\&q=85\&s=974a7720a89659ff80677e92f61b6fd3)

After purchasing, you can change the number's nickname to make it easier to find and identify.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/rxvYffEkEJPRL1KD/images/deploy/purchase-number/rename.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=rxvYffEkEJPRL1KD\&q=85\&s=2d38919aecddc341584dff635e13d6a1)

The number is ready to accept [inbound calls](/deploy/inbound-call) once you've assigned an inbound agent. Try calling it.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Some newly purchased numbers have a 2-minute hold on [outbound calls](/deploy/outbound-call) (as of November 2026). This hold does not block inbound calls.

### From the API

Check out [Create Phone Number API Reference](/api-references/create-phone-number)
for all the parameters you can use programmatically.

* Phone numbers are yours once purchased, and can be used indefinitely.
  Find numbers you own [here](/api-references/list-phone-numbers).
* You can assign different inbound and outbound agents to the number.
* If you don't want a user to be able to call this number (maybe you are doing [outbound calls](/deploy/outbound-call) and don't
  want callbacks), you can leave `inbound_agent_id` unset.
* To purchase a US toll-free number, set `toll_free` to `true`. Toll-free numbers cost more than regular numbers. See [Pricing](#pricing).

```typescript Node theme={"dark"}
const phoneNumberResponse = await retell.phoneNumber.create({
  inbound_agent_id: "oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD", // replace with the agent id you want to assign
  outbound_agent_id: "oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD", // replace with the agent id you want to assign
});

console.log(phoneNumberResponse);
```

```python Python theme={"dark"}
# Purchase a phone number
phone_number = client.phone_number.create(
  inbound_agent_id="oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD", # replace with the agent id you want to assign
  outbound_agent_id="oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD", # replace with the agent id you want to assign
)
print(phone_number)
```

### Pricing

We support **Twilio**, **Telnyx** and **Bandwidth** numbers:

* **Twilio**
  * US numbers: **\$2/month**
  * US toll-free numbers: **\$5/month**
  * Canadian numbers: **\$2/month**
* **Telnyx**
  * US numbers only: **\$2/month**
* **Bandwidth**
  * US numbers: **\$2/month**
  * US toll-free numbers: **\$5/month**
  * Canadian numbers: **\$2/month**

> [!NOTE]
>
> Telnyx and Bandwidth numbers do not support SMS registration yet.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Toll-free numbers cost \$0.06 per minute for inbound calls. Outbound calls are charged at the same rate as regular U.S. numbers.

The monthly number fee is billed to your payment method at the end of each billing cycle (prorated if purchased mid-month on credit-based accounts) and recurs until the number is released. See [Billing and payments](/accounts/billing) for how number charges appear on your invoice.

## FAQ

> [accordion] Can I use a phone number I already own?
>
> Yes. Connect your own telephony provider through [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony), or [import an existing number](/api-references/import-phone-number) into Retell.

> [accordion] Can I buy a number outside the US and Canada?
>
> Not directly. Retell-managed numbers are US and Canada only. To use numbers from other countries, connect your own provider via [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony). Retell-managed numbers can still place calls to [15 countries](/deploy/international-call).

> [accordion] How do I release a number I no longer need?
>
> Delete it from the phone number page in the dashboard, or call the [Delete Phone Number API](/api-references/delete-phone-number). The monthly fee stops once the number is released.


# SMS campaign application (A2P 10DLC)
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/sms-campaign-application

Register your business profile, brand, and A2P 10DLC SMS campaign on Retell, with templates and checklists that meet carrier requirements.

To send SMS from your own Retell-managed number, you need an approved A2P 10DLC campaign. US mobile carriers, not Retell, set this requirement: every business that texts from a standard 10-digit number must register with The Campaign Registry (TCR). Retell's telephony provider and the carriers' vetting partners review each application.

Retell submits the application for you but doesn't decide the outcome. This page explains how to give your application the best chance of approval. Most rejections come from missing opt-in, privacy policy, or terms details, so work through every checklist on this page before you submit.

Registration happens in three stages:

1. **Register your business profile.** This runs several checks to make sure your business is eligible for an A2P 10DLC campaign.
2. **Create a brand and get it verified.** This registers your brand with the carriers. After verification, you receive a Trust Score, which sets how many messages you can send a day.
3. **Create a campaign and get it approved.** This describes the messages you'll send and how people opt in.

For the rest of the SMS setup, such as attaching an agent to the number, see [Enable SMS](/deploy/enable-sms).

## Create your business profile and brand

Every business that sends SMS from a Retell US number needs an approved brand registered with the carriers. If your workspace already has a [business profile](/build/telephony/business-profile) and brand for this business, select it instead of creating a new one.

You can start your campaign as soon as your brand is submitted and is verified or pending. Retell holds the campaign and submits it automatically once your brand is verified.

Have these ready:

**Legal business name**, exactly as on your jurisdiction's official registration document, including punctuation and the LLC or Inc suffix.

**Registration ID type and number.** A wide range of registration IDs are supported, including a US EIN, a Canadian Business Number (CBN), or a UK Company Number.

**Business type, industry, and region of operation.**

**Website URL.** It must be live, public, and show the same business name, with no prohibited content anywhere on the site, such as cannabis or CBD, gambling, or sexual content.

**Physical address**, in the same country as your business registration number.

**An authorized representative's details:** first and last name, email, phone number (digits only, such as 4151231234), business title, and job position.

**A valid card on file** in your Retell billing settings.

Retell's messaging provider reviews your profile, and The Campaign Registry checks your brand against official business records. Retell doesn't decide whether to approve or reject.

**1. Add a business profile**

Open your phone number and go to **Advanced Add-Ons** > **SMS** > **Business Profile** > **Add Business Profile**. Fill in the form if you haven't already, and click **Save**.

**2. Choose a brand type**

Under **Brand Registration**, choose a brand type. The brand type can't be changed later.

* **Low-volume standard** (\$4 one time): up to 6,000 message segments a day (2,000 to T-Mobile). Fits most uses, such as reminders, call follow-ups, and support replies.
* **Standard** (\$45 one time): 6,000 to 400,000 segments a day (2,000 to 200,000 to T-Mobile), set by your vetting Trust Score. Suits high-volume notifications or marketing.

Pick standard if your busiest day could exceed the low-volume limit.

**3. Choose a company type and submit**

Choose **Public** or **Private** as the company type. For a public company, also enter your stock exchange and ticker. Then pay the verification fee and submit your brand for review.

If you register as a public company, your representative gets an email to confirm the brand, and the brand stays pending until they click the link in it.

**4. Wait for approval**

Your business profile is reviewed first, then your brand. Together, this usually takes about a week. If either is rejected or not verified, the SMS panel shows the reason in a notice.

To re-verify, click the brand under **Brand Registration** to open **Edit Brand**. You can adjust the company type and stock details, but the brand type stays locked. Click **Save**, then **Submit** to confirm.

Correcting an unverified brand is free. A brand is unverified, or has failed verification, if it hasn't received a Trust Score after going through brand vetting.

### Tips for getting your brand verified

Brands usually fail verification because their details don't match official records. To avoid this:

* **Copy the legal name exactly** from your registration document (the IRS EIN letter in the US), including punctuation and the LLC or Inc suffix. A name mismatch causes most rejections.
* **Use an active registration number** that belongs to that legal name, and pick the correct ID type for the country that issued it.
* **Match your website and address** to the same business name and the address on file with the registration authority.
* **Register the business that sends the messages.** An agency or reseller can't register a client's texts under its own brand.
* **Use a company email for the representative** on your website's domain, not Gmail or another free address. For a public company, The Campaign Registry emails this person to confirm the brand.

## Create your campaign

> [!NOTE]
>
> Write every field of the application in English.

Once your brand is submitted, create your campaign and get it approved. Campaign reviews usually take up to a week.

Open your phone number and go to **Advanced Add-Ons** > **SMS** > **Campaign Registration** > **Add Campaign Application**, then follow the steps below.

![Add Campaign Application dialog over a dimmed phone number page, with empty fields for Application Name, Use Case, Description for the use of sms, two Sample Message boxes, How do end-users consent to receive messages, Privacy Policy URL, and Terms and Conditions URL, all marked required, and a disabled Save button](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/mE3ueFGwO7zT6Bs5/images/sms/sms-campaign-application.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=mE3ueFGwO7zT6Bs5\&q=85\&s=8a516766194f042aee191636e3fff434)

The Add Campaign Application form, with the business profile and brand steps completed behind it.

### Step 1: Choose a use case

Pick the one that describes what you will actually send. If you're unsure, choose **Low Volume Mixed**. Retell's campaign fee is the same for every use case.

| Use case | Choose it when you send | Typical Retell scenario |
| - | - | - |
| Low Volume Mixed | Any combination, at low daily volume (under 2,000 message segments a day to T-Mobile) | Appointment reminders, a small business, or a pilot |
| Mixed | Any combination of the use cases below | Reminders and confirmations, or support plus occasional offers |
| Customer Care | Two-way support, account help, call follow-ups | Post-call summaries, "here's the link we discussed" |
| Delivery Notification | Order, shipping, or service-arrival status | Technician ETA, order ready |
| Account Notification | Account-status notices only, such as balance or plan changes | **Not appointment reminders.** Reviewers reject them, and the use case can't be changed afterwards. |
| Marketing | Promotional messages only: promotions, offers, announcements | Anything with a discount or sales pitch |
| 2FA | One-time passcodes | Verifying a caller's number |
| Security Alert | Account-security alerts, such as a new sign-in | Rare for voice agents |
| Fraud Alert Messaging | Suspicious-activity or fraud warnings | Rare for voice agents |
| Higher Education | Messages from a college or university | Admissions follow-ups |
| Polling and Voting | Non-political surveys and polls | Post-call satisfaction survey |
| Public Service Announcement | Informational messages for the public | Rare |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rejected regardless of use case:**
>
> * Third-party debt collection, debt consolidation, debt relief, and credit repair. A business can message about debts owed to itself, with the customer's consent.
> * Sex, hate, and gambling content, including sweepstakes and raffles. Cannabis, CBD, kratom, and drug paraphernalia businesses are rejected whatever the messages say.
> * Firearms, tobacco, and vape or e-cigarette content, even with age-gating. Alcohol is allowed only with age-gating: visitors must enter their full date of birth before they reach the opt-in page (a yes or no question doesn't count).
> * High-risk financial services: payday and short-term high-interest loans, third-party and student loans, and cryptocurrency or stock trading beyond 2FA and transactional messages.
> * Promotional messages for prescription drugs, get-rich-quick schemes, and phishing.
> * Lead generation, affiliate marketing, or messaging on behalf of a third party.
> * More than one brand in a campaign.
> * Prohibited content anywhere on your website, even on pages that have nothing to do with SMS.

### Step 2: Write the campaign description

The description must say:

* **Who** is sending the messages
* **To whom** you're sending them
* **What** the messages are about
* **When** you typically send them
* **How** recipients opted in

The field accepts 40 to 1,000 characters; aim for three to six sentences, 300 to 700 characters. Short or generic descriptions are a common reason for rejection.

```text Template wrap theme={"dark"}
[Business Name] ([Legal Name] doing business as [Website Name], if different) uses this campaign to send [message type 1], [message type 2] and [message type 3] to [existing customers / patients with a booked appointment]. Recipients opt in [verbally during a call with our automated AI phone assistant / by submitting a form at https://www.yourdomain.com/page / both]. Messages are [transactional only / promotional / a mix] and are sent [after a call / before an appointment / when an order status changes]. Every message identifies [Business Name] and includes opt-out instructions (reply STOP).
```

Example for **Customer Care**:

> Acme Home Services uses this campaign to send two-way customer support messages, follow-ups to phone conversations, requested quotes and service information to existing customers and prospective customers who contact us by phone or request a call on our website at [https://www.acmehomeservices.com/contact](https://www.acmehomeservices.com/contact). Recipients opt in verbally during a call with our automated AI phone assistant, or by submitting our website contact form. Messages are transactional and informational only, sent after a call or when a customer requests information. Every message identifies Acme Home Services and includes opt-out instructions (reply STOP).

Example for **Low Volume Mixed** appointment reminders:

> Bright Smile Dental uses this campaign to send appointment confirmations, appointment reminders, reschedule notices and post-visit follow-ups to patients who have booked an appointment with our office. Patients opt in verbally when they book by phone with our automated scheduling assistant, or by checking the SMS consent box on our online booking form at [https://www.brightsmiledental.com/book](https://www.brightsmiledental.com/book). Messages are informational only and are sent when an appointment is booked, 24 hours before the appointment, and after the visit. Every message identifies Bright Smile Dental and includes opt-out instructions (reply STOP).

> [!TIP]
>
> Say "automated AI phone assistant" plainly. Reviewers accept it, and hiding it reads as evasive. Name the content types you will send and stay consistent with the use case, rather than listing every message you might ever send.

### Step 3: Describe how end users consent

This field must say **where** a person sees the chance to opt in, the **exact action** they take, and every item in the checklist below. The field accepts 40 to 2,048 characters.

Consent must come directly from the person to your business. It can't be implied, collected by or shared with a third party, or taken from a purchased list.

Check that your consent text includes:

Your business name

The kind of messages you'll send

"Message and data rates may apply"

A frequency statement, such as "Message frequency varies" or "up to 4 msgs/month"

Reply STOP to opt out and reply HELP for help

Links to your Privacy Policy and Terms **inside the text**, as full URLs

**Where and how** the customer opts in (your web form's URL, a call with your agent, or a paper form), their "yes" or checked box, and the confirmation text they receive after opting in

**For web forms:** consent is optional, not a condition of purchase, and any checkbox is unchecked by default

**For voice:** the exact script your agent speaks

If you collect consent both ways, include both flows below, followed by one post-opt-in confirmation paragraph with the confirmation text.

**Verbal opt-in during a call**

```text Verbal opt-in flow wrap theme={"dark"}
End users opt in verbally during a phone call with [Business Name]'s automated AI phone assistant. Customers call [Business Name] at [published number] for [support / scheduling / quotes]. Before the call ends, the assistant reads this script:

Assistant: "Before we finish up, would it be alright if [Business Name] sends you text messages regarding [your appointment / a summary of this call]? Message and data rates may apply. Message frequency varies. You can opt out at any time by replying STOP, or reply HELP for help. Our Terms are at https://www.[yourdomain].com/terms and our Privacy Policy is at https://www.[yourdomain].com/privacy. Do I have your permission to send you these texts? Please say yes or no."

Customer: "Yes."

Assistant: "Great, you're opted in. You'll receive a confirmation text shortly. Reply STOP at any time to unsubscribe."

Only after an explicit "yes" does the assistant record consent and send this confirmation text:
"[Business Name]: You're opted in to receive [content type] texts. Msg & data rates may apply. Msg frequency varies. Reply STOP to cancel, HELP for help. https://www.[yourdomain].com/privacy"

If the customer says no or does not answer, no texts are sent.
```

For outbound calls, replace the second sentence of the script with: "\[Business Name]'s assistant calls customers who \[booked an appointment / requested a callback] at the number they provided."

If a website form only requests a callback, submitting it doesn't opt the person in to SMS. Say so in the consent text, then describe how the agent collects consent on the call.

**Web form with a consent checkbox**

```text Web form opt-in flow wrap theme={"dark"}
End users opt in at https://www.[yourdomain].com/[page]. On the form, users enter their phone number and see an optional, unchecked checkbox that reads:

"I agree to receive [transactional / promotional] SMS messages from [Business Name] regarding [content type]. Message and data rates may apply. Message frequency varies. Reply STOP to unsubscribe or HELP for help. Privacy Policy: https://www.[yourdomain].com/privacy. Terms: https://www.[yourdomain].com/terms."

Checking the box is optional and is not a condition of purchase; the form submits with the box unchecked. When submitted with the box checked, this confirmation text is sent:
"[Business Name]: You're opted in to receive [content type] texts. Msg & data rates may apply. Msg frequency varies. Reply STOP to cancel, HELP for help. https://www.[yourdomain].com/privacy"
```

Reviewers open your web form to check:

* The checkbox is unchecked by default and not required to submit.
* Transactional and marketing texts each have their own checkbox.
* SMS consent is separate from email consent and from accepting the Terms.
* The business name on the page matches the brand.
* The form has a field for the person's phone number.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Always include a checkbox, even if you send transactional messages only. Forms without one are rejected as forced opt-in.
>
> If reviewers can't open your opt-in themselves, such as a form behind a login, inside an app, or on paper, take a screenshot of it. Host the screenshot at a public URL on your own domain and paste that link into the consent text.

#### Update your agent to ask for consent

Whenever an agent collects consent, it must say the script you submitted. Add this to your agent's prompt, and paste in the exact script from above:

```text Agent prompt: SMS consent wrap theme={"dark"}
## SMS consent
You may only send a text message after the caller explicitly agrees to receive texts. Before sending any SMS, say this, word for word:

"[Paste the consent script from your campaign application here.]"

- If the caller clearly says yes: say "Great, you're opted in. You'll receive a confirmation text shortly. Reply STOP at any time to unsubscribe." Then send the SMS.
- If the caller says no, is unsure, or does not answer: say "No problem, we won't send you any texts." Do not send any SMS, and do not ask again on this call.
- Never send a text to a number the caller did not confirm is their mobile number.
```

Make the first text the confirmation message, and include the business name and "**Reply STOP to opt out**" in every SMS. If your real traffic doesn't match your samples, the number can be suspended.

### Step 4: Add your Privacy Policy and Terms URLs

Enter the full `https://` address of each page in the **Privacy Policy URL** and **Terms and Conditions URL** fields. Both pages must be live and on your own domain.

Your Privacy Policy must:

Say that **mobile opt-in data is never shared**. Add the clause below to the section on sharing data with third parties.

Show that clause without tabs or expanders. A short dedicated SMS privacy page also works.

Say how you use the data and how people can contact you.

```text Privacy Policy clause wrap theme={"dark"}
No mobile information will be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. All the above categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties.
```

Your Terms of Service must include:

Your business name

The kinds of messages you send

How often you send messages

How to reply STOP to opt out and HELP for help

"Message and data rates may apply"

A support contact

Across both pages, check that:

Both pages are live, use `https://`, sit on your own domain, and **open without logging in**.

Links to both pages appear **inside your consent text**.

### Step 5: Write two sample messages

Each sample must be 20 to 200 characters. Keep it under 160 characters so it sends as one segment. Your samples must:

* Include your **\[Business Name]**.
* Include an opt-out line such as "Reply STOP to opt out."
* Show templated values in square brackets: `[Date]`, `[Time]`, `[Agent Name]`.
* Use only links on your own domain, not a URL shortener like bit.ly.
* Match the use case, the description, and what your website offers.
* Use the same frequency statement, such as "Msg frequency varies" or "up to 4 msgs/month", across both samples and the consent text.

A good pair is one opt-in confirmation plus one message showing your real content. Recount after replacing placeholders: anything over 160 characters sends as two segments.

Retell submits every A2P campaign with "messages contain links" and "messages contain phone numbers" set to yes. Between your two samples, show at least one link on your own domain and one phone number. Some reviewers reject a campaign that declares them but shows neither. The opt-in confirmation below carries the link, so pair it with a content sample that includes a phone number, or add "Questions? Call \[Phone]."

```text Opt-in confirmation (any use case) wrap theme={"dark"}
[Business Name]: You're opted in to receive [content type] texts. Msg & data rates may apply. Msg frequency varies. Reply STOP to cancel, HELP for help. https://www.[yourdomain].com/privacy
```

```text Post-call summary (Customer Care, Mixed) wrap theme={"dark"}
[Business Name]: Thanks for calling today. As discussed, your quote is $[Amount]. Details: https://www.[yourdomain].com/quote/[ID]. Questions? Call [Phone]. Reply STOP to opt out.
```

```text Appointment reminder (Mixed, Low Volume Mixed) wrap theme={"dark"}
Reminder from [Business Name]: you have an appointment tomorrow, [Date] at [Time], at [Address]. Need to reschedule? Call [Phone]. Reply STOP to opt out.
```

```text Technician ETA (Delivery Notification) wrap theme={"dark"}
[Business Name]: Your technician [Name] is on the way and should arrive between [Start] and [End]. Track: https://www.[yourdomain].com/track/[ID]. Reply STOP to opt out.
```

```text Promotional (Marketing, Mixed) wrap theme={"dark"}
[Business Name]: Members get [Offer] on [Service] through [Date]. Book at https://www.[yourdomain].com/book. Msg frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> You don't need to create messaging for the *replies* to HELP, STOP, and START. Retell numbers send them automatically. Make sure your brand has the name customers know you by, along with a support phone, email, or website.

### Step 6: Save and submit

Click **Save**, then click **Next** on the SMS panel to submit the application for this number. Save stays disabled until every required field passes validation.

Registering the campaign costs \$15 one time, charged whether or not it's approved. Resubmitting a rejected campaign under the same use case is free; the \$15 is charged again only if a new campaign has to be registered.

Retell emails your account's email address when you submit, when the campaign is approved or rejected (with the reason), and when the number is enabled for SMS. The status and any rejection reason also show on the SMS panel.

## If your campaign is rejected

The rejection reason shows on the campaign in the dashboard. Fix every issue it names before resubmitting; most rejections cite more than one. To resubmit, click **Edit** on the rejected campaign, fix the fields, click **Save**, then click **Next** on the SMS panel.

Don't resubmit a campaign rejected for prohibited content, such as cannabis, gambling, sexual or hate content, lead generation, or high-risk lending: editing the application can't fix it. Campaigns declined repeatedly without real changes may be flagged, so make sure every resubmission fixes every reported reason.

Only rejected campaigns can be edited, and every field stays editable except **Use Case**. If the reason blames the use case, add a new campaign under the right one instead.

![The Edit Campaign dialog over a dimmed phone number page. A warning at the top reads 'The application was denied. Please correct it and resubmit' with the reason that the Call to Action could not be verified. Below it, Application Name holds the campaign name and is editable. The Use Case field, outlined in blue, is greyed out showing Low Volume Mixed with the note 'Cannot be changed after registration.' The remaining fields are all editable: Description for the use of sms, two Sample Message boxes, and How do end-users consent to receive messages, with Cancel and a disabled Save at the bottom.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/KkwtYfEYwIJC0EjR/images/sms/sms-campaign-use-case-locked.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=KkwtYfEYwIJC0EjR\&q=85\&s=801f55b6e3109277b604667af7eb0f70)

Reopening a rejected campaign. The reason sits at the top and every field stays editable except Use Case.

A rejection cascades downward. When a business profile or brand is rejected, its campaigns are marked rejected too, carrying the same reason. Identical text on all of them means only the profile or brand is at fault. Fix them in this order:

1. **Business profile.** No brand or campaign can be submitted while the business profile is unverified. The usual cause is a legal name or EIN that doesn't match the IRS record. See [handle application rejection](/build/telephony/branded-call-rejection).
2. **Brand.** Reopen it under **Brand Registration** and correct it. While it's rejected, the campaign controls stay disabled.
3. **Campaign.** Edit and resubmit it once the brand is approved or pending. Submitting the number while the brand or campaign is still rejected fails with "Please update and resubmit the brand first" or "...the campaign first".

### What does the rejection wording mean?

| Reviewer wording | Fix |
| - | - |
| "rejected due to issues verifying the Call to Action (CTA)" | Paste the exact opt-in page URL, or the full voice script including the customer's "yes" and the confirmation text. Check that the page opens without logging in and shows the same consent wording you submitted. If it can't be public, link a screenshot of it hosted on your domain. |
| "rejected because of provided Opt-in information" | Add every missing item from the consent checklist in [Step 3](#step-3-describe-how-end-users-consent). |
| "a compliant privacy policy can not be verified" | Link to a page where the no-sharing clause is visible, and paste the link inside the consent text too. |
| "rejected due to Terms and Conditions issues" | Make the terms page live on your domain with the required SMS terms, and link it inside the consent text. |
| "rejected because of invalid campaign description" | Rewrite it with the template in [Step 2](#step-2-write-the-campaign-description). |
| "consent cannot be a required condition for service or transaction completion" | Make the checkbox optional and unchecked, and let the form submit without it. Say so in the consent text. |
| "compliant opt-in consent language is missing or non-compliant" | Quote the exact consent wording, with every checklist item. |
| "rejected because of unverifiable website" | Make the site public, and make sure the business name on it matches the brand. |
| "the provided website URL does not match the Brand and Campaign registered" | Add "\[Legal Name] doing business as \[Website Name]" to the description and consent text. |
| "Appointment reminders are not allowed under Account Notification use case" | Add a new campaign as Low Volume Mixed or Mixed and resubmit. You can't change the use case of a campaign once it's submitted. |
| Use case doesn't match the content | Edit the description and samples to stay inside the use case, such as dropping a promotional sample under Customer Care. If that content is what you actually send, add a new campaign under Mixed instead, since the use case can't be changed once submitted. |
| "The submitted legal company name does not match with US EIN" | Correct the business profile's legal name to match the IRS record exactly. |
| Public URL shortener in a sample | Replace bit.ly or tinyurl links with a URL on your own domain. |
| Prohibited content | Remove debt collection, lending, credit, or other prohibited language from every field. |

## Fees

Retell bills these charges to the card on file (as of November 2026). Retell's telephony and vetting partners, The Campaign Registry, and the mobile carriers can revise them.

| Charge | Amount | When it's charged |
| - | - | - |
| Brand registration, low-volume | \$4, one time | When the brand is first registered. Correcting an unverified or rejected brand is free; you're charged again only if a new brand has to be registered. |
| Brand registration, standard | \$45, one time | Same as low-volume. |
| Campaign registration | \$15, one time | When the campaign is registered, whether or not it's approved. Resubmitting under the same use case is free; you're charged again only if a new campaign has to be registered. |
| SMS add-on | \$20 per number per month | From when the number is approved for SMS until SMS is removed from it. |
| Outbound SMS (managed numbers) | \$0.01 per message | Each message sent, whatever its length. Inbound messages are free. |

## FAQ

> [accordion] Why was my campaign rejected for "Call to Action" or "opt-in information"?
>
> Reviewers couldn't verify how people agree to receive your texts. Add a direct link to your opt-in form (or a public screenshot of it, if the form is behind a login), or the agent's full consent script, and include every item in the consent checklist in [Step 3](#step-3-describe-how-end-users-consent). These are the most common reasons for rejection.

> [accordion] My rejection lists several reasons. Can I fix them one at a time?
>
> No. Fix every reason before you resubmit. Every resubmission is reviewed in full, so fixing one reason at a time means another rejection for the rest.

> [accordion] Can my AI agent collect consent verbally on a call?
>
> Yes. Paste the exact script your agent speaks, including the customer's "yes" and the confirmation text they receive.

> [accordion] Can I make SMS consent required to book or buy?
>
> No. Consent must be optional and not a condition of purchase, and any checkbox must be unchecked by default. Reviewers reject any flow where texts are required. They also reject forms where the consent checkbox is missing.

> [accordion] Which use case should I pick for appointment reminders?
>
> Low Volume Mixed, or Mixed if you send more than 6,000 message segments a day (more than 2,000 to T-Mobile). Don't choose Account Notification: reviewers reject reminders filed there, and the use case can't be changed afterwards.

> [accordion] My brand was rejected because the legal name doesn't match my EIN. What do I do?
>
> Edit the business profile so the legal name matches your IRS EIN letter exactly, including punctuation and the suffix (LLC, Inc). Then resubmit the brand. This is one of the most common reasons a brand is rejected.

> [accordion] Can I register a non-US number?
>
> No. SMS registration is available only for US phone numbers.

> [accordion] How long does review take, and where do I see the result?
>
> Usually up to a week after submission. Retell emails you when the campaign is approved or rejected, and the status shows on the SMS panel for the number.

> [accordion] What does SMS cost after approval?
>
> \$20 a month per number plus \$0.01 per outbound message, on top of the one-time brand and campaign registration fees. Inbound messages are free. See [Fees](#fees) for the full list.

> [accordion] Do I need the brand approved before I submit the campaign?
>
> No. You can file the campaign as soon as the brand exists and isn't rejected. Retell holds it as pending and submits it for review automatically once the brand is approved.

> [accordion] Does resubmitting a rejected campaign cost another \$15?
>
> No, as long as the use case is unchanged. The corrected campaign is edited in place and reviewed again at no extra charge. You're charged \$15 again only when a new campaign has to be registered, which happens if the use case changed, the brand was re-registered, or the in-place edit was declined.

> [accordion] My business profile, brand, and campaign were all rejected. What do I fix first?
>
> The business profile, then the brand, then the campaign. A rejected business profile marks its brand and campaigns rejected as well, with the same reason. Correcting an unverified brand is free as long as the brand type stays the same. Campaign controls stay disabled until the brand is approved or pending.

> [accordion] The rejection says my use case is wrong. Can I just change it?
>
> No, Use Case is read-only after registration. File a new campaign under the right use case with **Add Campaign Application**, select it, and click **Next** to point the number at it. The new campaign is charged as a new registration (see [Fees](#fees)). Deleting the SMS capability first isn't necessary while the number's application is rejected.

> [accordion] Can I edit a campaign that is pending or approved?
>
> No. Only rejected campaigns can be edited. To change what an approved number sends, delete the SMS capability on the number and create a new campaign. Your business profile and brand are kept and reused.

> [accordion] Can I skip the campaign application?
>
> If you only need to send a fixed message during calls, you can send from an SMS-approved Retell number with no application. The content is a preset template you can't customize, and two-way SMS isn't supported. See [Option 3 on the SMS page](/deploy/enable-sms#option-3-use-an-sms-approved-retell-number-no-a2p-required).

> [accordion] Do I need to set up STOP and HELP keywords?
>
> No. Replies to STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT, REVOKE, OPTOUT, HELP, and START are handled automatically on Retell numbers. Your samples and opt-in script must still tell people they can reply STOP. Make sure your brand also shows the name customers know you by, plus a support phone, email, or website.


# Telnyx
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/telnyx

Connect Retell to a Telnyx account with elastic SIP trunking — create the trunk, configure FQDN routing, set up outbound auth, and import Telnyx numbers.

Connect a Telnyx number to Retell with [elastic SIP trunking](/deploy/custom-telephony), so your agents can make and receive calls on numbers you own in Telnyx. Create an FQDN trunk, configure routing and codecs, set up outbound auth, then import the number into Retell.

**1. Create elastic SIP trunking**

1. Create the trunk, select FQDN as the type, and give it a name.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/create.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=a0b5c74d7b0f9d0a27d6a2fb903b232b)

2. Add FQDN

Add the FQDN of Retell's SIP server: `sip.retellai.com`. Select `SRV` as the
DNS record type.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/setting.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=5c21b0780b66885597c416d98dd8fe1e)

3. Set up outbound calls authentication

Select credentials as the authentication method, and add the username and password.
You will need to use this username and password when importing the number to Retell.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/outbound-auth.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=87ba94312ebb879e7dc9b19ed27e5bf6)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Telnyx requires the header `X-Telnyx-Username: <username>` to be included in the outbound calls when using credentials as the authentication mechanism.
> See Telnyx [documentation](https://support.telnyx.com/en/articles/5271423-guide-to-sip-anchorsite-settings#h_0b59d6992a) for more details.
> You can find details on adding [custom SIP headers](/build/telephony/sip-headers), or on the [Make outbound calls](/deploy/outbound-call#step-2-make-outbound-calls) page.

4. Set up inbound setting

* Select `+E.164` as the number format.
* Select `G722`, `G711U`, `G711A` as the codecs.
* Select `TCP` as the transport method. (TCP is recommended over UDP for reliability.)
* Select your SIP region.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/TRHbNQLLwdXdtkVi/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/inbound-setting.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=TRHbNQLLwdXdtkVi\&q=85\&s=202c89ac9ebd5fe08ae5e24a9698541c)

5. Set up outbound setting

Create a new outbound voice profile

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/voice-profile.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=eb72458506714003dab29aec2140cdbb)

And select that in the outbound setting

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/outbound-setting.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=7a33bb6784839e1e0dbb662c4064c5bd)

**2. Move numbers to elastic SIP trunking**

You've created the elastic SIP trunk. Now purchase numbers or move
existing numbers to this trunk.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/telnyx/assign-number.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=a7118a51ec9841b2bed9c3d62d5b6a86)

**3. Import numbers to Retell**

Now that the number is set up with your elastic SIP trunk, import it to Retell so we know how to route the call.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/import-number.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=19c4a219923eb0adc03c807cb8d767c3)

Here you will supply Telnyx's FQDN as the termination SIP URI. You can find your FQDN based on
your choice of SIP region in this [doc](https://sip.telnyx.com/) (e.g. sip.telnyx.com). You will also need to supply
the username, password and any additional SIP headers you set up earlier in the outbound authentication as well.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/import-number-detail-telnyx.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=bdd4e9d406b74aa12a779c94c9d8697d)

Before saving, click **Test SIP Connection** to [check the termination connection](/deploy/custom-telephony#test-your-sip-connection). The test uses the termination URI, transport, and credentials; it does not validate your custom SIP headers. After saving, place real calls to verify the full configuration.

You can also import numbers programmatically via [Import Number API](/api-references/import-phone-number).

Now that the number is imported, you can make and receive calls with it just like a number
purchased from Retell. It shows up in your dashboard, and you can make phone calls from the
dashboard directly. You can also use the [Create Phone Call API](/api-references/create-phone-call)
to create calls programmatically.
To have Retell stop using this number, delete it from the dashboard or via
the [Delete Number API](/api-references/delete-phone-number).

## Troubleshooting

If an inbound call fails, check the FQDN and inbound settings on your Telnyx trunk. If an outbound call fails, check the termination FQDN, credentials, and the `X-Telnyx-Username` header you supplied to Retell. See [Debug outbound call](/reliability/debug-outbound-call) for common SIP failures, or [debug SIP calls with PCAP files](/reliability/debug-calls-pcap) to inspect the signaling in Wireshark.


# Connect a Twilio number to Retell with elastic SIP trunking
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/twilio

Connect Retell to your Twilio account using elastic SIP trunking. Set up termination, origination, credentials, and import Twilio numbers into Retell.

Connect a Twilio number to Retell with [elastic SIP trunking](/deploy/custom-telephony), so your agents can make and receive calls on numbers you own in Twilio. Set up termination (outbound) and origination (inbound), add credentials, then import the number into Retell.

## Steps

**1. Create elastic SIP trunking**

1. Create the trunk, give it a name, and toggle some general settings

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/general.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=45e4528d4346100ac95626af7b68ecd1)

2. Set up termination (this is for outbound)

* The termination SIP URI here is important; you'll use it in later steps. Use a localized termination URI near your region. You can expand and view your localized URIs in the Twilio console.
* A localized termination SIP URI uses the format `{your-trunk-domain}.pstn.{edge}.twilio.com`. For example, a trunk with the termination domain `my-retell-trunk` that uses the Ashburn (Virginia) edge looks like this:

```text theme={"dark"}
my-retell-trunk.pstn.ashburn.twilio.com
```

Replace `ashburn` with the edge closest to you, such as `umatilla`, `dublin`, `frankfurt`, `singapore`, `tokyo`, `sao-paulo`, or `sydney`. See Twilio's [localized termination URIs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/global-infrastructure/localized-uris/termination) for the full list.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/termination.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=914580b920340ea68cc0538f86b4634f)

* For your elastic SIP trunk to accept our outbound request, you need to whitelist
  an IP address or create an auth with a username and password.

  * If you opt for the auth route, you need to specify the username and password
    in the next step when importing the number to Retell.

  ![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/auth.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=b80e3f28082c1994258c80e484a32008)

  * Whitelist Retell's SIP SBC CIDR block `18.98.16.120/30` (signaling only):

  ![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/7L57j1f5OEkhUYOX/images/custom-telephony/twilio/acl.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=7L57j1f5OEkhUYOX\&q=85\&s=c2c2fb7e31abc2dd483a233aa639a2ce)

3. Set up origination (this is for inbound)

* Here you will specify Retell's SIP server address as the origination SIP URI:
  `sip:sip.retellai.com`.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/YUAGucMAZXdWZD8p/images/custom-telephony/twilio/origination.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=YUAGucMAZXdWZD8p\&q=85\&s=4267334c1b7365c242ab6f271d3efc66)

**2. Move numbers to elastic SIP trunking**

You've created the elastic SIP trunk. Now purchase numbers or move
existing numbers to this trunk.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/numbers.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=c0dc1323bc03138d736eaa31305f5d3a)

**3. Import numbers to Retell**

Now that the number is set up with your elastic SIP trunk, import it to Retell so we know how to route the call.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/import-number.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=19c4a219923eb0adc03c807cb8d767c3)

Here you supply the termination SIP URI you set up in Step 1. If you set up
auth via credentials, supply the username and password as well.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/import-number-detail-twilio.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=da61515fce726ff48b2a00846f81e190)

Before saving, click **Test SIP Connection** to [check the termination connection](/deploy/custom-telephony#test-your-sip-connection). After saving, place real calls to verify inbound routing and audio.

You can also import numbers programmatically via [Import Number API](/api-references/import-phone-number).

Now that the number is imported, you can make and receive calls with it just like a number
purchased from Retell. It shows up in your dashboard, and you can make phone calls from the
dashboard directly. You can also use the [Create Phone Call API](/api-references/create-phone-call)
to create calls programmatically.
To have Retell stop using this number, delete it from the dashboard or via
the [Delete Number API](/api-references/delete-phone-number).

## Common issues

**1. After connecting, inbound works but outbound does not?**

* Check your termination SIP URI.
  If there's a space in it, remove it. Also use a localized termination URI near your region. See this [doc](https://www.twilio.com/docs/global-infrastructure/localized-uris/termination) to select one.

* Check your username and credentials.
  Make sure you entered the username and credentials shown in this dialog.
  Note that the username is not the friendly name shown in the credential list;
  double-check that you didn't confuse the two.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/credentials.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=9261227c219742c9a8d02d29dde0d326)

**2. How do I enable call transfers on a Twilio trunk?**

Retell's [Call Transfer tool](/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call) works over your Twilio trunk, but two Twilio-side settings matter:

* **Cold transfer with SIP REFER**: your trunk must allow SIP REFER and PSTN transfer. Enable this in the Twilio console for the elastic SIP trunk. See [Custom telephony FAQ](/deploy/custom-telephony) for the exact setting.
* **Custom SIP headers on cold transfer**: Twilio does not honor custom SIP headers on SIP REFER, so headers you set in the Call Transfer tool are dropped for cold transfers over Twilio. Use SIP INVITE if you need those headers to reach the destination. See [SIP headers](/build/telephony/sip-headers).
* **Dialing outside your country**: enable the destination country under **Voice Geographic Permissions → Elastic SIP Trunking** (see below).

**3. How do I set up dialing to international countries?**

* Search "geo" to find the "Voice Geographic Permissions" setting.

  ![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/geo.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=a0c345fdd79fd5ae1a1018630ec9c472)

* Choose "Elastic SIP Trunking" in the selector, and select the countries you would like to dial. See [International calling](/deploy/international-call) for Retell's supported destinations and fees.

  ![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7/images/custom-telephony/twilio/international.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=32uO5g9DswfoJ9j7\&q=85\&s=e63218daa41a0660de38538b952785e8)

Still stuck? See [Debug outbound call](/reliability/debug-outbound-call) for common SIP failures, or [debug SIP calls with PCAP files](/reliability/debug-calls-pcap) to inspect the signaling in Wireshark.

## Phone number masking

If you have a personal phone number or a trusted business number you'd like to display to the callee, you can import verified phone numbers into Twilio to serve as the caller ID.

### Add a caller ID

1. Go to the [Verified Caller IDs page](https://www.twilio.com/console/phone-numbers/verified?_gl=1*l511c3*_gcl_aw*R0NMLjE3NTQ0MTE4NjUuQ2p3S0NBancxZExEQmhCb0Vpd0FRTlJpUVk5QWVqRDFrc2hEZl9ycVdOVlI4bmR3RVNTei1nM3JBcGpORVFXX3BCLXdMRFZPTnM3ei14b0NWNmdRQXZEX0J3RQ..*_gcl_au*MTAzNDAwNDYyNi4xNzUyNTE4OTQy*_ga*MjA5ODY1MzAyMS4xNzUyNTE4OTQy*_ga_RRP8K4M4F3*czE3NTczNzcyODAkbzI0JGcxJHQxNzU3MzgwOTUxJGo2MCRsMCRoMA..)
2. Click **Add a new Caller ID**
3. Enter the desired phone number to verify, select the desired verification method, and then click **Verify Number**

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/wDbYgGV0r_bHeVyI/images/custom-telephony/twilio/add-caller-id.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=wDbYgGV0r_bHeVyI\&q=85\&s=9b365e1a769c73efccf907d0431497b1)

4. The number entered will receive an OTP Authentication code for verification. Enter this verification code on the next window.

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/T6odbQPcAHafphF3/images/custom-telephony/twilio/otp-code.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=T6odbQPcAHafphF3\&q=85\&s=6af725385dab140d234749ffb9a82ef7)

5. Once you click **Submit**, if the correct OTP code was entered, you will receive a **Successful** notification and the number will be added to your account as a verified caller ID.

### Configure SIP header rules to display caller ID

This uses Twilio's own header manipulation. To set or parse [custom SIP headers](/build/telephony/sip-headers) on the Retell side, see the SIP headers guide.

1. In the Twilio Console, navigate to Elastic SIP Trunking → Trunks → \[your trunk] → Termination
2. Scroll down to Header Manipulation and open **View all SIP header manipulation policies**

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/xg079QHgWguuhP1T/images/custom-telephony/twilio/header-policies.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=xg079QHgWguuhP1T\&q=85\&s=1bcd8c4549e65c7d06945d4cd88b6123)

3. Click on **Create a policy** in the top right and give your policy a friendly name
4. Click on **+ Add request rule** and give the rule a friendly name
5. Under the Actions section, set the following values:
   * **SIP header field**: **From number**
   * **Action**: **Replace with**
   * **Value**: Your caller ID in E.164 format (e.g. +18881230987)

![](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/xg079QHgWguuhP1T/images/custom-telephony/twilio/actions.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=xg079QHgWguuhP1T\&q=85\&s=ab914fc9a20b9bfb5c33e8c619a93900)

6. Click **Add rule**, and then click **Save policy**
7. Return to the Termination tab within your trunk, and select the new header manipulation policy from the dropdown
8. Now, any number imported from this Twilio trunk into your Retell account will use your verified caller ID. Place an outbound test call to validate the changes.
   * *Note:* You will need at least one number purchased from Twilio in your SIP trunk in order to apply the caller ID.

# Make a web call
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call

Make browser voice calls with Retell: use the Web SDK to connect users to an agent, control microphone audio, and handle transcripts and call events.

A web call connects a user to your voice agent directly in the browser, using their microphone and speakers. The [Retell Web SDK](https://github.com/RetellAI/retell-client-js-sdk) creates the call and connects its audio; no phone number is involved.

## When to use web calls

* **Voice inside your product.** Add a support agent to your help center, a sales assistant to a landing page, or voice-guided onboarding, with a UI you fully control.
* **Custom call experiences.** Build call controls and audio visualizations. Enable live transcripts separately for captions or conversation flow updates.
* **Development and testing.** Talk to an agent while building it. For a quick test without writing code, use the dashboard's [web call testing](/test/test-web).

If you want a voice entry point on your website without building a frontend, embed the [website widget](/deploy/chat-widget). For iOS and Android apps, see [web calls in native apps](/deploy/native-web-call). To reach users on their phones, see [outbound calls](/deploy/outbound-call) and [inbound calls](/deploy/inbound-call).

For example, an e-commerce site adds a "Talk to support" button to its order page. Clicking it starts a web call that passes the customer's name and order ID as [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables), so the agent can look up the right order.

## Set up web calls

**1. Install the Web SDK**

```bash theme={"dark"}
npm install retell-client-js-sdk@latest
```

**2. Configure authentication**

Create a [public key](/accounts/public-keys) and allow your website's domain. Add `localhost` to test locally. Use the public key in your browser code; keep API keys on your server.

If your public key has reCAPTCHA enabled, obtain a fresh token before each call and pass it as `recaptchaToken` to `createWebCall()`.

**3. Create and connect the call**

Initialize `RetellClient` and call `createWebCall()` from your button's click handler. Replace the public key and agent ID with your own values.

```javascript theme={"dark"}
import { RetellClient } from "retell-client-js-sdk";

const client = new RetellClient({ key: "public_key_YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY" });
let call;

function startCall() {
  if (call && call.status !== "ended") return;

  call = client.createWebCall({
    agent_id: "agent_oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD",
    retell_llm_dynamic_variables: { customer_name: "John Doe" },
    metadata: { internal_customer_id: "cust_123" },
    hooks: {
      onStatus: (status) => console.log("Call status:", status),
      onEnd: () => console.log("Call ended"),
      onError: (error) => console.error("Call error:", error),
    },
  });
}
```

`createWebCall()` returns a session immediately with `status: "connecting"`, then reports `live` and `ended` through `onStatus`. Audio may take a moment to connect after `live`. Once creation succeeds, `call.callId` identifies the call.

The browser prompts for microphone permission. Serve your page over HTTPS; `localhost` also works during development.

`agent_id` is the only required call option. Common optional fields:

| Field | What it does |
| - | - |
| `retell_llm_dynamic_variables` | String key-value pairs injected into the agent's prompt and tool descriptions as [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables). |
| `metadata` | An arbitrary object stored on the call, such as an internal customer ID. Not used for processing; returned when you retrieve the call later. |
| `agent_version` | The numeric [agent version](/agent/version) to use for this call. |
| `agent_override` | Override agent configuration for this call only. |

See [Create Web Call](/api-references/create-web-call) for the REST request fields, and [audio controls](#control-audio-during-the-call) for browser audio options.

**4. End the call**

```javascript theme={"dark"}
await call?.end();
```

The agent can also end the call. Either way, the session reports `ended` through `onStatus` and fires `onEnd`.

## Handle call events

Pass hooks when creating the call, as shown above, or register listeners on the returned session:

```javascript theme={"dark"}
call.on("end", () => {
  console.log("Call ended");
});
```

| Hook | Event | When it fires |
| - | - | - |
| `onStatus` | `status` | The session reports `live` or `ended`. Read the initial `call.status` for `connecting`. |
| `onAudio` | `audio` | An audio visualization snapshot is available. Requires `audio.emitRawAudioSamples`. |
| `onEnd` | `end` | The session ends, including after a failed connection. The payload may be empty. |
| `onError` | `error` | The SDK reports an error, such as a failed creation request or microphone permission denial. The payload is an `Error` object. |
| `onTranscript` | `transcript` | The live transcript changes. Requires the transcript connection described below. |
| `onNodeTransition` | `node_transition` | A conversation flow node first appears in the transcript, including nodes in the initial snapshot. Requires the transcript connection. |

Reset call controls in `onEnd`, including when no `onError` fires. Use [Get Call](/api-references/get-call) for the recorded disconnection reason.

## Enable live transcripts

Live transcripts use a separate [monitoring WebSocket](/api-references/monitor-call-websocket) and are off by default. With the public-key client configured above, add `transcript: true`:

```javascript theme={"dark"}
call = client.createWebCall({
  agent_id: "agent_oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD",
  transcript: true,
  hooks: {
    onTranscript: (transcript, preSessionTranscript) => {
      console.log("Conversation:", transcript);
      console.log("Pre-session tools:", preSessionTranscript);
    },
    onNodeTransition: (transition) => console.log("Flow node:", transition),
    onError: (error) => console.error("Call error:", error),
  },
});
```

`onTranscript` receives the full transcript so far and a separate array of pre-session tool calls. The SDK merges updates by each item's stable ID. Items include spoken turns, tool calls, and flow nodes; see the [transcript item spec](/api-references/monitor-call-websocket#transcript-item-spec). Transcript text can change as a turn progresses and does not mark exact speaking boundaries.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If the optional transcript connection fails, the SDK logs a console warning and the audio call continues. This failure does not fire `onError`. See [WebSocket authentication](/api-references/monitor-call-websocket#authentication) if you create calls through your own backend.

To follow a web call from a second screen, or to let a supervisor step in, see [Monitor live calls](/features/live-monitoring).

## Control audio during the call

Mute and unmute the microphone without ending the call:

```javascript theme={"dark"}
call.mute();
call.unmute();
```

Some browsers block playback until the user interacts with the page. To resume audio, call this from a click handler:

```javascript theme={"dark"}
await call.startAudioPlayback();
```

Pass capture, playback, or visualization settings in the `audio` option of `createWebCall()`:

| Option | Type | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `sampleRate` | number | Requested audio sample rate. See [audio basics](/knowledge/audio-basics). |
| `captureDeviceId` | string | Microphone device ID. |
| `playbackDeviceId` | string | Speaker device ID. |
| `emitRawAudioSamples` | boolean | Emit `Float32Array` snapshots through `onAudio` or the `audio` event. Defaults to `false`. |

Use `onAudio` snapshots to calculate a level for an orb or volume meter. They contain incoming audio, including any background sound, and are sampled for visualization rather than continuous recording.

## After the call

Collect full results after the call ends:

* [Register a webhook](/features/register-webhook) to receive `call_started`, `call_ended`, and `call_analyzed` events on your server.
* Use `call.callId` with the [get call API](/api-references/get-call) to fetch the complete transcript, recording, and analysis, or review the call in [session history](/features/session-history).

## Example project

The [React and Node.js demo](https://github.com/RetellAI/retell-frontend-reactjs-demo) uses `RetellClient` with an API key kept on the Node.js backend.

## FAQ

> [accordion] Why does my call fail before it starts?
>
> Read the error passed to `onError`. Check your public key's allowed domains, the agent ID, and microphone permission. If reCAPTCHA is enabled, provide a fresh token for each call.

> [accordion] Why can't the user hear the agent?
>
> Browsers can block audio playback before user interaction. Start the call from a click handler, or call `call.startAudioPlayback()` inside one.

> [accordion] Why doesn't the microphone work?
>
> The user may have denied microphone permission, or the page isn't served over HTTPS. Microphone access requires a secure context; localhost works during development.

> [accordion] How do I pass customer data into the call?
>
> Use `retell_llm_dynamic_variables` for values the agent should use in conversation. Use `metadata` for values you only need to look up later, such as an internal customer ID. See [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables).

> [accordion] Do web calls count toward my concurrency limit?
>
> Yes. Web calls draw from the same [concurrency](/deploy/concurrency) pool as outbound phone calls.


# Explicit cold transfer mode selection
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/01-23_cold_transfer_mode_selection

On 01/23/2026 the `show_transferee_as_caller` field changes meaning — Retell switches to explicit cold transfer mode between SIP REFER and SIP INVITE.

## Cold Transfer Mode Selection

The behavior of the `show_transferee_as_caller` parameter in Cold Transfer options is changing. Previously, this parameter was used to toggle between SIP REFER and SIP INVITE transfer modes.

**Affected APIs:**

* [Create Retell LLM](/api-references/create-retell-llm)
* [Update Retell LLM](/api-references/update-retell-llm)
* [Create Conversation Flow](/api-references/create-conversation-flow)
* [Update Conversation Flow](/api-references/update-conversation-flow)
* [Create Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/create-conversation-flow-component)
* [Update Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/update-conversation-flow-component)

**What's changing:**

* The `show_transferee_as_caller` parameter will no longer control the transfer mode (SIP REFER vs SIP INVITE).
* Use the new `cold_transfer_mode` parameter to explicitly choose between `sip_refer` and `sip_invite`.
* The `show_transferee_as_caller` parameter will only control caller ID display and will only take effect when `cold_transfer_mode` is set to `sip_invite`.

**Migration:**

* Set `cold_transfer_mode` to `sip_refer` or `sip_invite` to choose the transfer method.
* Set `show_transferee_as_caller` to `true` only if you want to show the transferee as the caller when using `sip_invite` mode.

**Effective date:** After 01/23/2026, `show_transferee_as_caller` will no longer affect the transfer mode selection.


# Phone number single-agent fields removed
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/03-31_phone_number_agent_fields

On 03/31/2026 Retell deprecates single-agent fields on phone numbers in favor of weighted inbound, outbound, and SMS agent lists across the phone number APIs.

## Phone number single-agent fields

The single-agent fields on phone number configuration are deprecated in favor of weighted agent lists for inbound/outbound calls and SMS.

**Affected APIs:**

* [Create Phone Number](/api-references/create-phone-number)
* [Import Phone Number](/api-references/import-phone-number)
* [Update Phone Number](/api-references/update-phone-number)
* [Get Phone Number](/api-references/get-phone-number)
* [List Phone Numbers](/api-references/list-phone-numbers)

**Deprecated fields:**

* `inbound_agent_id`, `inbound_agent_version`
* `outbound_agent_id`, `outbound_agent_version`
* `inbound_sms_agent_id`, `inbound_sms_agent_version`
* `outbound_sms_agent_id`, `outbound_sms_agent_version`

**Use instead:**

* `inbound_agents`
* `outbound_agents`
* `inbound_sms_agents`
* `outbound_sms_agents`

**Migration:**

* For a single agent, set the corresponding `*_agents` list to a single entry with `weight: 1`.
* For multiple agents, split weights so they sum to 1.
* For SMS, use `*_sms_agents` with the same weighting rules.

**Note:** Existing data is converted automatically and no action is required. Until the deprecation date, the APIs remain backwards-compatible as long as only a single agent is used for each of the deprecated fields.

**Example:**

* Before:
  ```json theme={"dark"}
  {
    "inbound_agent_id": "oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD",
    "inbound_agent_version": 3
  }
  ```
* After:
  ```json theme={"dark"}
  {
    "inbound_agents": [
      { "agent_id": "oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD", "agent_version": 3, "weight": 1 }
    ]
  }
  ```

**Effective date:** After 03/31/2026, the deprecated single-agent fields will no longer be supported.

# Conversation node tools replaced by subagent
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/04-18_conversation_node_tools

On 04/18/2026 Retell deprecates `tools` and `tool_ids` on conversation nodes in favor of the new subagent node for dialogue that calls tools mid-call.

## Deprecating tools on conversation nodes — use subagent nodes instead

The `tools` and `tool_ids` fields on conversation nodes are deprecated in favor of the new `subagent` node type. The conversation node type itself is **not** deprecated — it continues to work for nodes that don't use tools. The new `subagent` node type provides the same conversation-with-tools functionality — the agent converses with the user while being able to call tools — but as a dedicated node type.

**Affected APIs:**

* [Create Conversation Flow](/api-references/create-conversation-flow)
* [Update Conversation Flow](/api-references/update-conversation-flow)
* [Get Conversation Flow](/api-references/get-conversation-flow)
* [List Conversation Flows](/api-references/list-conversation-flows)
* [Create Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/create-conversation-flow-component)
* [Update Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/update-conversation-flow-component)
* [Get Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/get-conversation-flow-component)
* [List Conversation Flow Components](/api-references/list-conversation-flow-components)

**Deprecated fields on `type: "conversation"` nodes:**

* `tools`
* `tool_ids`

**Use instead:** Set `type: "subagent"` on nodes that need tools.

**What's changing on 04/18/2026:**

1. Existing conversation nodes with tools will be automatically migrated to `type: "subagent"` — API responses will return the new type for these nodes.
2. Conversation nodes with tools that use static text instructions will be converted to subagent nodes with prompt text instructions.
3. The API will stop accepting `tools` or `tool_ids` fields on `type: "conversation"` nodes.

**Migration:**

* For conversation nodes **with** tools: change `type` from `"conversation"` to `"subagent"`. If the node uses a `static_text` instruction, change it to `prompt`. All other fields remain the same.
* For conversation nodes **without** tools: no changes needed — these remain `type: "conversation"`.

**Example:**

* Before:
  ```json theme={"dark"}
  {
    "id": "handle_order",
    "type": "conversation",
    "instruction": {
      "text": "Help the user check their order status.",
      "type": "prompt"
    },
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "custom_function",
        "name": "check_order_status",
        "description": "Look up order by order number",
        "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string" } } }
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
* After:
  ```json theme={"dark"}
  {
    "id": "handle_order",
    "type": "subagent",
    "instruction": {
      "text": "Help the user check their order status.",
      "type": "prompt"
    },
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "custom_function",
        "name": "check_order_status",
        "description": "Look up order by order number",
        "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string" } } }
      }
    ]
  }
  ```

**Effective date:** After 04/18/2026, the API will no longer accept `tools` or `tool_ids` on `type: "conversation"` nodes. Use `type: "subagent"` instead.

# Legacy list endpoints removed for v2/v3
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/06-15_legacy_list_endpoints

On 06/15/2026 Retell removes legacy list endpoints (batch tests, conversation flows, phone numbers, Retell LLMs) — migrate to versioned v2 and v3 endpoints.

## Legacy list endpoints are deprecated

The following list endpoints are deprecated in favor of newer versioned endpoints with unified pagination patterns.

**Affected APIs:**

* [List Batch Tests](/api-references/list-batch-tests)
* [List Conversation Flow Components](/api-references/list-conversation-flow-components)
* [List Conversation Flows](/api-references/list-conversation-flows)
* [List Phone Numbers](/api-references/list-phone-numbers)
* [List Retell LLMs](/api-references/list-retell-llms)
* [List Test Case Definitions](/api-references/list-test-case-definitions)
* [List Test Runs](/api-references/list-test-runs)
* [List Calls](/api-references/list-calls)
* [List Chats](/api-references/list-chats)

## Endpoint migrations

* `GET /list-batch-tests` -> `GET /v2/list-batch-tests` ([List Batch Tests](/api-references/list-batch-tests))
* `GET /list-conversation-flow-components` -> `GET /v2/list-conversation-flow-components` ([List Conversation Flow Components](/api-references/list-conversation-flow-components))
* `GET /list-conversation-flows` -> `GET /v2/list-conversation-flows` ([List Conversation Flows](/api-references/list-conversation-flows))
* `GET /list-phone-numbers` -> `POST /v2/list-phone-numbers` ([List Phone Numbers](/api-references/list-phone-numbers))
* `GET /list-retell-llms` -> `GET /v2/list-retell-llms` ([List Retell LLMs](/api-references/list-retell-llms))
* `GET /list-test-case-definitions` -> `GET /v2/list-test-case-definitions` ([List Test Case Definitions](/api-references/list-test-case-definitions))
* `GET /list-test-runs/{test_case_batch_job_id}` -> `GET /v2/list-test-runs/{test_case_batch_job_id}` ([List Test Runs](/api-references/list-test-runs))
* `POST /v2/list-calls` -> `POST /v3/list-calls` ([List Calls](/api-references/list-calls))
* `GET /list-chat` -> `POST /v3/list-chats` ([List Chats](/api-references/list-chats))

> [!NOTE]
>
> `GET /v2/list-phone-numbers` also replaces `GET /list-phone-numbers`, and Retell isn't removing it soon. Don't use it for new integrations. `POST /v2/list-phone-numbers` takes the same pagination query parameters, returns the same response, and adds optional `filter_criteria` in the request body.

**What's changing on 06/15/2026:**

1. The legacy list endpoints above will no longer be supported.
2. `GET /list-chat` changes both method and path to `POST /v3/list-chats`.
3. Versioned list endpoints return unified pagination fields: `items`, `pagination_key`, and `has_more`.

**Migration:**

* Update each client call to the new method/path listed above.
* Update response handling to read `items` from the paginated response object (instead of expecting a top-level array from legacy endpoints).
* Keep using `pagination_key` and `has_more` for page traversal.

**Effective date:** After 06/15/2026, the legacy endpoints listed above will no longer be supported.

## Analysis prompt fields are deprecated

The following top-level analysis prompt fields on voice and chat agent configurations are deprecated in favor of the `post_call_analysis_data` and `post_chat_analysis_data` arrays.

**Deprecated fields:**

* `analysis_summary_prompt`
* `analysis_successful_prompt`
* `analysis_user_sentiment_prompt`

These fields exist on both voice agent and chat agent endpoints:

* [Create Agent](/api-references/create-agent) / [Update Agent](/api-references/update-agent)
* [Create Chat Agent](/api-references/create-chat-agent) / [Update Chat Agent](/api-references/update-chat-agent)

**What's changing on 06/15/2026:**

1. The three prompt fields above will be removed from the API.
2. Use system preset items inside `post_call_analysis_data` (voice agents) or `post_chat_analysis_data` (chat agents) to customize prompts for summary, success, and sentiment analysis.

**Migration:**

Replace each deprecated field with a system preset entry in the corresponding analysis data array. Set `type` to `system-presets`, `name` to the preset identifier, and `description` to your custom prompt.

| Deprecated field | Preset `name` (voice) | Preset `name` (chat) |
| - | - | - |
| `analysis_summary_prompt` | `call_summary` | `chat_summary` |
| `analysis_successful_prompt` | `call_successful` | `chat_successful` |
| `analysis_user_sentiment_prompt` | `user_sentiment` | `user_sentiment` |

For example, if you currently set `analysis_summary_prompt` on a voice agent:

```json Before theme={"dark"}
{
  "analysis_summary_prompt": "Summarize the outcome of the conversation in two sentences."
}
```

```json After theme={"dark"}
{
  "post_call_analysis_data": [
    {
      "type": "system-presets",
      "name": "call_summary",
      "description": "Summarize the outcome of the conversation in two sentences."
    }
  ]
}
```
