# Legacy agent list endpoints removed
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/07-31_agent_list_endpoints

On 07/31/2026 Retell removes GET /list-agents and GET /list-chat-agents. Migrate to the unified POST /v2/list-agents endpoint with filters.

## Legacy agent list endpoints are deprecated

**Deprecation date:** 07/31/2026

The following APIs are deprecated as of 07/31/2026. Migrate to the listed replacements.

**Affected APIs:**

* `GET /list-agents`
* `GET /list-chat-agents`

## Endpoint migrations

* `GET /list-agents` -> `POST /v2/list-agents`
* `GET /list-chat-agents` -> `POST /v2/list-agents`

## Migration details

* Update client calls to use `POST /v2/list-agents`.
* To list only voice agents, set `filter_criteria.channel` to `{ "type": "string", "op": "eq", "value": "voice" }`.
* To list only chat agents, set `filter_criteria.channel` to `{ "type": "string", "op": "eq", "value": "chat" }`.
* Read results from `items` instead of expecting a top-level array.
* Continue pagination with the returned `pagination_key` while `has_more` is `true`.
* Stop sending `pagination_key_version`; the new endpoint does not use it.
* Deprecation date: 07/31/2026.

The new endpoint returns one unified list for voice and chat agents. Use the `channel` filter to preserve the old voice-only or chat-only behavior, and update any array-based response handling to read from `items`.


# Multilingual agent locale array required
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/07-31_legacy_multilingual_setting

On 07/31/2026, the scalar "multi" value of the agent language field is removed in favor of an explicit locale array for multilingual Retell agents.

## Legacy multilingual setting is deprecated

The legacy scalar value `"multi"` of the agent `language` field is deprecated in favor of the explicit locale-array form (e.g. `["en-US","es-ES"]`). The array form is supported on the same `language` field and lets you pick the exact set of languages your agent should handle, which improves accuracy compared to the static 10-language `"multi"` set.

**Affected APIs:**

* [Create Agent](/api-references/create-agent)
* [Update Agent](/api-references/update-agent)
* [Create Chat Agent](/api-references/create-chat-agent)
* [Update Chat Agent](/api-references/update-chat-agent)

**What's changing on 07/31/2026:**

1. The scalar `"multi"` value of `language` will be rejected by the Create Agent, Update Agent, Create Chat Agent, and Update Chat Agent endpoints.
2. The dashboard's legacy **Multilingual** toggle will be removed.
3. Existing agents that still have `language: "multi"` will be **automatically migrated by Retell** to the equivalent locale array (`["en-US", "es-ES", "fr-FR", "de-DE", "hi-IN", "ru-RU", "pt-PT", "ja-JP", "it-IT", "nl-NL"]`). No action is required on your existing agents.

**Action required for API integrators:**

If your client code constructs agent payloads with `"language": "multi"`, update it to send the locale array form before 07/31/2026. After that date, requests using the scalar `"multi"` value will be rejected. For better accuracy, narrow the array down to the languages your agent actually needs — see the accuracy trade-offs in [Configure a multilingual agent](/agent/multilingual).

```json Before theme={"dark"}
{
  "language": "multi"
}
```

```json After theme={"dark"}
{
  "language": ["en-US", "es-ES", "fr-FR", "de-DE", "hi-IN", "ru-RU", "pt-PT", "ja-JP", "it-IT", "nl-NL"]
}
```

Also update any code that reads agent configurations and branches on `language === "multi"`, since after the automatic migration the field will return the array form instead.

**Effective date:** After 07/31/2026, agents created or updated with `language: "multi"` will be rejected. Existing agents are migrated automatically on or before this date.


# Update Call restricted to ended calls
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/08-31_update_call_ended_calls_only

Update Call becomes ended-calls-only on 08/31/2026; override_dynamic_variables and mid-call data_storage_setting changes move to Update Live Call.

## Update Call is moving to ended calls only

The [Update Call](/api-references/update-call) API (`PATCH /v2/update-call/{call_id}`) is changing to operate on **ended calls only**. As part of this change, the `override_dynamic_variables` input on Update Call is deprecated.

Previously, Update Call could change settings mid-call — for example, updating `data_storage_setting` would take effect on the ongoing call. After this change, updates you make through Update Call (including `data_storage_setting`) take effect only on **ended calls** and no longer affect ongoing calls. To override dynamic variables or change settings like `data_storage_setting` on an ongoing call, use the new [Update Live Call](/api-references/update-live-call) API (`PATCH /v2/update-live-call/{call_id}`).

**Affected APIs:**

* [Update Call](/api-references/update-call)

**Deprecated field:**

* `override_dynamic_variables` (on Update Call)

**Use instead:**

* For ongoing (live) calls: [Update Live Call](/api-references/update-live-call) (`PATCH /v2/update-live-call/{call_id}`). Dynamic variable overrides go under `fields_to_override.override_dynamic_variables`; the same request can also override `metadata` and `data_storage_setting`, and control the live agent via `call_control` (`trigger_response`, `additional_context`).
* For ended calls: continue using [Update Call](/api-references/update-call) to update `metadata`, `data_storage_setting`, and `custom_attributes`.

**What's changing on 08/31/2026:**

1. Update Call will only accept requests for calls that have already ended. Requests targeting ongoing calls will be rejected.
2. Updates you make through Update Call — including `data_storage_setting` — will take effect only on ended calls, not on ongoing calls.
3. The `override_dynamic_variables` input on Update Call will no longer be accepted.
4. To change settings on an ongoing call (dynamic variables, `data_storage_setting`, etc.), use the Update Live Call API instead.

**Migration:**

* If you call Update Call on an ongoing call to change dynamic variables, switch to [Update Live Call](/api-references/update-live-call) and move the values under `fields_to_override.override_dynamic_variables`.
* If you call Update Call on an ongoing call to change `data_storage_setting`, switch to [Update Live Call](/api-references/update-live-call); through Update Call, `data_storage_setting` takes effect only after the call ends.
* If you call Update Call on an ended call, no change is needed for `metadata`, `data_storage_setting`, or `custom_attributes`. Remove `override_dynamic_variables` from those requests — it has no effect on an ended call.

```json Before — PATCH /v2/update-call/{call_id} theme={"dark"}
{
  "override_dynamic_variables": { "additional_discount": "15%" }
}
```

```json After — PATCH /v2/update-live-call/{call_id} theme={"dark"}
{
  "fields_to_override": {
    "override_dynamic_variables": { "additional_discount": "15%" }
  }
}
```

**Effective date:** After 08/31/2026, Update Call will only work for ended calls and will no longer accept `override_dynamic_variables`. Use the [Update Live Call](/api-references/update-live-call) API (`PATCH /v2/update-live-call/{call_id}`) to update ongoing calls.

# Legacy browser JavaScript SDK
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/09-30_create_web_call_v2

Migrate from the deprecated Retell AI browser client SDK v2 to v3: replace RetellWebClient with RetellClient and update call creation and event handlers.

Version 2.x of the browser JavaScript SDK, `retell-client-js-sdk`, will be
deprecated on **October 18, 2026**. Upgrade to SDK 3.x and replace
`RetellWebClient` with `RetellClient` for call creation, audio, and event handling.
Existing integrations continue working during migration.

## Upgrade the browser SDK

Upgrade to the latest browser SDK:

```bash theme={"dark"}
npm install retell-client-js-sdk@latest
```

SDK 3.x retains `RetellWebClient` for compatibility. Upgrading the package alone
does not migrate your integration to `RetellClient`; update call creation and
event handlers as shown below.

## Replace call creation and connection

Replace the request to your server and `RetellWebClient.startCall()` with
`RetellClient.createWebCall()`. The SDK sends the v3 request and connects audio
automatically.

Create a [public key](/accounts/public-keys) and allow your website's domain
(`localhost` for local testing). Keep API keys on your server. If reCAPTCHA is
enabled for the public key, pass a fresh token as `recaptchaToken` with each call.

Add call controls to your page:

```html theme={"dark"}
<button id="start-call">Start call</button>
<button id="end-call">End call</button>
```

In your frontend JavaScript, replace the public key and agent ID with your own.
Load this code after the buttons exist, using your frontend's module bundler.

```javascript app.js theme={"dark"}
import { RetellClient } from "retell-client-js-sdk";

const client = new RetellClient({ key: "public_key_YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY" });
let call;

document.getElementById("start-call").addEventListener("click", () => {
  if (call && call.status !== "ended") return;

  call = client.createWebCall({
    agent_id: "agent_oBeDLoLOeuAbiuaMFXRtDOLriTJ5tSxD",
    hooks: {
      onStatus: (status) => console.log("Call status:", status),
      onEnd: () => console.log("Call ended"),
      onError: (error) => console.error("Call error:", error),
    },
  });
});

document.getElementById("end-call").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  await call?.end();
});
```

Serve the page over HTTPS or on `localhost`, click **Start call**, and allow
microphone access. Talk to the agent, then click **End call**. The session ends
and fires `onEnd`. See the [web call guide](/deploy/web-call) for audio controls
and live transcripts.

## Update event handlers

Calls created through v3 do not deliver every event from the previous connection
type. Audit handlers as well as call creation:

| Existing behavior | Migration |
| - | - |
| Call lifecycle handlers | Use `onStatus`, `onEnd`, and `onError`. Always reset the UI in `onEnd`, even when no error is reported. |
| `update` / `onUpdate` transcript updates | Enable `transcript: true` and use `onTranscript`. It receives merged transcript arrays; the old `turntaking` field is not supplied. |
| `node_transition` / `onNodeTransition` | With `RetellClient`, enable the transcript connection. Nodes from the initial snapshot also trigger the callback. |
| `agent_start_talking`, `agent_stop_talking`, or `isAgentTalking` | Use audio levels for visual activity estimates. Exact speaking boundaries and finalized-sentence events are not available. |
| `metadata` / `onMetadata` | No metadata event is delivered on the new connection. If you need the call's stored `metadata`, retrieve it with Get Call. |
| `audio` / `onAudio` | Set `audio.emitRawAudioSamples: true` for visualization snapshots. These are not a continuous audio stream. |

See the web call guide for [supported hooks](/deploy/web-call#handle-call-events),
[transcript authentication](/deploy/web-call#enable-live-transcripts), and
[audio options](/deploy/web-call#control-audio-during-the-call).

## Related endpoint change for server-created calls

As part of this migration, `POST /v2/create-web-call` will also be deprecated on
October 18, 2026 in favor of
[`POST /v3/create-web-call`](/api-references/create-web-call).
`RetellClient.createWebCall()` uses v3 automatically.

If you retain an existing server-created call flow, upgrade both your server
SDK and browser SDK. The server SDK's web-call creation method now uses v3 and
returns connection details instead of the full call object. If you make HTTP
requests directly, switch to `POST /v3/create-web-call` with the same JSON body.

Upgrade the browser SDK before switching the server to v3. For an existing
`RetellWebClient` integration on SDK 3.x, forward these fields to `startCall()`:

| API response field | `startCall()` option |
| - | - |
| `call_id` | `callId` |
| `access_token` | `accessToken` |
| `transport` | `transport` |
| `ice_servers` | `iceServers` |

Use [get call](/api-references/get-call) if your application needs call fields
such as `call_status`, `agent_id`, or `metadata` after creation.


# Legacy monthly billing
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/09-30_legacy_billing

Legacy monthly billing on Retell AI moves to prepaid credits on 09/30/2026. The workspace switches when you click Switch now and add credits.

## Monthly billing switches to credits on 09/30/2026

On **September 30, 2026**, workspaces still on monthly billing move to [credit-based billing](/accounts/billing). Click **Switch now** on the Billing page and add credits to switch yourself. If you don't, Retell moves the workspace that day and the credit balance starts at **\$0**. Calls, chat, and other usage then come out of those credits instead of a bill at the end of the month. You can't switch back.

If you already see **Credits Balance**, you're already on the new billing.

Enterprise workspaces stay on monthly invoicing. You won't see **Switch now**.

## What changes

* Calls, chat, and other usage come out of your credits as you use them. If the balance hits zero, that usage stops until you [buy more credits](/accounts/billing) or turn on auto recharge.
* You get one last bill for what you've used so far. It's charged to your card.
* Any credit already on your workspace is added to the new balance, after that last bill.
* You need a card saved. The credits you add, and that last bill, are both charged to it. Add a card under [payment methods](/accounts/add-payment) before you switch.

## What still bills monthly

These stay on your card. They are not paid with credits:

* Phone numbers [purchased through Retell](/deploy/purchase-number)
* [Concurrency](/deploy/concurrency)
* Knowledge base hosting beyond the free tier
* Calls per second (CPS)
* SMS subscriptions

A percent-off discount on your current subscription carries over.

You don't need to change your agents or phone setup.

## Switch to credit-based billing

Do this on each [workspace](/accounts/workspace) that is still on monthly billing.

**1. Open the Billing page**

Go to **Billing**. If you're on monthly billing, you won't see **Credits Balance**. You'll see a notice to switch.

![Billing notice saying you'll switch to credit-based billing on September 30, 2026, with Switch now and Learn what changes](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/d-UO6p2cCiO6V5N2/images/billing-page/billing-credit-switch-notice.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=d-UO6p2cCiO6V5N2\&q=85\&s=ba8626e73aaed8980c3d727f95232abf)

The Billing page notice: this workspace switches to credit-based billing on September 30, 2026.

If **Switch now** is grayed out, ask an admin on your team. See [Access control](/accounts/access-control).

**2. Add a card if you don't have one**

**Switch now** asks you to add a card first. See [Add payment methods](/accounts/add-payment).

**3. Choose how many credits to add**

Pick **\$10**, **\$50**, or **\$100**, or type your own amount from **\$10** to **\$10,000**.

![Switch to credit-based billing dialog with \$50 selected, options for \$10 and \$100, a custom amount of \$50, and a Switch now button](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/d-UO6p2cCiO6V5N2/images/billing-page/billing-switch-starting-credits.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=d-UO6p2cCiO6V5N2\&q=85\&s=d1cc983c21d8fedc42e84dc0b84de24f)

Starting credits: $10, $50, or \$100, or your own amount, then Switch now.

**4. Confirm the switch**

Click **Switch now**.

> [!TIP]
>
> You see **Credits Balance**, with **Buy credits** and **Auto recharge**.

![Billing page showing a Credits Balance of \$21.60 with Budget settings, Auto recharge, and Buy credits actions above the Invoices, Credits purchased, and Usage tabs](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/JHgpRoh9hcAz6D7s/images/billing-page/billing-credit-overview.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=JHgpRoh9hcAz6D7s\&q=85\&s=a720838a107fe3f40ff789ff979d3f46)

After the switch, the Billing page shows Credits Balance, Buy credits, and Auto recharge.

**5. Turn on auto recharge**

This buys more credits for you when the balance gets low, so usage doesn't stop. Set **When credits drop below** and **Bring credits back to**, then click **Save**.

![Auto Recharge Setting with the toggle on, When credits drop below set to \$10, and Bring credits back to set to \$100](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/a1LftRqc_k-5TDA7/images/billing-page/billing-auto-recharge.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=a1LftRqc_k-5TDA7\&q=85\&s=9eb18e850f7d4767931bdb6366a97510)

Auto recharge on: top up when the balance drops below $10, and restore it to $100.

See [Set up auto recharge](/accounts/billing#set-up-auto-recharge).

> [!WARNING]
>
> You can't switch back. Credits don't expire, and they can't be refunded. Add a card before September 30 so the last bill can be charged.

If the Billing page says something on your workspace can't be moved yet, email [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com) before September 30.

## FAQ

> [accordion] Why do I have to leave monthly billing?
>
> Monthly billing ends on September 30, 2026. After that, calls, chat, and other usage come out of credits instead of a bill at the end of the month. If you don't click **Switch now**, Retell moves the workspace that day and the credit balance starts at **\$0**. [Auto recharge](/accounts/billing#set-up-auto-recharge) can refill the balance so usage doesn't stop. Enterprise workspaces stay on monthly invoicing.

> [accordion] Can the September 30 date be moved?
>
> No. September 30, 2026 stays the date so billing lines up with the 1st of the month.

> [accordion] When does my workspace switch?
>
> The workspace switches when you click **Switch now** and add credits. If you don't click **Switch now**, it switches on September 30, 2026, and the credit balance starts at **\$0**. Calls, chat, and other usage stop until you add credits or turn on [auto recharge](/accounts/billing#set-up-auto-recharge).

> [accordion] Can I switch back to monthly billing?
>
> No. After you click **Switch now** and add credits, you stay on credit-based billing.

> [accordion] What about charges from this month?
>
> You get one last bill for what you've used up to the switch, charged to your card. After that, calls, chat, and other usage come out of your credits.

> [accordion] Will my phone numbers and discount stay?
>
> Yes. Phone numbers and your other monthly fees stay on your card. A percent discount stays too. Calls, chat, and other usage move to credits.

> [accordion] Do I need to change anything in my setup?
>
> No. Your agents and phone numbers keep working. You only change how you pay, on the Billing page.

> [accordion] I'm on an enterprise plan. Does this apply to me?
>
> No. Enterprise workspaces stay on monthly invoicing. **Switch now** is only for workspaces on monthly billing.

> [accordion] My card was charged, but the switch didn't finish. Will I be charged again?
>
> Email [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com).

For how credits, auto recharge, and invoices work after the switch, see [Billing](/accounts/billing).


# Legacy SIP endpoint removed
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/09-30_sip_legacy_endpoint

Retell retires SIP endpoint sip:5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud on 09/30/2026; migrate elastic trunks and dial-to-sip integrations to sip:sip.retellai.com.

## The legacy SIP endpoint is being removed

**Removal date:** 09/30/2026

> [!NOTE]
>
> Migrate from `sip:5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud` to `sip:sip.retellai.com`.

The legacy SIP endpoint `sip:5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud` has been deprecated since November 2025 and will be retired on 09/30/2026. Route your inbound calls to the supported Retell SIP server `sip:sip.retellai.com` instead. See the [Connect to custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony) guide for setup.

After 09/30/2026, calls sent to `sip:5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud` may no longer connect.

## Who is affected

Only integrations that dial or route directly to the hardcoded `5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud` host. If your trunk or code already targets `sip.retellai.com`, no change is needed.

## Migration

* **Elastic SIP trunking:** update the SIP server URI/Origination URI on your trunk from `sip:5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud` to `sip:sip.retellai.com`. If you pin a transport, keep it on the new host: `sip:sip.retellai.com;transport=tls` (also `;transport=tcp` or `;transport=udp`).
* **Dial to SIP URI:** dial each call to `sip:{call_id}@sip.retellai.com`, replacing `{call_id}` with the `call_id` returned by [Register Phone Call](/api-references/register-phone-call) — previously `sip:{call_id}@5t4n6j0wnrl.sip.livekit.cloud`.
* **Allowlist Retell's IP ranges:** make sure your firewall permits Retell's SIP CIDR blocks, listed in the [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony) guide. Many providers require this before they accept traffic to the new host.
* **TLS / mTLS:** `sip.retellai.com` presents Retell's server certificate; if you pin a root CA or use mTLS, follow the [Security center](/deploy/custom-telephony#security-center) section.

No other part of your Retell configuration changes — only the SIP hostname you route to.

# Cal.com built-in tools
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/10-31_legacy_calcom_tools

Retell's built-in Cal.com tools are gone from the dashboard, frozen by the API on 09/30/2026, and migrated to the Cal.com integration on 10/31/2026.

## The Cal.com integration replaces the built-in Cal.com tools

The built-in Cal.com tool types `check_availability_cal` and `book_appointment_cal` are deprecated in favor of the [Cal.com integration](/integrations/cal-com). This lands in three stages: the dashboard no longer offers these tools, the API stops accepting them on **09/30/2026**, and on **10/31/2026** Retell migrates the tools you already have to the integration.

Each built-in tool carries its own `cal_api_key`, so a workspace with ten booking agents holds ten copies of the same key, and rotating that key means editing all ten tools. The integration stores credentials per workspace connection, supports OAuth on **cal.com** or API keys on **cal.com** and **cal.eu**, and adds booking lookup, reschedule, and cancel on top of availability and booking. The automatic migration below reuses the built-in tools' API keys; it doesn't convert them to OAuth.

**Affected APIs:**

* [Create Retell LLM](/api-references/create-retell-llm), [Update Retell LLM](/api-references/update-retell-llm) — fields: `general_tools`, `states[].tools`
* [Create Conversation Flow](/api-references/create-conversation-flow), [Update Conversation Flow](/api-references/update-conversation-flow) — field: `tools` (flow-level and on `type: "subagent"` nodes)
* [Create Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/create-conversation-flow-component), [Update Conversation Flow Component](/api-references/update-conversation-flow-component) — field: `tools`

**Deprecated tool types:**

* `check_availability_cal` — fields `cal_api_key`, `event_type_id`, `timezone`
* `book_appointment_cal` — fields `cal_api_key`, `event_type_id`, `timezone`

**Use instead:** [connect Cal.com](/integrations/cal-com) once for the workspace, then add its [agent functions](/integrations/cal-com-functions) to each agent.

| Built-in tool | Integration replacement |
| - | - |
| `check_availability_cal` | **Check Availability** (`check_calcom_availability`) |
| `book_appointment_cal` | **Book Appointment** (`book_calcom_appointment`) |
| No equivalent | **List Bookings**, **Get Booking**, **Reschedule Booking**, **Cancel Booking** |

**What changed on 08/23/2026:**

1. The dashboard's function menu no longer offers **Check Calendar Availability** or **Book Appointment**, so you can't add one to an agent from the dashboard.
2. The API still creates and updates built-in Cal.com tools until 09/30/2026.

**What's changing on 09/30/2026:**

1. The API stops accepting `check_availability_cal` and `book_appointment_cal` on both create and update. Requests that add one of these tools, or change one you already have, fail.
2. Existing tools keep running unchanged until the migration, but no surface can edit them any more, since the dashboard writes through those same endpoints. **09/30/2026 is your last day to change a built-in tool's API key, event type ID, or timezone.**

**What's changing on 10/31/2026:**

1. Retell migrates existing built-in Cal.com tools to the integration. One connection covers each distinct API key: tools that share a key all point at the same connection, and a key you've already connected reuses that connection instead of getting a duplicate. Any connection the migration creates shows up on the **Connected** tab of the dashboard's Integrations page.
2. Migrated tools keep their current function name, so prompt text that calls the function by name (for example, "call the `check_calendar_availability` function") keeps working. The event type ID and timezone carry over.
3. **Tools that can't be migrated are skipped and stop working.** A tool is skipped when Cal.com rejects its key at migration time, because the key expired or was revoked. A skipped tool fails mid-call, the first time the agent tries to check availability or book.
4. API responses stop returning `check_availability_cal` and `book_appointment_cal`. Read a migrated agent back and you'll get the integration's tools instead, so client code that keys off the old tool types needs updating.

> [!WARNING]
>
> If your Cal.com key expires before 10/31/2026, replace it on the built-in tool before 09/30/2026, the last day an edit is accepted. After that the only fix is migrating the agent to the integration by hand.

**Migration:**

1. Find the agents still on the built-in tools. On the dashboard, check each agent's **Functions** section for **Check Calendar Availability** or **Book Appointment**. Through the API, call [Get Retell LLM](/api-references/get-retell-llm) or [Get Conversation Flow](/api-references/get-conversation-flow) and look for tools with `type` set to `check_availability_cal` or `book_appointment_cal`.
2. [Connect Cal.com](/integrations/cal-com) on the dashboard's **Integrations** page. Create the API key with **Never expires** turned on, and set **Domain** to `Cal.com`, the instance the built-in tools used. Pick `Cal.eu` only if your account has since moved to Cal.com's EU instance.
3. On each agent, add the integration's **Check Availability** and **Book Appointment** tools and give them the same [event type ID](/integrations/cal-com-functions#find-an-event-type-id) the built-in tool used.
4. Delete the built-in tool. If your prompt names the old function, update it to the new tool's name.
5. Test the agent before you ship it. [Simulation testing](/test/llm-simulation-testing) can mock the booking tools so you don't create real bookings.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can create the connection through the API: [Create App](/api-references/create-app) takes the Cal.com API key in `auth_config` and the instance in `tenant_url` (`cal.com` or `cal.eu`). Adding the resulting tools to an agent is dashboard-only (as of August 2026), so an agent built entirely through the API still needs one dashboard pass.

**Effective dates:** The dashboard stopped offering the built-in Cal.com tools on 08/23/2026. The API stops creating and updating them on 09/30/2026, after which existing tools keep running but can no longer be edited. On 10/31/2026 Retell migrates them to the [Cal.com integration](/integrations/cal-com).

# Multi-prompt agents
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/2026/12-15_multi_prompt_agents

Migrate multi-prompt agents to conversation flow in Retell AI. Creation ends on 12/15/2026 and editing ends on 02/01/2027; review and switch your traffic.

## Conversation flow replaces multi-prompt agents

Retell is retiring multi-prompt agents in favor of [conversation flow](/build/conversation-flow/overview). New multi-prompt creation ends on **12/15/2026**, and editing ends on **02/01/2027**. Single prompt and conversation flow agents aren't affected.

## What's changing

* **Already in effect:** The dashboard no longer offers new multi-prompt agents or lets you assign them to new phone numbers. [Update Retell LLM](/api-references/update-retell-llm) also rejects adding the first state to a single prompt LLM. Existing phone assignments keep working.
* **12/15/2026:** New multi-prompt creation ends, including through the API, dashboard duplication, and import.
* **02/01/2027:** Editing existing multi-prompt agents ends.

Existing multi-prompt agents continue handling calls during migration. Retell will migrate remaining multi-prompt agents to conversation flow after editing ends.

## Migrate your agents

Delete any multi-prompt agents you no longer need. For agents you still use, follow the steps below.

**1. Create or open the conversation flow copy**

Find **Multi-Prompt** agents in the **Agents** list and open an agent, then choose **Convert to conversation flow** in its deprecation banner. Retell builds a separate conversation flow agent named `<agent name> (Conversation Flow)` with a new agent ID, then opens it. Your source agent and its phone-number assignments stay unchanged.

The conversion maps each state to a node and carries over your tools, settings, tags, and dynamic variables. If something can't carry over cleanly — for example a voice the converted model doesn't support — the conversion flags it as a warning to review.

If **Open converted agent** appears, open that copy instead of converting again.

**2. Review and test**

Review the generated flow and tools, then test with the [LLM playground](/test/llm-playground) or [simulation testing](/test/llm-simulation-testing). Conversion can change how the agent handles calls.

**3. Switch your phone numbers**

Existing phone assignments continue using the original agent until you switch them. After testing, open the assigned number in **Phone Numbers** and choose **Switch to converted agent** when available, or assign the new agent manually. Review the selected agent version after switching.

**4. Update integrations**

Update code, batch calls, and transfers that use the old agent ID. If your integration creates or edits multi-prompt Retell LLMs, move those operations to the conversation flow APIs, such as [Create Conversation Flow](/api-references/create-conversation-flow) and [Update Conversation Flow](/api-references/update-conversation-flow), before the relevant cutoff.

Automatic migration does not update your integration code.

# Compliance checks
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/dialer/compliance-checks

DNC scrubbing for AI outbound calls with Retell AI: screen campaign contacts against federal and state do-not-call registries, TCPA litigators, and line type.

Before a [Dialer](/dialer/overview) campaign dials anyone, Retell screens each contact with the compliance checks you choose: your internal DNC list, the federal and state do-not-call registries, known TCPA litigators, reassigned numbers, and landline or VoIP line types. A contact that fails a check is never dialed in that campaign, and the campaign shows which check it failed.

You choose the checks for each campaign, and they lock at launch.

## What each check catches

In the campaign's **Contacts** tab, [choose your contacts](/dialer/contacts) and click **Continue**. The next screen, **Contacts - screening**, lists the checks. When you create a campaign in the dashboard, only **Retell Contacts DNC** is on. A campaign created through the API has no checks unless you set them.

![Contacts - screening screen. Under DNC / TCPA check, Retell Contacts DNC is on; Federal DNC Check is on with the FTC Org ID and Subscription Account Number (SAN) fields filled in, a Register link, and a green Verified tag; State DNC Check is off; Reassigned Number Database Check is on with a Consent lookback period of 30 days; Litigator List Check is on. Under Opt out specific line type, Landline and VoIP are on.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-compliance-checks.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=5ef536d2f2231c7783b6c6e218b97188)

The Contacts - screening screen with Federal DNC Check on and a verified SAN.

| Check | What it catches | Default | Needs FTC registration | Label on a failed contact |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| **Retell Contacts DNC** (internal DNC) | Contacts marked do-not-call in your workspace [Contacts](/features/contacts) | On | No | Marked Do Not Call in Retell |
| **Federal DNC Check** | Numbers on the FTC National Do Not Call Registry | Off | Yes | On the federal Do Not Call registry |
| **State DNC Check** | Numbers on a state's own do-not-call registry | Off | Yes | On a state Do Not Call registry |
| **Reassigned Number Database Check** | Numbers that changed owners within the **Consent lookback period** | Off (lookback 30 days) | No | Reassigned number |
| **Litigator List Check** | Numbers tied to serial litigators who sue businesses under consumer-protection laws (TCPA, FDCPA, FCRA, and similar) | Off | No | History of TCPA lawsuits |
| **Landline** | Landline numbers | Off | No | Landline number |
| **VoIP** | VoIP numbers | Off | No | VoIP number |

**Reassigned Number Database Check** checks the Reassigned Numbers Database for numbers reassigned within the **Consent lookback period**, counted back from the day the check runs. A number reassigned before that period isn't caught, so set the period to reach back to when you collected consent. It takes a whole number of days, 0 or greater.

The line-type checks skip only landline and VoIP numbers. You can't filter out mobile numbers.

If the screening provider can't tell whether a number matches a check, for example a line type it can't identify, the number passes that check. A check is a screen, not a guarantee.

Screening is billed per number checked. The **Cost estimates** panel on the **Contacts - screening** screen shows the estimate. Retell Contacts DNC alone is free, and Auto-enroll contacts are billed as they're checked.

## Set up your FTC registration

Federal DNC and state DNC run under your own FTC National Do Not Call Registry account, so Retell needs your FTC Org ID and Subscription Account Number (SAN). A campaign with either check on can't launch until the FTC verifies them. Until then, launch shows "This campaign can't launch until the FTC verifies your SAN."

**1. Get an Org ID and SAN from the FTC**

If you don't have them, register at [telemarketing.donotcall.gov](https://telemarketing.donotcall.gov/). The **Register** link next to the SAN field opens the same site. Subscribe to every area code you plan to call.

**2. Enter them in Retell**

Go to **Settings → Compliance**. In **Federal and State DNC Checks**, enter the **FTC Org ID** and **Subscription Account Number (SAN)**, then click **Confirm**. The same fields also appear on the **Contacts - screening** screen when you turn on Federal DNC Check or State DNC Check.

**3. Wait for the FTC to verify**

Click **Confirm** in the **Verify the DNC with the FTC** dialog. The dashboard says the process "may take up to 1 hour", and you can leave the page while it runs. The SAN field shows **Pending**, then **Verified** once the FTC accepts it. If it's still **Pending** after an hour, check back later instead of submitting again.

![Federal and State DNC Checks card explaining that federal and state checks run under your FTC National Do Not Call Registry account and that campaigns using either check launch only after the FTC verifies the Org ID and SAN. The FTC Org ID field holds 12345678-12345, and the Subscription Account Number (SAN) field holds 12345678-123456-78 with a green Verified tag and a Register link above it.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-compliance-settings.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=8ec71153aada9926e539cf233021bf5c)

The Federal and State DNC Checks card on Settings → Compliance, with a verified SAN.

If the FTC rejects the values, the SAN field shows the FTC's message or "The FTC could not verify this number. Check it and submit again." Correct the values and click **Confirm** again.

If a verified SAN expires, the field shows the expiry date. Renew your subscription with the FTC. Retell checks an expired SAN again when it's used, so the field returns to **Verified** once the FTC renews it. Until then, campaigns with federal or state DNC on can't launch. If your renewal comes with a new SAN, enter it and click **Confirm**.

### Area codes your SAN covers

Your SAN covers only the area codes you subscribed to with the FTC. Retell can't check a contact in any other area code against the registries, so that contact fails as **Area code not covered by your SAN**. The dashboard doesn't show which area codes your SAN covers, so confirm your subscription with the FTC before you launch.

### Change your SAN

To replace a verified SAN, hover over the SAN field, click the **X**, and click **Change SAN**. The dialog warns: "Changing your SAN turns off federal and state DNC checks until the FTC verifies the new value. Until then, running campaigns that use these checks fail their new contacts." In an Auto-enroll campaign, that's every contact that enrolls before the new SAN is verified. A failed contact is never checked again, so change the SAN when no running campaign with these checks is enrolling contacts.

### Who can edit the registration

Anyone who can edit phone numbers, such as Admins and Developers, can edit the FTC registration (see [access control](/accounts/access-control)). Members see it read-only, with "Ask someone who can edit phone numbers to add your FTC registration."

## When checks run

* **At launch.** Standard and Auto-enroll campaigns both check every contact when you launch. A scheduled campaign checks its contacts when you schedule it, not at its start time.
* **When a contact joins an Auto-enroll campaign.** Retell checks a contact that enrolls after launch, usually within about 5 minutes.
* **Before each call or SMS attempt, for internal DNC only.** If a contact is marked do-not-call after it passed, Retell stops it before the next attempt. Its stage becomes **Failed** with the reason **Marked Do Not Call in Retell**. A call already queued, or the second dial of a [double dial](/dialer/sequences#double-dial), isn't rechecked. The other checks don't run again, so federal and state DNC results stay as they were at launch for the life of the campaign.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Federal DNC, state DNC, TCPA, reassigned-number, and line-type results are a snapshot from the moment Retell checked the contact. Retell doesn't refresh them. For a scheduled campaign, that moment is when you schedule it, so results can be days or weeks old at the first call. The same applies to later attempts after long delays, to campaigns paused for a while, and to Auto-enroll contacts that enroll while a campaign is scheduled or paused. To screen against current registry data, launch close to the start time, or [duplicate the campaign](/dialer/overview#pause-stop-duplicate-or-delete) and launch the copy. Ask your legal counsel how recent your registry data must be.

While checks run, the contact's stage is **Validating**. Retell never dials a contact before its checks finish. If the screening provider is unavailable, the contact stays **Validating** and Retell retries it about every 10 minutes. After 24 hours from enrollment, it fails as **Validation timed out**.

A contact that fails a check gets the stage **Enroll failed**. On the campaign's **Contacts** tab, hover over the stage or open the contact to see the reason. The failure is final: Retell never retries the contact in that campaign. The contact stays in your workspace Contacts.

Each failed contact shows one reason, the first match in this order: internal DNC, federal DNC, area code not covered by your SAN, state DNC, landline, VoIP, TCPA, RND.

To use different checks after launch, [duplicate the campaign](/dialer/overview#pause-stop-duplicate-or-delete) and launch the copy.

## Which numbers are checked?

Retell Contacts DNC applies to every number. As of October 2026, the other checks run only on valid US and Canadian numbers (+1). Other numbers, including numbers in other +1 regions such as Puerto Rico and Jamaica, skip those checks and enroll as if they passed.

Federal DNC and State DNC check US registries only. Retell doesn't check Canada's National Do Not Call List (DNCL), so screen Canadian contacts against it yourself before you add them to a campaign.

## Do-not-call requests during a campaign

Compliance checks screen contacts before the first dial. During the campaign, a contact can still ask you to stop:

* **On a call**, the agent's [Do-not-contact Handling](/build/do-not-call) confirms the request and ends the call. With Retell Contacts DNC on, Retell turns on Do-not-contact Handling for the campaign's calls, even if the agent has it off.
* **By SMS**, the contact replies to a campaign message with an [opt-out keyword](/build/do-not-call#sms-opt-out-keywords) such as `STOP`.

Either way, Retell marks the workspace contact do-not-call, and the contact gets the **Do Not Call** outcome, which ends its [sequence](/dialer/sequences). If the contact replies `STOP` after the SMS chat has closed, Retell still marks the contact, but the sequence stops only at its next attempt, and only if Retell Contacts DNC is on. The mark is workspace-wide, so every campaign with Retell Contacts DNC on skips the contact from then on.

## What stays your responsibility

Compliance checks skip numbers you shouldn't call. They don't establish that you may call the rest.

* **Consent.** Retell doesn't verify that you have consent to call a contact. Before launch, you check a box that reads: "I confirm this campaign respects all applicable legal and consent requirements for the contacts being dialed, including TCPA, state DNC laws, and any opt-in obligations."
* **Calling hours.** Retell doesn't enforce TCPA calling hours. It dials only inside the calling window you set on the [sequence](/dialer/sequences), in the time zone the sequence picks for each contact. With **Contact's local time**, that's the time zone of the area code of a US or Canadian number, which may not match where the person is. Other numbers use the fallback time zone. Set a window that meets the calling-hour rules for your contacts. A callback that a contact requests for a specific time goes out at that time, even outside the window.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page describes what Retell checks. It isn't legal advice. Confirm which rules apply to your campaigns with your legal counsel.

## FAQ

> [accordion] Does Retell scrub against the national DNC registry?
>
> Yes. Turn on **Federal DNC Check** for the campaign. Retell checks contacts against the FTC National Do Not Call Registry under your own [FTC registration](#set-up-your-ftc-registration) and never dials a match. **State DNC Check** does the same for state registries.

> [accordion] Do I need my own SAN?
>
> Yes, for federal DNC and state DNC. Retell runs those checks under your FTC Org ID and SAN, and a campaign that uses them can't launch until the FTC verifies the SAN. Retell Contacts DNC, Reassigned Number Database Check, Litigator List Check, and the line-type checks don't need one.

> [accordion] What happens to contacts that fail a check?
>
> They get the stage **Enroll failed** and a reason, such as **On the federal Do Not Call registry**, on the campaign's **Contacts** tab. Retell never dials them in that campaign and never checks them again. They stay in your workspace Contacts.

> [accordion] Can Retell filter out mobile numbers?
>
> No. The line-type checks skip only landline and VoIP numbers.

> [accordion] Does Retell check that I have consent to call a contact?
>
> No. Consent is your responsibility. **Reassigned Number Database Check** skips numbers that changed owners within the consent lookback period, but it doesn't confirm consent.

> [accordion] If one agent marks a contact do-not-call, do other campaigns skip it?
>
> Yes, if they have Retell Contacts DNC on. The mark is on the workspace contact, not the agent or the campaign, so running campaigns skip the contact before their next dial too.

Related: [Dialer overview](/dialer/overview), [choose contacts](/dialer/contacts), [build a sequence](/dialer/sequences), [do-not-call requests](/build/do-not-call), and [Contacts](/features/contacts).


# Choose contacts
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/dialer/contacts

Upload a call list CSV or auto-enroll contacts into an outbound campaign with Retell AI: filter contacts, map file columns, and call new matches automatically.

A Standard campaign calls a fixed list: contacts you select with a filter, or a CSV or XLSX file you upload. An Auto-enroll campaign calls every contact that matches your conditions at launch, and every contact that comes to match them later.

You choose contacts on the campaign's **Contacts** tab. You pick the campaign type when you create the campaign (see [Standard and Auto-enroll campaigns](/dialer/overview#standard-and-auto-enroll-campaigns)). After you choose contacts, click **Continue** to set up the [compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks) that screen each contact before its first dial.

Every campaign contact is a record in your workspace [Contacts](/features/contacts), keyed by phone number.

## Standard campaigns

A Standard campaign gets its contacts in one of two ways, never both:

* **Filter** the contacts already in your workspace.
* **Upload** one CSV or XLSX file. The upload adds the file's rows to your workspace Contacts, and the campaign calls exactly those contacts.

**Upload CSV or XLSX** is hidden while a filter exists. To switch from a filter to a file, open **Filter contacts**, remove every row, and click **Continue**.

### Filter your contacts

**1. Open the filter**

On the **Contacts** tab, click **Filter contacts**.

**2. Add conditions**

In each row, pick a field, an operator, and a value. Click **Add filter** for another row. A contact must match every row.

**3. Apply**

Click **Continue**. The table lists every matching contact, 20 per page.

![Contacts tab of a Standard campaign with the description that contacts matching your filters are included by default and you can uncheck any you don't want to dial. A Filter contacts button sits at the top right. The table lists checked rows with columns Phone, Name, Contact ID, Related Conversations, Latest Conversation, External ID, and a Company custom field.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-contacts-standard.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=f79b67bcac06987987eea11459d7924b)

A Standard campaign's Contacts tab, listing the contacts that match its filter.

You can filter on these fields:

| Field | Operators | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| **Phone number** | equals, does not equal, contains, starts with, ends with | Numbers are stored in E.164 format. To match an area code, use **starts with** `+1415`, not `415` or `(415)`. |
| **Do not call** | equals `true` or `false` | A contact with no value counts as `false`. |
| **Tags** | is any of | Listed once your workspace has tags. |
| Text custom fields | equals, does not equal, contains, starts with, ends with | |
| Number custom fields | equals, does not equal, greater than, greater than or equal, less than, less than or equal | |
| Boolean custom fields | equals `true` or `false` | |
| Selector custom fields | is any of | |

Conditions follow these rules:

* **All conditions must match.** There's no OR between rows. To accept several values of one field, use **is any of** on a Tags or Selector field.
* **Text matching is case-sensitive.** `Mission` doesn't match `mission`.
* **A missing value never matches.** A contact with no value in a field fails every condition on that field, including **does not equal**. **Do not call** is the exception.
* **Some fields aren't available.** You can't filter on first name, last name, or Date and Datetime fields.
* **Phone number, Do not call, and Tags take one row each.** A custom field can take several rows, for example `balance_due` greater than `100` and less than `500`.

[Auto-enroll campaigns](#auto-enroll-campaigns) use the same conditions.

### Upload a CSV or XLSX file

**1. Pick the file**

On the **Contacts** tab, click **Upload CSV or XLSX** and choose a file. If a workbook has more than one sheet, select the worksheet to import. The preview shows the row count. Click **Continue**.

**2. Map the columns**

Select the columns to import and map each one to a contact field. A column whose header matches a field name, such as `first_name`, maps automatically. Map exactly one column to **Phone Number**. To store a column that has no field yet, create one from the mapping list.

**3. Set the default country**

Under **Phone number formatting**, choose the country for numbers that don't include a country code. It defaults to the United States.

**4. Confirm**

Click **Confirm**. The dashboard checks every value first. If one doesn't fit its field, you see "Invalid value · Row N" with the column and the expected format. Fix the file, map the column to another field, or unselect it. Then the import runs, and the table fills in when it finishes.

The file must meet these requirements (as of October 2026):

| Requirement | Value |
| - | - |
| File type | `.csv` or `.xlsx` |
| File size | Up to 50 MB |
| Rows | Up to 50,000 data rows. The dashboard doesn't count rows up front. A larger file fails after you confirm, with "1 contact failed to import", and nothing imports. |
| Header | The first row holds the column names. Each selected column needs a unique name. |
| Phone number | Exactly one column, mapped to **Phone Number**. A row whose phone number is missing or can't be read doesn't import. Extensions such as `x123` are dropped. |
| Mapped columns | Up to 200 |

Each value must match the type of the contact field it maps to:

| Contact field type | Accepted values |
| - | - |
| Text | Any text |
| Number | A number, such as `42` or `19.99` |
| Boolean, including **Do Not Call** | `true`, `false`, `1`, or `0`, in any case |
| Date or Datetime | `2026-11-12`, `11/12/2026`, `2026/11/12`, or an ISO 8601 timestamp such as `2026-11-12T15:30:00Z` |
| Selector | Exactly one of the field's options, with the same capitalization |

An empty cell, or one that reads `null`, is skipped. Retell checks the values again when it runs the import. A row that fails that check is skipped, and the result banner counts it as failed.

Here's a short file for a dental reminder campaign. The last two rows show phone numbers without a country code, which the default country fills in:

```csv theme={"dark"}
phone_number,first_name,last_name,clinic,balance_due
+14155550101,Ada,Lovelace,Mission,0
(415) 555-0102,Alan,Turing,Sunset,45.50
4155550103,Grace,Hopper,Mission,120
```

With `clinic` mapped to a Text field, the agent's prompt can say `Hi {{first_name}}, this is Bright Smile Dental at our {{clinic}} office.` See [Use contact fields in the agent's prompt](#use-contact-fields-in-the-agents-prompt).

#### What the upload changes in your Contacts

The upload is a normal [contact import](/features/contacts#import-from-csv-or-xlsx), so it writes to your workspace Contacts:

* **Rows match by phone number.** A number that already has a contact updates that contact. A new number creates one. Numbers are formatted first, so `(415) 555-0102` and `+14155550102` are the same contact.
* **Blank cells don't clear values.** An existing contact keeps any value your file leaves empty, and any field you don't map.
* **Do Not Call can be set but not cleared.** `true` marks the contact as [do-not-call](/build/do-not-call). `false` never removes an existing mark. Clear it on the [Contacts](/features/contacts) page instead.
* **The contacts stay.** Replacing the file or deleting the campaign doesn't remove contacts that an upload created or updated.
* **Each upload adds a hidden tag.** Retell tags every contact in the file with a new tag that the dashboard doesn't show, and the campaign filters on it. A workspace can hold up to 1,000 contact tags, so heavy re-uploading can reach the limit.
* **Running Auto-enroll campaigns see the changes.** An uploaded contact that matches an Auto-enroll campaign's conditions enrolls in that campaign too. See [When contacts enroll](#when-contacts-enroll).

Only one contact import runs at a time per workspace. If another is running, wait for it to finish.

Uploading needs CRM write access, the permission to edit workspace Contacts. Admins and Developers have it. Members don't, and a custom role has it only if it includes CRM write permission. **Upload CSV or XLSX** is disabled without it, with "You need CRM write access to do this." To get it, ask an Admin to change your role:

1. Go to **Settings** → **Workspace** → **Users**.
2. Open the menu on your row and click **Edit Roles**.
3. Pick **Developer**, **Admin**, or a custom role with CRM write permission.

See [access control](/accounts/access-control) for what each role can do.

To use a different file, click **Edit upload** and replace it. Replacing the file restores any rows you excluded. To go back to a filter, remove the file in **Edit upload**.

### Exclude contacts

Every matching contact is included by default. To leave one out, uncheck its row. There's no select-all, so to drop many contacts, narrow the filter or the file instead. Click **Restore excluded** to bring every excluded contact back.

### When the list is fixed

Until launch, the list is a live filter. Contacts that are created or updated to match appear in the table, and the count changes.

At launch, Retell takes a snapshot. Every contact that matches at that moment, minus the ones you excluded, enrolls in the campaign. For a scheduled campaign, the snapshot happens when you launch, not at the start time. Contacts that match later never join a Standard campaign. To keep adding contacts, use an [Auto-enroll campaign](#auto-enroll-campaigns).

Each phone number enrolls once. A number that appears in several rows of your file is one contact, so it's called once, and the later row's values win. If the earlier row had a value that the later row leaves blank, whether it survives depends on where the rows fall in the file. Keep one row per number so you know which values the agent gets.

A campaign can hold up to 100,000 contacts (as of October 2026). Launch stops with one of these messages:

| Message | What to do |
| - | - |
| "Choose contacts before launching this campaign." | Add a filter or upload a file. |
| "Add contacts before launching this campaign." | Change the filter or file. It matches no contacts. |
| "The campaign exceeds the 100,000 contact limit." | Narrow the filter, or split the list across two campaigns. |

## Auto-enroll campaigns

An Auto-enroll campaign's **Contacts** tab opens **Setup Trigger**, which has three parts:

* **When to enroll**: contacts enroll automatically when they're created or updated.
* **Who to enroll**: your conditions. Click **Add filter** to add a row. They work exactly like the [Standard campaign filter](#filter-your-contacts).
* **Enrollment**: a live count, such as "1,240 contacts match right now." That's how many contacts would enroll if you launched now, before compliance checks.

An Auto-enroll campaign needs at least one condition to launch.

![Setup Trigger with three connected cards. When to enroll reads: Contacts enroll automatically when they're created or updated. Who to enroll has two condition rows, Where Country is any of United States, and And Form equals Outbound Sales, with an Add filter button. Enrollment reads: 1,284 contacts match right now.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-auto-enroll-trigger.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=e31b532d7b29ec90b4c33d9b8e8bfce5)

Setup Trigger for an Auto-enroll campaign with two conditions.

For example, a home-services company syncs web leads from its CRM with the tag `web-lead`. Its Auto-enroll campaign uses one condition, **Tags** is any of `web-lead`, so each new lead enrolls as soon as it syncs. The campaign's Interested outcome [writes](/dialer/sequences) `qualified` to a `lead_status` contact field. A second Auto-enroll campaign with the condition `lead_status` equals `qualified` then enrolls the lead for a follow-up with a different agent.

### When contacts enroll

At launch, every contact that matches enrolls. After launch, Retell checks a contact against your conditions when the contact is created, and when an update changes a field your conditions use. These changes count:

* Edits on the [Contacts](/features/contacts) page or through the API.
* Contact imports, including uploads to a Standard campaign.
* [CRM sync](/integrations/crm-overview).
* Field writes after a phone call or SMS chat, such as [Post Call Extraction](/features/post-call-analysis-overview) mappings and campaign outcomes that save to a contact field.
* [Backfills from past conversations](/features/contacts#backfill-fields-from-past-conversations), which can enroll many contacts at once.

Web calls and web chats have no phone number, so they never create or update a contact.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Every phone call or SMS chat with a new number creates a contact. If a brand-new contact meets your conditions, as it does with **Do not call** equals `false` on its own, the campaign enrolls and calls every new number your agents talk to. Base conditions on a tag or a field you set on purpose.

A new match enrolls right away with the stage **Validating**. Its compliance checks usually run within about 5 minutes, and then it's scheduled for its first attempt in its calling window. If the screening provider is unavailable, Retell retries, and the contact can stay in **Validating** for up to a day before it fails.

### Enrollment rules

* **Once per campaign, ever.** A contact that finished, stopped, or failed in a campaign never enrolls in that campaign again, even if it matches again. To call it again, use a new campaign.
* **No removal when a contact stops matching.** A contact stays enrolled after its fields change. To end its calls, use **Stop contact** on the [campaign page](/dialer/overview#monitor-a-campaign).
* **Overlapping campaigns both call.** If a contact matches two campaigns, it enrolls in both, and both call it. Keep the conditions of related campaigns mutually exclusive, for example with different tags.
* **Paused campaigns keep enrolling.** Scheduled, running, and paused campaigns enroll new matches. A paused campaign dials them after you resume it. A stopped campaign enrolls no one.
* **The campaign doesn't end on its own.** It runs until you stop it.
* **Up to 100,000 enrollments** (as of October 2026). The count includes every contact that ever enrolled, including contacts that failed a compliance check. After that, new matches don't enroll. Launch is blocked if more than 100,000 contacts match at launch.
* **Conditions lock at launch.** To change them, [duplicate the campaign](/dialer/overview#pause-stop-duplicate-or-delete) with **Settings + contacts**, edit the copy's conditions, and launch it. **Just settings** starts the copy with no conditions.
* **There's no exclusion list.** To keep contacts out, add a condition that rules them out.

## Use contact fields in the agent's prompt

Each call or SMS in a campaign passes the contact's fields to the agent as [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables):

* `{{first_name}}`, `{{last_name}}`, and `{{do_not_call}}`
* `{{contact_memory}}`, when the contact has [contact memory](/features/contact-memory)
* One variable per custom contact field, named after the field, such as `{{clinic}}` or `{{balance_due}}`. A Date or Datetime field arrives as a timestamp in milliseconds, so store any date the agent reads aloud, such as an appointment time, in a Text field.

The phone number is in `{{user_number}}`, like on any outbound call.

Retell reads the contact again before each attempt. A field that changes between attempts, from a new upload, a CRM sync, or an earlier call's outcome, reaches the next attempt. A campaign has no dynamic variables of its own, so store anything the agent needs per contact in a contact field.

If a contact has no value for a field, its variable is missing. Write prompts that read correctly without it. See [Handling missing variables](/build/dynamic-variables#handling-missing-variables).

## FAQ

> [accordion] Do I need a time zone column in my file?
>
> No. By default, a campaign dials each contact during the calling window in the contact's local time, worked out from the area codes of US and Canadian numbers. Other numbers use the sequence's fallback time zone. See [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences#timezone).

> [accordion] Will uploading a file overwrite my existing contacts?
>
> Only the fields you map, and only where the cell has a value. Blank cells and unmapped fields keep their current values. A `false` in the **Do Not Call** column never clears an existing do-not-call mark. See [What the upload changes in your Contacts](#what-the-upload-changes-in-your-contacts).

> [accordion] My call list has more than 50,000 rows. How do I use it?
>
> A Standard campaign takes one uploaded file. Split the list into files of up to 50,000 rows and import each one from **Actions → Upload CSV or XLSX** on the [Contacts](/features/contacts) page, adding the same tag to every file. Then filter the campaign on **Tags** is any of that tag. One campaign holds up to 100,000 contacts.

> [accordion] Why does my filter match fewer contacts than I expect?
>
> Check the [condition rules](#filter-your-contacts). Text matching is case-sensitive, phone numbers need the `+` and country code, every condition must match, and a contact with no value in a field never matches a condition on that field.

> [accordion] Can I add contacts to a Standard campaign after launch?
>
> No. Its list is fixed at launch. Launch another Standard campaign for the new contacts, or use an Auto-enroll campaign for a list that keeps growing.

> [accordion] Can the same contact be in two campaigns?
>
> Yes. Campaigns don't check each other, so a contact in two campaigns is called by both. The one exception is a copy made with **Contacts not yet contacted**, which skips numbers the original campaign already reached. Within one campaign, a contact enrolls only once. See [Enrollment rules](#enrollment-rules).

Related: [Dialer overview](/dialer/overview), [Compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks), [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences), [Caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers), and [Contacts](/features/contacts).


# Outbound call campaigns
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/dialer/overview

Run outbound call campaigns with the Retell AI Dialer: call and text a contact list, retry on a schedule, screen for DNC, and track conversions per contact.

The Dialer runs outbound campaigns from the Retell dashboard. It calls or texts your contacts with your agents, retries on a schedule you set, and decides each contact's next step from what happened in the conversation.

You build a campaign on four tabs (**Overview**, **Contacts**, **Sequence**, and **Numbers**), launch it, and follow every contact's progress on the campaign page. Open it from **Dialer** under **Deploy** in the dashboard sidebar.

A video walkthrough of building an outbound call and text campaign with the Dialer:

[Building an AI Dialer to automate outbound call and text campaigns](https://www.youtube.com/embed/xeMrI3YpcME)

## When to use it

* **You need several attempts per contact.** Appointment reminders, payment follow-ups, and lead reactivation rarely connect on the first call.
* **You want new contacts called automatically.** An Auto-enroll campaign calls every contact that matches your rules, such as each new web lead, without a new upload.
* **You must screen numbers before dialing.** Campaigns can check federal and state Do Not Call registries, TCPA litigators, and line types before the first call.
* **You want more calls answered.** [Local presence](/dialer/phone-numbers) calls each contact from a number in its own area code, and [spam check](/dialer/phone-numbers#spam-and-reputation) tells you when carriers label one of your US numbers "Spam Likely".

For example, a dental clinic runs an Auto-enroll campaign for contacts tagged `recall-due`. The agent calls each patient up to four times over three weeks, during clinic hours in the patient's time zone. When a patient books, the campaign writes `booked` to a contact field and stops calling them.

If you only need one call to each number in a CSV, with no retries, set the sequence to one attempt. [Batch calls](/deploy/make-batch-call) are deprecated but still available. To place calls from your own code, use [Create Phone Call](/api-references/create-phone-call).

## Standard and Auto-enroll campaigns

Choose the type when you create a campaign. You can't change it later.

| | Standard campaign | Auto-enroll campaign |
| - | - | - |
| Who is called | Contacts you select with a filter or upload as a CSV or XLSX file | Contacts that match your conditions at launch, and any contact that matches later |
| Contact list after launch | Fixed at launch | Grows as contacts are created or updated to match |
| When it ends | Completes on its own when every contact is done | Runs until you stop it |
| Typical use | A reminder or reactivation push to a known list | Calling each new lead within minutes |

## Key concepts

* **Contact**: a record in your workspace [Contacts](/features/contacts), keyed by phone number. Its contact fields reach the agent as [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables).
* **Sequence**: the plan each contact follows. It's made of conversation nodes connected by outcomes. See [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences).
* **Conversation node**: one step of the sequence, run by one agent over a phone call or SMS, with one or more attempts.
* **Attempt**: one call or SMS conversation. If the contact doesn't answer, the next attempt runs after the delay you set.
* **Outcome**: a result such as "Success" or "Not Interested" that sends the contact to another conversation node or ends the sequence. The **Disposition mix** chart on the Analytics tab counts contacts by outcome.
* **Calling window**: the days and hours when the campaign dials, in each contact's time zone.
* **Stage**: where a contact is in the campaign, such as Enrolled, In progress, or Completed. A campaign has a **status** instead, such as Running or Paused.

## How a campaign runs

**1. Choose contacts**

Select contacts for a Standard campaign, or set the conditions for an Auto-enroll campaign. See [Choose contacts](/dialer/contacts).

**2. Turn on compliance checks**

Pick the checks every contact must pass before it's dialed. See [Compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks).

**3. Build the sequence**

Assign agents, set attempts and delays, define outcomes, and set the calling window. See [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences).

**4. Set caller IDs and dialing rate**

Pick the numbers the campaign calls from and how many calls run at once. See [Caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers).

**5. Launch and monitor**

Review the campaign on the **Overview** tab, launch it now or schedule it, and track results on the campaign page. Both are covered below.

## Before you start

* **An agent for each channel you use.** Call steps need a voice agent and SMS steps need a chat agent.
* **Billing and identity verification.** Your workspace's billing must be in good standing, and its identity verification complete. Billing isn't in good standing when, for example, an invoice is overdue, a free trial has ended, or a spend budget or credit is used up. Buying your first phone number starts verification. Without both, you can't create, edit, launch, resume, or duplicate campaigns. You can still pause, stop, and delete them. A running campaign stops dialing while billing isn't in good standing, and resumes when it is. Buying numbers for a campaign also needs a payment method on file.
* **The right role.** Admins and Developers can create and run campaigns. Members can view campaigns but can't change them. See [access control](/accounts/access-control).
* **Phone numbers.** Use numbers you own, or buy new ones while you set up the campaign.
* **An FTC registration, if you screen against federal or state DNC lists.** See [Set up your FTC registration](/dialer/compliance-checks#set-up-your-ftc-registration).

## Create a campaign

**1. Pick a campaign type**

In **Dialer**, click **Create new campaign** and choose **Standard campaign** or **Auto-enroll campaign**. Retell saves a draft named "Untitled campaign" and opens it. Click the name to rename it.

**2. Set up each tab**

Work through **Contacts**, **Sequence**, and **Numbers**. Click **Done** on a tab to save it and return to **Overview**. On **Contacts**, click **Continue** first to reach the compliance checks. The **Sequence** tab saves each change as you make it.

**3. Review the Overview tab**

**Overview** summarizes the contacts, phone numbers, and sequence. In a draft, **Contacts**, **Sequence**, and **Numbers** each show a check mark once they're set up.

![Overview tab of a draft Standard campaign named Spring recall reminders. Check marks show the Contacts, Sequence, and Numbers tabs are set up. The left column shows a Contacts card with 100 contacts, a Phone numbers card with 9 existing numbers grouped by region under Local presence dialing, Launch timing set to Schedule for later with an empty date field, a notice that the start time can't change after launch, and a checked consent statement. The right column previews the sequence: Start, Conversation 1 with its agent and one attempt, and Other outcome ending the sequence. The Schedule Launch button is at the bottom right.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-overview-tab.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=294a5ffd45c961f59bb01ae8c4f05fac)

The Overview tab of a draft Standard campaign, set to schedule its launch.

## Launch a campaign

**1. Choose the launch timing**

Under **Launch timing**, pick **Start now** or **Schedule for later**. A scheduled start must be at least 5 minutes away, and you can pick its time zone. You can't change the start time after launch.

**2. Confirm consent**

Check the box that confirms the campaign "respects all applicable legal and consent requirements for the contacts being dialed, including TCPA, state DNC laws, and any opt-in obligations."

**3. Launch**

Click **Launch Now** or **Schedule Launch**. A launch that starts now, or that buys new numbers, asks you to confirm. If it buys numbers, choose Twilio or Telnyx in that dialog. If it buys US numbers, a second step asks whether to verify them first. **Verify first, launch in 7 days** is on by default and delays the start by 7 days, even for **Launch Now**. To start on time, select **Skip for now**. See [Buy new numbers](/dialer/phone-numbers#buy-new-numbers).

If something is missing, the launch stops with "Campaign is not ready to launch" and names the first problem, such as a sequence step without an agent.

At launch, Retell runs the compliance checks and enrolls the contacts right away, even for a scheduled campaign. Calls start at the start time, inside each contact's calling window. The only exception is a callback the lead asked for, which goes out at the requested time (see [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences#auto-schedule-callbacks)). Each contact is dialed at the start time, or when its calling window next opens, but never faster than the campaign's concurrency and calls-per-second limits allow. See [Caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers#set-the-dialing-rate). If the screening provider is unavailable, contacts stay in **Validating** until it recovers. Contacts of an Auto-enroll campaign show **Validating** for about 5 minutes before their first attempt is scheduled.

The launch runs in the background. While it enrolls contacts, the campaign shows a **Launching** status, then moves to **Scheduled** (for a later start) or **Running** once enrollment finishes. You can't edit or delete a launching campaign, but you can stop it, which ends its enrollment.

### What you can change after launch

Contacts, compliance checks, and the sequence lock at launch. You can still rename a running, scheduled, or paused campaign, and change its [phone numbers and dialing rate](/dialer/phone-numbers). To change anything else, [duplicate the campaign](#pause-stop-duplicate-or-delete) and launch the copy.

On the campaign page, click **Edit** to open the setup tabs. They're read-only, except **Numbers**. For a stopped or completed campaign the button reads **Details**, and every tab is read-only.

## Monitor a campaign

A launched campaign opens on its campaign page, with an **Analytics** tab and a **Contacts** tab.

![Campaign page for a running Auto-enroll campaign, Analytics tab. Above the charts are an All time date range, a Filter button, and a Phone number filter. Four cards show Dialed 3,875, Connected 2,480, Converted 932, and Conversion rate 24.1%. Below, the Disposition mix chart flows from Enrolled to outcomes such as Appointment booked, Do not call, Not interested, and Transferred to agent.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-campaign-analytics.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=20d62aabc35dc358a1cfc42799be9a17)

The Analytics tab of a running Auto-enroll campaign.

### Analytics

| Metric | Definition |
| - | - |
| **Dialed** | Contacts called or texted at least once. |
| **Connected** | Contacts who picked up a call or replied to a text. |
| **Converted** | Contacts who reached a successful exit. |
| **Conversion rate** | Converted contacts divided by dialed contacts. |

**Disposition mix** shows how many contacts reached each outcome, starting from Enrolled. **Dials over time** counts every call and SMS attempt, retries included, and how many of them connected. **Conversion rate over time** shows the share of dialed contacts that converted. Both charts group by day, week, or month, depending on the date range.

Filter everything on the tab by date range, stage, phone number, or contact ID. Dates use your browser's time zone unless you pick another in the date range.

### Contacts

The **Contacts** tab lists every contact in the campaign with its stage, current conversation node, next attempt, and whether it was contacted and connected. Click a contact to see each call or SMS grouped by conversation node, with its outcome and the next scheduled attempt. Click a conversation to open its full transcript and recording.

![Contacts tab of a running campaign with a contact's side panel open; the contacts table behind it is dimmed. The panel shows the contact's name, a Stop contact button, the stage In progress, contact information with phone number and last contacted date, and a View link. Under Conversation 1 are Call attempt 1 with Dial no answer, the same attempt's double dial, a Call back that was picked up, Call attempt 2 that was picked up, and a Chat agent conversation tagged with the outcome Interested. Under Conversation 2, a Next attempt row reads Attempt 1, Scheduled on Jul 10, 9:00 AM.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-contact-details.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=65b47023b6d981eff2d8e03a40d56ef8)

A contact's details on the Contacts tab, with its conversations grouped by conversation node.

Each contact has one of these stages:

| Stage | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **Validating** | Compliance checks are still running. If they don't finish within 24 hours, the contact moves to **Enroll failed** with the reason "Validation timed out". |
| **Enrolled** | Waiting for its next call or text. |
| **In progress** | A call or text is happening now. |
| **Completed** | Reached an exit, a Do Not Call outcome, or its last attempt. |
| **Enroll failed** | Failed a [compliance check](/dialer/compliance-checks), such as federal Do Not Call, was a duplicate, or its checks timed out. It's never dialed in this campaign. |
| **Stopped** | You stopped the contact, or the campaign was stopped while this contact was in a call or text conversation, or still being checked. Contacts that were waiting in **Enrolled** when you stopped the campaign stay there and are never dialed. |
| **Failed** | Could not be dialed after it enrolled, for example with no number to call from. |

The first three stages are active. The rest are final. Hover over a failed contact's stage to see the reason.

To stop one contact, open its menu and click **Stop contact**. The contact gets no more calls or messages from this campaign, and a conversation already in progress finishes.

## Pause, stop, duplicate, or delete

Open a campaign's **More actions** menu on the campaign page or the Dialer list.

* **Pause** stops new dials within about a minute. Calls already placed or about to start finish. When you **Resume**, contacts that came due during the pause are dialed first, inside their calling window.
* **Stop** ends the campaign for good: it "stops dialing new contacts and cannot be resumed. Calls already in flight finish." It also releases the campaign's phone numbers and stops Auto-enroll intake.
* **Duplicate** creates a new draft named "Duplicated from" followed by the original name. It copies the settings, number pool, planned number purchases, and dialing capacity, but not the schedule. Choose **Just settings**, **Settings + contacts**, or, for a stopped or completed campaign, **Contacts not yet contacted**.
* **Delete** removes a draft, stopped, or completed campaign, and "its dialing history will be removed. This cannot be undone." Stop a launching, scheduled, running, or paused campaign before you delete it.

A Standard campaign moves to **Completed** on its own once every contact reaches a final stage. An Auto-enroll campaign keeps running until you stop it.

## Limits

These limits apply to every workspace (as of October 2026).

| Limit | Value |
| - | - |
| Contacts per campaign | 100,000. An Auto-enroll campaign stops adding contacts at 100,000, counting contacts that failed their checks. |
| CSV or XLSX upload | 50 MB and 50,000 rows. A file over the row limit is rejected as a whole, and the dashboard shows the error only after you confirm the upload. |
| Phone numbers per campaign | 500 in total: the numbers you own plus the new numbers you plan to buy |
| Scheduled start | In the dashboard, at least 5 minutes after you launch |

## FAQ

> [accordion] How is the Dialer different from batch calls?
>
> A [batch call](/deploy/make-batch-call) places one call to each row of a CSV. The Dialer adds retries, call and SMS steps, outcome-based routing, compliance checks, calling windows in each contact's time zone, and per-contact tracking. Batch calls are deprecated but still available: open them from **Legacy batch calls** in the header of the Dialer page.

> [accordion] Do campaign calls count toward my concurrency limit?
>
> Yes. Campaign calls can use your workspace's concurrency limit minus any [reserved inbound concurrency](/deploy/concurrency#reserved-inbound-concurrency), and they share it with your other outbound and web calls.
