Without an inbound reserve, a busy campaign can leave no room for inbound calls. Each campaign also has its own limit. See [Caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers).

> [accordion] Why is a contact stuck in Validating?
>
> Its compliance checks haven't finished. Retell retries them, and a contact is never dialed until it passes. After 24 hours without a result, the contact fails with "Validation timed out". See [Compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks).

> [accordion] Why can't I create a campaign?
>
> Your workspace's billing must be in good standing, for example no overdue invoice, no ended free trial, and no spent budget or credit. Identity verification must be complete, and you need the Admin or Developer role. A payment method is required only to buy phone numbers.

Related: [Choose contacts](/dialer/contacts), [Compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks), [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences), and [Caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers).


# Caller ID and pacing
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/dialer/phone-numbers

Set up local presence dialing and caller ID rotation for Retell AI outbound campaigns, buy numbers by area code, and cap each campaign's concurrency and CPS.

The **Numbers** tab of a [Dialer](/dialer/overview) campaign sets the caller ID each contact sees and how fast the campaign dials. You choose the numbers the campaign calls from, called its number pool, and how they rotate, then cap the campaign's concurrent calls and calls per second (CPS).

Open the tab from a draft campaign, or click **Edit** on a launched campaign's page.

## Choose how numbers rotate

Under **Phone number setup**, pick one option:

* **Local presence dialing**: "Match local area codes to improve pickup rates." This is the default. Each contact is called from a number assigned to its own area.
* **Round robin phone numbers**: "Initiate call from your numbers pool." Each new contact gets the next number in the pool, so calls spread evenly across every number.

| | Local presence dialing | Round robin phone numbers |
| - | - | - |
| Caller ID for a new contact | A number assigned to the contact's region, or a **Default phone number** | The next number in the pool |
| Numbers to add | Numbers in the regions where your contacts are | Any numbers you own or buy |
| Contact with no matching number | Called from a **Default phone number**, or fails if there's none | Can't happen, since every number serves every contact |
| Good fit | Contacts spread across many area codes | Contacts in one area, or a few numbers your customers already know |

In both modes, a contact keeps the caller ID it got first for every later call and text, as long as that number stays in the pool. The contact sees one number from your campaign, and a callback to that number reaches the campaign. See [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences) for how callbacks are handled.

The choice locks at launch.

For example, a solar installer calls 6,000 leads across Texas with local presence. Dallas leads see a 214 number, Houston leads see a 713 number, and leads in smaller towns see the installer's Default phone number.

![Phone number setup with Local presence dialing selected and Round robin phone numbers unselected. The Numbers by area code card has an Auto-fill button and United States and Canada tabs. Rows show Bay Area, CA with 780 contacts, 3 numbers, Suggest 16 numbers, and an Edit button; Greater Los Angeles, CA with 652 contacts and Suggest 14 numbers; New York Metro, NY with 404 contacts and Suggest 9 numbers; each with area code tags. The last row, Default phone number, reads Used to call contacts when you haven't added a number for their area code, with a Set up button.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-local-presence.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=377e2b04e508bcbbbc13d78ba0fe5dfa)

Local presence dialing with regions ranked by contact count.

## How local presence picks a caller ID

The **Numbers by area code** card lists the regions where your contacts are, ranked by contact count, with a **United States** or **Canada** tab for each country that has contacts. A region is a group of area codes that serve the same place, such as all the overlay codes of one city. Eleven metro regions, such as Bay Area, CA and New York Metro, NY, combine several neighboring areas. A number you assign to a region can call every contact in all of its area codes.

When a contact is due, Retell picks its caller ID in this order:

1. The caller ID the contact already has from this campaign, if that number is still in the pool.
2. A number assigned to the contact's region. The contact's country and area code must match the region exactly. When a region has several numbers, they take turns.
3. A number in the **Default phone number** row: "Used to call contacts when you haven’t added a number for their area code." Contacts outside the US and Canada also use this row.
4. If none of these exist, the contact fails with "No number available to call from" and isn't called.

Retell doesn't fall back to a nearby area code at dial time. To cover a region with a number from a different area code, click **Set up** on the region, then **Use other area code**.

Each region row shows how many numbers it has and a suggestion, such as "Suggest 3 numbers." Retell suggests one number per 50 contacts in the region, and at least one. Click **Set up** (or **Edit**, once the region has numbers) to pick numbers you own in that region or plan new ones.

**Auto-fill** sets up every region at once. It selects each number you own in a region that has contacts, then fills in purchase quantities so each region reaches its suggestion. Review the quantities on the **United States** and **Canada** tabs, then click **Save**.

> [!TIP]
>
> An Auto-enroll campaign keeps adding contacts after launch, some from areas you haven't covered. Add at least one Default phone number so those contacts don't fail.

## Add numbers you own

Any number in your workspace can join the pool, including numbers you [connected through custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony).

* **Round robin**: click **Add numbers**, select numbers under **Reusing numbers you own**, and click **Save**.
* **Local presence**: click **Set up** on a region. The list shows the numbers you own in that region's area codes.

Campaign calls use the agents in your [sequence](/dialer/sequences), not the number's own outbound agent. A number can be in more than one campaign at a time.

A toll-free number from Retell can call US numbers only. A contact outside the US that gets a toll-free caller ID fails with "Destination not allowed". Under local presence, every toll-free number you buy for the campaign joins the Default phone number row, including toll-free numbers planned on the **Canada** tab. If you call contacts in Canada, don't buy toll-free numbers for the campaign, and keep toll-free numbers you own out of a round robin pool and out of the Default phone number row.

## Buy new numbers

While the campaign is a draft, you can plan new numbers in the **Buy new numbers** section of the **Add numbers** or **Auto-fill** dialog. Local numbers cost $2 per month and toll-free numbers cost $5 per month (as of October 2026).

* A region's dialog offers that region's area codes.
* The round robin dialog and the Default phone number row offer **Normal numbers**, which can have any US area code, and **Toll free**.
* **Auto-fill** offers area codes, normal numbers, and toll-free numbers in both the US and Canada.

Saving the dialog saves the plan but buys nothing. Planned numbers show "Bought at launch" until Retell buys them, in one of two ways:

* **Now:** on the **Overview** tab, click **Purchase** on the **Phone numbers** card. Retell "buys the numbers now and adds them to this campaign."
* **At launch:** when you click **Launch Now** or **Schedule Launch**, Retell buys the remaining planned numbers. For a scheduled campaign, the numbers are bought and billed from that moment, not from the start time.

Both ask you to choose a provider: Twilio (the default) or Telnyx. Telnyx sells US local numbers only. If you choose Telnyx, **Purchase** skips the Canadian and toll-free numbers, and launch is blocked until you switch to Twilio or remove them.

When you buy US numbers at launch, the confirm dialog has a second step that asks whether to verify them first. **Verify first, launch in 7 days** is selected by default, and the button reads **Schedule and verify**. This moves the start to at least 7 days from now, so **Launch Now** does not dial until then. A start time you picked later than 7 days out stays. To keep your start time, select **Skip for now**. Verified numbers cost \$10 per month each.

If you click **Purchase** on the **Overview** tab instead, the same choice appears as **Purchase and verify**. It does not change when the campaign starts.

A campaign can use at most 500 numbers in total (as of October 2026). Keep the numbers you own plus the new numbers you plan to buy at or under 500. The dashboard checks the two counts separately, so a pool over 500 can fail after the purchase, once the numbers are already bought and billed.

Numbers you buy stay in your workspace and in the campaign's pool, even if the launch fails after the purchase. They're billed monthly until you delete them on the **Phone Numbers** page. See [Purchase phone number](/deploy/purchase-number) for how number billing works.

After launch, you can't plan purchases in the campaign. [Buy numbers](/deploy/purchase-number) on the **Phone Numbers** page, then add them as numbers you own.

![Add numbers dialog over the dimmed Numbers tab, subtitled Needs 14 numbers to cover 652 contacts locally. Reusing numbers you own, tagged suggested, lists one Los Angeles number with Select all and Use other area code buttons. Buy new numbers shows the notice Suggest spam verification for new numbers, then rows for area codes 213 and 323 at \$2 per number with quantity steppers; 213 is set to 2. The footer reads 2 new numbers, Bought at launch, 0 you own, 2 total, with Cancel and Save buttons.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-buy-numbers.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=044d74c76f1f4ddf4c07cc334ed44706)

The Add numbers dialog for one region, with two new numbers planned.

## SMS requirements

If your sequence has an SMS node, two rules apply to the pool:

* **Every number must be SMS-enabled.** That means a Retell Twilio number with an approved [A2P campaign](/deploy/sms-campaign-application), or your own Twilio number set up for SMS. See [Enable SMS](/deploy/enable-sms).
* **The plan can't include new numbers.** Newly bought numbers can't send SMS, so **Purchase** is disabled. Remove planned numbers on the **Numbers** tab.

Launch is blocked until both rules hold, with a message such as "The sequence sends SMS, but 2 numbers can’t." After launch, Retell rejects a pool change that adds a number without SMS.

## Spam and reputation

Carriers can label a number that places many calls as "Spam Likely", and a recycled number can arrive already flagged. Retell doesn't replace flagged numbers in a campaign automatically. To keep pickup rates up:

* **Use enough numbers.** More numbers means fewer calls from each one. Follow the suggestion of one number per 50 contacts.
* **Check new numbers.** After Retell buys them, turn on **Daily spam check** for them on the **Phone Numbers** page. It checks carrier spam flags once a day, Sunday through Thursday. If carriers flag a number on a Friday or Saturday, the number shows as spam after the Sunday check. The check covers US numbers only and costs \$2 per month per number (as of October 2026).
* **Register your numbers.** Apply for a [verified phone number](/build/telephony/verified-phone) and [branded call](/build/telephony/branded-call), both for US numbers.
* **Swap out flagged numbers.** Remove a flagged number from the pool and add a clean one. The change reaches the campaign within about 15 minutes, and contacts that had the flagged number then get a new caller ID.

See the [Spam Likely overview](/build/telephony/call_efficiency_overview) for how to check a number's status.

## Set the dialing rate

The **Dialing capacity** section caps how many calls the campaign runs at once and how fast it starts them. Both are caps, not reservations: they limit this campaign, but they don't hold capacity for it.

![Dialing capacity section. The Campaign concurrency limit card has an Adjust concurrency link, a stepper set to 25, and the line Total limit 200, Inbound reserve 60, Other 115. The Calls per second (CPS) card has a CPS calculator link, a box reading 3 CPS capacity with an Adjust CPS limit button, and the line Twilio 1, Telnyx 1, Custom Telephony CPS 1.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-dialing-capacity.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=168bf2ea834574db0384233d1be658c6)

The Dialing capacity section of the Numbers tab.

### Campaign concurrency limit

The campaign concurrency limit is the most calls this campaign runs at the same time. In the dashboard, the default is half your workspace [concurrency limit](/deploy/concurrency), rounded down, but never more than your workspace limit minus the inbound reserve. A campaign created through the API without a dialing capacity has no campaign limit.

* **The lower limit wins.** The campaign runs at most its own limit, and never more than the workspace's free outbound capacity.
* **No burst, no inbound reserve.** Campaign calls never use [concurrency burst](/deploy/concurrency#concurrency-burst) or the [reserved inbound concurrency](/deploy/concurrency#reserved-inbound-concurrency).
* **Shared capacity.** All campaigns, your other outbound calls, and web calls share the same outbound capacity. Several campaigns can each set the full amount, and the first call ready takes the next free slot. Hover over **Other** in the "Total limit · Inbound reserve · Other" line to see the other campaigns' limits.
* **Calls wait at capacity.** When no slot is free, the next call waits until one opens. Waiting doesn't use one of the contact's attempts.

If your workspace has no inbound reserve, a notice reads "No concurrency is reserved for inbound calls." If this campaign's limit also takes all outbound capacity, it reads "No concurrency is left for inbound calls."

Raising your workspace limit doesn't raise the campaign's limit. Update it here too.

**Adjust concurrency** opens the **Adjust concurrency limit** dialog. It changes your workspace, not just this campaign: set **Concurrent calls** and **Inbound reserve**. Each concurrent call above your included limit costs \$8.00 per month (as of October 2026). You're charged immediately when you increase the limit, and a decrease doesn't change charges for the current billing cycle. In the Dialer, this button is available to Admins only. Developers can change the concurrent calls on **Settings > Limits**, but not the inbound reserve.

### Calls per second (CPS)

CPS caps how many calls the campaign starts each second, separately for each telephony provider: Twilio, Telnyx, and Custom Telephony. SMS steps don't count toward the concurrency or CPS limits. A call counts against the provider of the number it's placed from. The card shows the sum, such as "3 CPS capacity".

By default, the campaign can use your full workspace CPS for each provider. A workspace has 1 CPS per provider unless it's been raised. All campaigns share the workspace CPS.

To cap the campaign lower, click **Adjust CPS limit** and set a value for each provider, between 1 and your workspace limit. This buys nothing. To raise workspace CPS, [adjust it on Settings > Limits](/deploy/concurrency#adjust-cps-calls-per-second). After you confirm, the campaign keeps these values even if you buy more workspace CPS later.

**CPS calculator** opens the same [calculator](/deploy/concurrency#estimate-values-with-the-calculator) as the Limits page.

## Live estimates

The **Live estimates** panel estimates how fast the campaign can reach your contacts. Edit the inputs to test scenarios:

| Input | Default |
| - | - |
| **Concurrency** | The campaign concurrency limit |
| **Calls per second (CPS)** | The campaign's CPS for the providers in your pool |
| **Answer rate** | 20% |
| **Avg. call duration** | 20 min |

The panel returns:

* **Capacity**: calls per hour. It's the lower of what CPS allows and what concurrency allows, since only answered calls hold a line for the average duration.
* **Time**: how long one call to each of the **Total contacts** takes.
* **Costs**: an estimate for the answered first calls: contacts × answer rate × average duration × the starting agent's price per minute, plus \$0.01 per minute when the pool has Retell Twilio or Telnyx numbers. It shows a dash unless the sequence starts with a phone call node that has an agent.

Estimates leave out ringing time, retries, and later sequence steps. "Changing these inputs does not change campaign limits."

## What you can change after launch

On the campaign page, click **Edit** and open **Numbers**. For a stopped or completed campaign, the button reads **Details** and every tab is read-only. Until then, you can:

* Add or remove numbers you own. You can't remove the last number.
* Change the campaign concurrency limit and CPS.

You can't switch between local presence and round robin, or plan new purchases.

Changes to numbers, concurrency, and CPS save when you click **Done** or switch tabs. **Save** in the numbers dialog only stages the change, and **Back to campaign** discards it. Concurrency and CPS changes apply from the next call. Number changes reach the campaign within about 15 minutes. A call already in progress keeps its caller ID.

Once the campaign is stopped or completed, the **Numbers** tab is read-only. Its numbers stay in your workspace and keep their monthly fee until you delete them.

## FAQ

> [accordion] How does caller ID rotation work?
>
> Rotation happens across contacts, not across calls to one contact. With round robin, each new contact gets the next number in the pool. With local presence, each new contact gets the next number assigned to its region. Every later call and text to that contact uses the same caller ID while the number stays in the pool.

> [accordion] Why do my campaign calls show as Spam Likely?
>
> Carriers can flag a number that places many calls, and a recycled number can arrive already flagged. Retell doesn't swap flagged numbers out of a campaign. Remove the flagged number on the **Numbers** tab, add a clean one, and follow the steps in [Spam and reputation](#spam-and-reputation).

> [accordion] How many phone numbers does a campaign need?
>
> At least one. For local presence, Retell suggests one number per 50 contacts in each region, and **Auto-fill** plans that many. More numbers spread the volume, so each one places fewer calls. A pool holds up to 500 numbers.

> [accordion] Can a campaign make only one call at a time?
>
> Yes. Set the campaign concurrency limit to 1, and the campaign starts its next call only after the current one ends. The limit applies to the campaign, not to a phone number. Another campaign or your own outbound calls can still use the same number at the same time.

> [accordion] How do campaigns share concurrency with inbound calls?
>
> Campaign calls use only outbound capacity: your concurrency limit minus the inbound reserve. They never use the reserve, so those slots stay free for inbound calls. If you have no inbound reserve, inbound calls get whatever campaigns and other outbound calls leave free. Set a reserve with **Adjust concurrency** or on **Settings > Limits**. See [concurrency](/deploy/concurrency#reserved-inbound-concurrency).

> [accordion] Why is my campaign dialing slower than its limits?
>
> The limits are maximums. A campaign waits while other campaigns and outbound calls use the workspace's outbound capacity, starts calls no faster than its CPS, and dials only inside the [calling window](/dialer/sequences). A contact that waits keeps all its attempts. To see what else shares your capacity, hover over **Other** under **Campaign concurrency limit**.

Related: [Dialer overview](/dialer/overview), [Choose contacts](/dialer/contacts), [Build a sequence](/dialer/sequences), and [Understand concurrency & limits](/deploy/concurrency).


# Build a sequence
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/dialer/sequences

Build a call retry sequence in Retell AI: set attempts and delays, route each AI call disposition to the next step, and dial in each contact's local hours.

A sequence is the plan a [Dialer](/dialer/overview) campaign runs for each contact: which agent calls or texts them, how many attempts it makes, and how long it waits between attempts. After each answered call or SMS reply, the sequence's outcomes decide whether the contact moves to another conversation or exits, and its calling hours decide when Retell may dial.

You build the sequence on the **Sequence** tab of a draft campaign.

## How does a sequence work?

Each contact starts at the first conversation node. What happens after each attempt decides the next step:

| After an attempt | Next step |
| - | - |
| The contact answered the call or replied to the SMS | The node's outcomes send the contact to another conversation node or to an exit. |
| Nobody answered, the call reached voicemail, or the SMS got no reply | The node's next attempt, after its delay. |
| The node has no attempts left | The node's built-in **No Response** outcome applies. By default it ends the sequence. |

Every node has a **No Response** outcome. Retell applies it when the node's last attempt goes unanswered. To send these contacts to another node, such as an SMS follow-up, change its **Next**. It can't end the sequence as successful.

Either exit sets the contact's [stage](/dialer/overview#contacts) to **Completed**. Only the successful exit counts the contact as **Converted** in the campaign's analytics.

### The default sequence

Every new campaign starts with this sequence:

| Setting | Default |
| - | - |
| Conversation node | **Conversation 1**, a phone call node with no agent selected |
| Attempts | 4: **Immediately**, then after 3, 7, and 10 days. Each delay counts from the previous attempt, so dials go out on days 0, 3, 10, and 20. |
| Global outcomes | **Success** ends the sequence as successful. **Not Interested** and **Do Not Call** end it. |
| Calling window | 9:00 to 18:00, every day |
| Timezone | **Contact's local time**, with Los Angeles as the fallback |
| Automatic retries | **Double dial** and **Auto-schedule callbacks** are on |

Select an agent for Conversation 1 before you launch. Then check the global outcome descriptions. **Success** reads "The lead agreed to move forward and booked an appointment." Rewrite it to match what success means for your campaign.

### Start from a template

While the sequence is still the default one, the canvas shows **Start with a template** in its lower-left corner, with two ready-made multi-step sequences to build on:

| Template | What it builds |
| - | - |
| **Call + SMS follow-up** | Three nodes. **First call** (phone) tries twice, immediately and after 1 day, leaving a voicemail each time. If no one answers, **Text follow up** (SMS) texts after a 1-day delay, then **Final call** (phone) tries twice more, immediately and after 3 days. |
| **Multi-stage follow-up** | Two phone nodes. **Pitch** tries three times, immediately and after 1 and 2 days, leaving a voicemail each time. A **Still evaluating** outcome routes unsure leads to **Convince** after a 1-day delay, which tries three more times, hanging up on voicemail. |

Both templates come with the standard **Success**, **Not Interested**, and **Do Not Call** global outcomes, a 9:00 to 18:00 calling window every day, **Contact's local time** with Los Angeles as the fallback, and **Double dial** and **Auto-schedule callbacks** on. The voicemail messages use [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables) such as `{{first_name}}` and `{{company_name}}`, which you edit per attempt.

Picking a template replaces the current sequence, so the option disappears once you edit the sequence. A **Template applied** message with an **Undo** button lets you revert the change. The nodes come without an agent, so pick one for each node before launch, and review the voicemail text and outcome descriptions.

## The canvas

![Sequence canvas. Start leads to Conversation 1, a phone call node with an agent set to Latest Created and two attempts, Day 0 and Day 2. Below it, a Success line with a globe icon leads to a flagged Ends the sequence exit, an Interested line leads to Conversation 2, and a +4 line leads to a plain Ends the sequence exit. Conversation 2 is a green SMS node with a chat agent and one attempt on Day 0, with its own Success and +4 lines to exits. The Global panel on the right shows Automatic retries with Double dial and Auto-schedule callbacks both on, Timezone options with Contact's local time selected and Los Angeles as the Otherwise time zone, and the start of the Calling window section. A Select, Pan, and Center canvas toolbar sits at the bottom.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-sequence-canvas.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=6574e1922b01fbf3836d37624f1b28be)

A two-node sequence: a call node that sends Interested contacts to an SMS node, with the Global panel open.

The canvas draws the sequence from top to bottom:

* **Start** marks where every contact enters.
* Each **conversation node** shows its agent and its attempts. Each attempt row shows the day it runs, such as "Day 3". Hover the timing to see the delay after the previous attempt. A voicemail icon on an attempt means it leaves a voicemail.
* **Ends the sequence** marks an exit. The exit with a flag is the successful exit.
* Each line between them carries an outcome name. Outcomes that go to the same place share one label, such as **+3**; hover it to list them. A globe icon marks a global outcome, and **Other outcome** is the line a contact follows when no outcome matches. A line for an outcome with a [delay](#outcomes) shows how long the contact waits before the next node.

Click a node to open its **Settings** and **Outcomes** tabs. Click an outcome label to open that outcome. Click empty canvas, **Start**, or an exit to open the **Global** panel, which holds global outcomes, retries, and calling hours.

### Add and delete nodes

To add a branch, click **+** under a node ("Create new outcome and conversation node"). Retell adds an outcome named "Outcome N" with an empty condition, and points it at a new "Conversation N" node. The new node uses the same channel as its parent, starts with the same four attempts as Conversation 1, and has no agent. **Add outcome** on a node's **Outcomes** tab does the same.

To delete a node, select it and click its trash icon, or click **Delete** at the bottom of its **Settings** tab:

* If other nodes come after it, "Delete node and children?" asks you to confirm. Those nodes are deleted too, unless another path still reaches them.
* If it's the first node, "Delete entire sequence?" asks you to confirm, and the sequence starts over with one empty node.
* You can't delete the only node.
* Node outcomes that pointed to a deleted node stay, with no destination. Pick a new **Next** for each one before launch. An **Other outcome** that pointed to it changes to **Ends the sequence**.

You can't drag nodes or draw lines. The layout follows each outcome's **Next** setting, so to reconnect nodes, change where an outcome points. A node that no outcome points to stays on the canvas, detached, and launch fails with `Campaign is not ready to launch: Node "Conversation 2" is not reachable from the start node`. Delete the node or point an outcome at it.

Use the toolbar at the bottom of the canvas to switch between **Select** and **Pan**, or click **Center canvas** to fit the sequence on screen. Press `Cmd/Ctrl + Z` to undo and `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + Z` to redo, up to 100 steps.

### Saving and launch

Every change saves automatically, and the footer shows "Auto saved at" with the time of the last save. If Retell rejects a change, "Failed to save sequence. Changes reverted" appears and that change is undone. If the save fails for another reason, "Failed to save sequence" appears with a **Retry** button, your edits stay, and the footer reads "Changes are not saved".

Before launch, every conversation node needs an agent, every outcome needs a condition and a destination, and the calling window needs at least one time and a time zone. Retell also rejects agents that take payments and agents whose channel doesn't match the node. The sequence locks when you launch or schedule the campaign. To change it afterward, [duplicate the campaign](/dialer/overview#pause-stop-duplicate-or-delete) and edit the copy.

## Conversation nodes

![Sequence canvas dimmed behind the open panel for Conversation 1, Settings tab. The Agents section shows Default inbound and outbound agent set to Q4 Campaign follow-up at Latest Created, and Override Inbound agent on with Q4 Campaign inbound selected. The Attempts section shows Attempt 1, Immediately on Day 0, Leave a voicemail on with Agent's default and a summary of the agent's static voicemail sentence, and Attempt 2, 2 days after Attempt 1 with the note 2 days after first attempt, Leave a voicemail on with Static sentence and its message text.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-node-settings.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=9850f12809dd3280f82d1d3bb5ab30d9)

The Settings tab of a selected phone call node.

A conversation node is one step of the sequence, run by one agent. Its **Settings** tab has an **Agents** section and an **Attempts** section. Click the node name at the top of the panel to rename it.

### Choose the agent

Pick the agent under **Default inbound & outbound agent**. The agent decides the node's channel:

* A voice agent makes it a phone call node.
* A chat agent makes it an SMS node.

One sequence can mix both. Transfer agents can't run a node.

Then pick which version of the agent the campaign uses:

| Choice | Version each dial uses |
| - | - |
| A specific version, such as **V3** | Always that version |
| **Latest Published** | The newest published version |
| A tag, such as `prod` | The version the [environment tag](/agent/version#environment-tags) points to |
| **Latest Created** | The newest version, including an unpublished draft |

Retell resolves the version at each dial, not at launch. Choose a specific version to keep the agent fixed for the whole campaign, or **Latest Published** to roll published changes into a running campaign. Avoid **Latest Created**: a draft you're still editing reaches live calls on the next dial. If the agent or version is deleted, contacts that reach the node fail with "Agent not found".

### Answer callbacks to the campaign number

When a lead calls back the number the campaign dialed them from, the node's agent answers if all of these are true:

* The lead calls within 30 days of the campaign's last dial to them.
* The campaign is Running or Paused.
* The contact is waiting for its next attempt (stage **Enrolled**) on a phone call node.

To answer these calls with a different agent, turn on **Override Inbound agent** and pick an agent in the selector that appears below it. The callback doesn't use an attempt, and its outcomes work like a dialed call's. If it counts as unanswered (see [When are outcomes evaluated?](#when-are-outcomes-evaluated)), the node's attempts start over at Attempt 1. After the contact exits, or once the campaign stops, the number's own inbound agent answers.

### Set attempts and delays

Attempt 1 runs **Immediately**, and a node needs at least one attempt. Each later **Attempt** card sets a number of minutes, hours, or days **after** the previous attempt started, and a line below it shows how long after the first attempt it runs. Click **Add attempt** to add one with a 1-day delay. There's no limit on the number of attempts or the length of a delay.

If an attempt comes due outside the [calling window](#calling-window), it waits for the next opening. An attempt is one dial (plus its [double dial](#double-dial)) or one SMS conversation. The contact moves to the next attempt only when the current one goes unanswered.

### Leave a voicemail

On a phone call node, each attempt has its own voicemail setting. With **Leave a voicemail** on, choose the message:

| Option | What the agent leaves |
| - | - |
| **Agent's default** | Whatever the agent's own [voicemail setting](/build/handle-voicemail) does. The card shows a summary, such as "Hangs up when the call reaches voicemail." |
| **Static sentence** | The exact text you enter, with [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables) such as `{{first_name}}` filled in. |
| **Prompt** | A message that an LLM writes from your instructions and the call transcript. |

Turn **Leave a voicemail** off to hang up on voicemail for that attempt.

Campaign calls always detect voicemail. If the attempt uses **Agent's default** and the agent has voicemail detection off, the call hangs up when it reaches voicemail. A voicemail always counts as unanswered, even when the agent leaves a message, so the next attempt follows.

> [!TIP]
>
> Leave a message only on the last attempt or two. Earlier attempts then hang up on voicemail and redial right away with [double dial](#double-dial).

### SMS nodes

An SMS node texts the contact from one of the campaign's numbers:

* The chat agent writes the first message. There's no message template, so describe the opening message in the agent's prompt.
* The chat stays open for replies until the next attempt is due. If the agent has **Auto-Close Inactive Chats** on, the chat can close sooner. On the last attempt, the chat closes on that timeout, or after 2 days if the agent has none.
* If the lead replies, the chat stays open until the agent's auto-close timeout plus about 1 hour, or 2 days if the agent has none. Retell evaluates the outcomes when the chat closes, so timing is approximate. A chat with no reply counts as unanswered.
* A reply that arrives after the chat closes goes to the number's own inbound SMS agent.

SMS nodes need SMS-enabled numbers. See [Caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers) and [Enable SMS](/deploy/enable-sms). The chat agent must also be set to **AI speaks first**. If it's set to **User speaks first**, launch is blocked with "X is set to User speaks first, so it can't send the first SMS. Change it to AI speaks first."

## Outcomes

![Sequence canvas dimmed behind the open panel for Conversation 1, Outcomes tab, with the helper text These outcomes apply only to this conversation. The Interested outcome card shows Description on the Prompt tab with the text The contact is interested and wants a follow-up, Save outcome to contact field off, Next set to Conversation 2, and Add delay off. Below it, the built-in No Response outcome card shows its fixed description, Save outcome to contact field off, and Next set to Ends the sequence.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-outcome-card.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=8cb28acc213ad27c07eed9d72c9d8f4e)

A node outcome that routes Interested contacts to the next conversation node.

An outcome is one result of a conversation, such as "Booked" or "Not interested", and where that result sends the contact. There are two kinds:

* **Node outcomes** apply only to one conversation node. They're on the node's **Outcomes** tab.
* **Global outcomes** apply to every node. They're on the **Global** panel's **Outcomes** tab. A global outcome ends the sequence. To route one to another node, choose **Add Conversation Node** on it. Retell then moves it onto every conversation node, so you can set the next step on each node.

Each node also has two built-in outcomes:

* **Other outcome** sets where the contact goes when no outcome matches ("When no outcome matches, continue to:").
* **No Response** applies when the node runs out of attempts without a pickup or reply. You can change where it goes, but not its condition.

Each outcome card has these settings:

| Setting | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Description** | The condition, written as a **Prompt** or as **Metrics**. See [Write the condition](#write-the-condition). |
| **Save outcome to contact field** | Writes fixed values to the contact when the outcome applies. See [Save the outcome to a contact field](#save-the-outcome-to-a-contact-field). |
| **Next** | Where the contact goes. See the table below. |
| **Add delay** | Node outcomes only. Waits the minutes, hours, or days you set before the next node's first attempt. |

**Next** offers these destinations:

| Next | What happens to the contact |
| - | - |
| A conversation node | Starts that node at Attempt 1, after any delay, inside the calling window. |
| **Ends the sequence (Successful)** | Exits with stage **Completed** and counts as **Converted**. |
| **Ends the sequence** | Exits with stage **Completed**. |

In the dashboard, a node outcome can point to any conversation node except its own and the nodes that lead to it, so a sequence can't loop. Rename an outcome with its pencil icon, and delete it with its trash icon.

### Write the condition

Each outcome's **Description** has two tabs:

* **Prompt**: describe the result in plain words, such as "The lead booked an appointment." An LLM classifier reads the transcript, up to its last 100 entries, and picks the outcome whose description matches by meaning.
* **Metrics**: compare variables with values, in code rather than with an LLM. Choose **All** or **Any** "of the following conditions match", then add rows with **Add Condition**. Each row has a `{{variable}}`, an operator, and a **Value**. The operators are `=`, `≠`, `>`, `≥`, `<`, `≤`, **Contains**, **Does not contain**, **Exists**, and **Does not exist**.

Metrics read the conversation's [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables). These include the contact's fields as they were when the call was placed, such as `{{first_name}}` or a custom field, and values the agent collected during the call, such as with an [Extract Dynamic Variable tool](/build/single-multi-prompt/extract-dv). They also read the call's post-call analysis fields, such as `call_successful`, `user_sentiment`, and your custom analysis fields, plus `disconnection_reason` and `call_status`.

`=` and `≠` compare text and ignore case. `>`, `≥`, `<`, and `≤` need a number on both sides, so a value such as `$5,000` never matches.

> [!TIP]
>
> If a prompt outcome depends on a tool, such as a booking tool, describe the confirmed result: "The appointment was booked." The classifier needs the tool's result in the transcript to match, not only the agent's intent.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Every Metrics row needs a variable. Retell won't launch a campaign with an empty variable field. An empty **Value** is allowed and compares to an empty value.

### When are outcomes evaluated?

Retell evaluates outcomes when a person picked up the call, when the call reached an automated phone menu (IVR), or when the lead replied to the SMS. These attempts count as unanswered instead, and the contact moves to the node's next attempt without reaching **Other outcome**:

* No answer, a busy line, or a failed dial
* Voicemail
* An SMS with no reply
* A call where the conversation never got going, for example when someone else answered or the lead had no time to talk. The contact still counts as **Connected** in analytics.

A call that reaches an IVR has no conversation, so only a [Metrics outcome](#write-the-condition) can route it. Compare `{{disconnection_reason}}` to `ivr_reached` to send these contacts to another node, such as a retry with a different message. When no outcome matches, the call counts as unanswered and the node's next attempt follows.

A dial to a number that doesn't exist fails the contact with "Invalid phone number". A dial the carrier rejects fails it with "Destination not allowed". Either way, the contact's stage becomes **Failed** and it gets no more attempts.

### Evaluation order

When a person answered, Retell picks one outcome:

1. **Metrics** outcomes, in list order: the node's outcomes, then the global outcomes. The first one whose conditions match wins.
2. If none match, every **Prompt** outcome, node and global, goes to the classifier together. The classifier picks the best match.
3. If no outcome matches, or the classifier fails, the contact follows **Other outcome**.

You can't reorder outcomes, so list order is the order you added them. A call that the agent ends with [Do-not-contact Handling](/build/do-not-call) skips these steps and gets **Do Not Call** directly.

### Save the outcome to a contact field

Turn on **Save outcome to contact field** to write values to the workspace [contact](/features/contacts) when the outcome applies. Pick a contact field, enter a value of the field's type, and click **Add field** to write more than one.

* The outcome writes the value you enter, not data from the call.
* **Phone number** and **Contact memory** can't be written.
* For the same field, the outcome's value overwrites a value from a [post-call analysis mapping](/features/contacts#define-contact-fields).
* With a [CRM connected](/integrations/crm-overview), the change syncs out if the field is in your [CRM mappings](/integrations/crm-mappings).
* The change can enroll the contact in an [Auto-enroll campaign](/dialer/contacts) whose conditions it now matches.

To add a field without leaving the sequence, pick **Create contact field** in the field list. You need permission to manage contact fields.

### The Do Not Call outcome

Every sequence has a global **Do Not Call** outcome that you can't edit, rename, or delete. It sets the contact's **Do not call** field to true and ends the sequence, without counting as a successful exit. It applies when:

* The agent's [Do-not-contact Handling](/build/do-not-call) ends a call after the lead confirms a do-not-call request.
* The classifier matches its description, "The lead asked not to be called or contacted again."
* The lead replies to an SMS with an [opt-out keyword](/build/do-not-call#sms-opt-out-keywords) such as STOP.

To skip marked contacts in later campaigns, see [Compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks#do-not-call-requests-during-a-campaign).

## Calling hours

![Calling window section of the Global panel set to Custom per day. Sunday and Saturday have only an Add a time button, so no dialing happens on those days. Monday through Friday each have one window from 09:00 to 18:00 with a delete icon and an Add a time button. Below, the Holidays section shows Exclude holidays with a Set Up button.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u/images/dialer/dialer-calling-window.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=vuwPMEb2Qq5g6X0u\&q=85\&s=9e07017270e9d685a4aa299291fb2a83)

A calling window of 09:00 to 18:00 on weekdays, set with Custom per day.

Calling hours are on the **Global** panel's **Settings** tab. They apply to every call and SMS in the sequence.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Retell doesn't enforce legal calling hours, such as TCPA rules. Set a calling window that meets the rules for your contacts. See [what stays your responsibility](/dialer/compliance-checks#what-stays-your-responsibility).

### Timezone

* **Contact's local time** (Recommended): Retell works out each contact's time zone from the area code of their US or Canadian number. The zone is the area code's, which may not match where the person is. Other numbers, including US territory and toll-free numbers, use the **Otherwise** time zone, which defaults to Los Angeles.
* **Dynamic variable**: Retell reads a time zone name, such as `America/Chicago`, from a text contact field you pick. A contact with an empty or invalid value uses the **Otherwise** time zone.
* **Fixed timezone**: "Dial everyone on the same clock." Every contact uses the time zone you pick.

On campaign calls, the agent's clock uses the contact's time zone too, so the current time the agent sees and any callback time it collects are in the contact's local time.

### Calling window

Choose **Same every day** or **Custom per day**, then set start and end times in 15-minute steps. Click **Add a time** to add a second window to a day, for example to skip a lunch hour.

* A day with no window has no dialing.
* A window can't cross midnight. The end must be after the start, up to 24:00.
* Switching to **Same every day** copies Monday's windows to every day.

Retell applies the window like this:

* An attempt that comes due outside the window waits for the next opening. It doesn't use up an attempt.
* New dials stop 1 minute before the window closes. A call in progress isn't cut off.
* A callback for a time the lead asked for goes out at that time, even outside the window. See [Auto-schedule callbacks](#auto-schedule-callbacks).

### Holidays

Under **Exclude holidays:**, click **Set Up**:

* **Public holidays** lists US and Canadian public holidays for the next 12 months, on their calendar date rather than the observed weekday. Check the ones to skip, or click **Select all**.
* **Custom dates** adds a single date or a range.

Retell doesn't dial on these dates, judged by the contact's local date. One list applies to every contact, so a US holiday also pauses calls to Canadian contacts.

## Retries

Both retry settings are on the **Global** panel under **Automatic retries**, and both are on by default. They apply only to phone calls.

### Double dial

With **Double dial** on, a dial that goes unanswered gets a second dial right away. Each dial bills as a normal call. The second dial is part of the same attempt, and it never triggers a third. A voicemail that the agent hung up on counts as unanswered, so it gets a second dial.

The second dial goes out immediately, and Retell doesn't check it against the calling window or holidays again. Retell skips the double dial when:

* The agent left a voicemail message on the first dial.
* The call reached an automated phone menu (IVR). Retell [evaluates its outcome](#when-are-outcomes-evaluated) instead.
* The number doesn't exist or the carrier rejected it.
* The campaign is paused or stopped.
* You stopped the call manually, or the contact is no longer in progress.

### Auto-schedule callbacks

With **Auto-schedule callbacks** on, the agent handles callback requests on campaign calls. It works with agents that use a Retell LLM or a Conversation Flow. When a lead asks to be called back, the agent asks once for a time if they didn't give one, reads the time back, and ends the call. The request sets when the contact's next call goes out:

* **With a time**: at that time, even outside the calling window or on a holiday. The time is in the contact's time zone unless the lead names another, such as "3 PM Eastern".
* **Without a time**: at the first time inside the calling window that's at least 24 hours after the call.

A callback restarts the node's attempts from Attempt 1 at that time, whether or not the node has attempts left. If the call's outcome leads to another phone call node, the callback becomes that node's first attempt instead. Outcomes that lead to an exit or an SMS node aren't applied to a lead who asked for a callback.

With it off, the agent doesn't take callback requests on campaign calls.

## Examples

### Appointment reminders with an SMS follow-up

A dental clinic calls patients two days before their appointment, and texts a booking link to patients who need a new time.

* **Conversation 1** is a phone call node with the clinic's reminder agent. Attempt 1 runs **Immediately** and Attempt 2 **After** 4 hours, both with **Leave a voicemail** off. Attempt 3 runs **After** 1 day with a **Static sentence**: `Hi {{first_name}}, this is Bright Smile Dental confirming your cleaning on {{appointment_time}}. Please call us at 555-0134.` Here `appointment_time` is a Text contact field, such as "Tuesday, November 12 at 10 AM".
* The global **Success** description reads "The patient confirmed or booked an appointment."
* A node outcome, **Needs new time**, has the prompt "The patient can't make the appointment and wants to reschedule." Its **Next** is **Conversation 2**.
* **Conversation 2** is an SMS node with a chat agent that offers new times, with 1 attempt. If the patient replies and confirms a new time, the global **Success** outcome ends the sequence as successful. A patient who doesn't reply exits when the chat closes.
* The calling window is **Custom per day**: 9:00 to 17:00 on weekdays and 9:00 to 12:00 on Saturday.

A patient who never answers gets three attempts and then exits. The text goes only to patients who answered and asked for a new time.

### Lead qualification that updates a contact field

A software company qualifies new leads and hands the qualified ones to a demo-booking campaign.

* **Conversation 1** is a phone call node with a qualification agent pinned to a specific version. Its attempts run **Immediately**, then **After** 1 day and 3 days. The agent saves `budget` and `wants_demo` with an Extract Dynamic Variable tool.
* A node outcome, **Qualified**, uses **Metrics** with **All**: `{{wants_demo}} = true` and `{{budget}} ≥ 5000`. It saves `lead_status` = `Qualified` to the contact, and its **Next** is **Ends the sequence (Successful)**.
* A node outcome, **Send pricing**, has the prompt "The lead asked to receive pricing by text message." Its **Next** is **Conversation 2**, an SMS node with a chat agent that sends the pricing and answers questions.
* The global **Success** outcome is deleted, so only **Qualified** leads count as converted. **Not Interested** and **Do Not Call** stay.

Metrics outcomes run first, so a lead who meets both conditions is **Qualified** whatever the classifier would decide. An [Auto-enroll campaign](/dialer/contacts) with the condition `lead_status` equals `Qualified` then enrolls the lead and calls to book the demo.

## FAQ

> [accordion] Does the campaign retry when nobody answers or it reaches voicemail?
>
> Yes. With **Double dial** on, Retell redials once right away. If that dial goes unanswered too, the node's next attempt runs after its delay, inside the calling window. When the node has no attempts left, the contact exits. A voicemail counts as unanswered even when the agent leaves a message.

> [accordion] What is double dial, and does it cost extra?
>
> It places a second dial right after an unanswered one, as part of the same attempt. Each dial bills as a normal call. See [Double dial](#double-dial).

> [accordion] Can the agent call back on a date the lead asks for?
>
> Yes, with **Auto-schedule callbacks** on. The agent reads the time back, and the next call goes out then, even outside the calling window. The node's attempts start over from Attempt 1. See [Auto-schedule callbacks](#auto-schedule-callbacks).

> [accordion] Can I call each contact during their own local hours?
>
> Yes. Choose **Contact's local time** under **Timezone**, and Retell applies the calling window in each contact's time zone, worked out from the area code of their US or Canadian number. Other numbers use the **Otherwise** time zone.

> [accordion] What happens if a lead calls the campaign number back?
>
> If the contact is still waiting for an attempt on a phone call node, the node's agent answers and the call's outcomes apply as if the campaign had dialed. See [Answer callbacks to the campaign number](#answer-callbacks-to-the-campaign-number).

> [accordion] Can I send contacts who never answer to an SMS step?
>
> Yes. When the call node runs out of attempts, its **No Response** outcome applies. Change its **Next** to the SMS node. By default, **No Response** ends the sequence.

> [accordion] Can I edit the sequence after launch?
>
> No. The sequence locks when you launch or schedule the campaign. [Duplicate the campaign](/dialer/overview#pause-stop-duplicate-or-delete), edit the copy's sequence, and launch it.

Related: [Dialer overview](/dialer/overview), [choose contacts](/dialer/contacts), [compliance checks](/dialer/compliance-checks), [caller ID and pacing](/dialer/phone-numbers), and [handle voicemail and IVR](/build/handle-voicemail).


# Alert rules for call and chat metrics
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/features/alerting-overview

Create Retell AI alert rules that email or webhook you when call or chat volume, success rate, cost, latency, or API errors cross a threshold you set.

Alerting watches your call and chat metrics and notifies you the moment one crosses a threshold you set, so you catch a volume spike, a drop in success rate, or a wave of API errors without watching a dashboard. You define rules; Retell evaluates them on a schedule and sends an email or webhook when a rule triggers.

![Alerting page in the Retell dashboard showing the Alerts tab with three saved alert rules, each listing its metric and filters, and a Create Alert button in the top right corner.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/GWDpUspWhecmEo9X/images/alerting/rules-list.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=GWDpUspWhecmEo9X\&q=85\&s=62670e9d951df73617d1fb86d019acb2)

The Alerting page lists your saved rules on the Alerts tab.

## When to use it

Reach for alerting when you need to catch a change in your call or chat operations fast, without a person watching for it. Common cases:

* **Catch outages early.** Alert when call or chat success rate drops or API errors climb, so you react before customers complain.
* **Detect volume anomalies.** Alert on an unexpected spike or drop in call or chat volume, or when concurrency approaches your limit.
* **Control spend.** Alert when total call or chat cost over a window exceeds a budget.
* **Watch quality.** Alert on rising negative sentiment or a growing count of calls that fail QA.

Alerting evaluates *aggregate* metrics over a time window. It isn't built for reacting to a single call or chat; for per-session automation, send a [webhook](/features/webhook-overview) from the agent instead. To explore the same metrics interactively, use the [analytics dashboard](/features/analytics-dashboard).

> [!NOTE]
>
> Alerting is a dashboard feature. Rules are created and managed in the dashboard, not through the public API.

### Example

A support team wants to know the instant call quality slips. They create a rule on **Call success rate**, set it to trigger when the rate **is below 90%** over the last **1 hour**, checked every **5 minutes**, and add a webhook that posts to their on-call Slack channel. When success rate dips, the on-call engineer is paged within minutes instead of hearing about it from customers.

## Create an alert rule

Open the **Alerting** tab in the dashboard and select **Create Alert**.

![Create Alert dialog with an alert name field, a Time Configuration row reading 'Check every 5 min for the last 30 min', a metric-condition toggle between 'Compare to certain value' and 'Compare to last cycle', a metric dropdown set to Number of Calls with a 'when sum is above 2' condition, a Filter section with an agent picker defaulting to All Agents, and Notify via fields for email addresses and webhook URLs, each webhook URL having a Test button, with Cancel and Save buttons.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/ksPrWbndKPAvsxM-/images/alerting/create-rule.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=ksPrWbndKPAvsxM-\&q=85\&s=114aeb20d61e9feebdf61cf2166fbe52)

The Create Alert dialog, configuring a rule on call volume.

**1. Name the rule**

Give it a descriptive name, such as `Call success rate drop`. The name appears in every notification.

**2. Pick the metric and condition**

Choose the [metric](#metrics-you-can-monitor) to watch; the picker groups them into **API**, **Call**, **Chat**, and **QA**. Then pick a [threshold type](#thresholds): **Compare to certain value** (absolute) or **Compare to last cycle** (relative). Choose the comparator (for example, *is above* or *is below*) and enter the threshold value.

**3. Set the window and frequency**

Under **Time Configuration**, set how often the rule runs (**Check every**, the frequency) and how far back each check looks (**for the last**, the window). See [Evaluation window and frequency](#evaluation-window-and-frequency) for the valid combinations.

**4. Narrow with filters (optional)**

Restrict the metric to specific agents, agent [environment tags](/agent/version#environment-tags), disconnection reasons, API error codes, a QA cohort, or Post Call Extraction fields. See [Filters](#filters).

**5. Add notification channels**

Add one or more email addresses, webhook URLs, or both. At least one is required. Use **Test** next to a webhook URL to send a sample payload and confirm your endpoint accepts it before saving.

**6. Save**

Select **Save**. The rule starts evaluating on its next scheduled check.

## Metrics you can monitor

The `metric_type` value is what appears in the webhook payload.

| Metric | `metric_type` | What it measures |
| - | - | - |
| Number of calls | `call_count` | Count of calls that ended within the window. |
| Concurrency used | `concurrency_used` | Peak number of concurrent calls during the window. |
| Call success rate | `call_success_rate` | Percentage of calls marked successful (0–100). |
| Negative sentiment rate | `negative_sentiment_rate` | Percentage of calls with negative user sentiment (0–100). |
| Custom function latency | `custom_function_latency` | Average response time of custom function calls, in milliseconds. |
| Custom function failures | `custom_function_failure_count` | Number of custom function calls that failed. |
| Transfer call failures | `transfer_call_failure_count` | Number of call transfers that failed. |
| QA not passed | `qa_not_passed_count` | Number of analyzed calls in a QA cohort that did not pass. Requires a cohort. |
| Total call cost | `total_call_cost` | Total cost of calls in the window, in USD. |
| API error count | `api_error_count` | Number of API requests that returned an error status code. |
| Number of chats | `chat_count` | Count of chats that ended within the window. |
| Chat success rate | `chat_success_rate` | Percentage of chats marked successful (0–100). |
| Chat negative sentiment rate | `chat_negative_sentiment_rate` | Percentage of chats with negative user sentiment (0–100). |
| Total chat cost | `total_chat_cost` | Total cost of chats in the window, in USD. |

The metric decides which channel the rule watches. Call metrics aggregate over voice calls; chat metrics aggregate over [chat agent](/build/create-chat-agent) sessions, counting each chat when it ends, the same way call metrics count a call.

## Thresholds

Every rule uses one of two threshold types.

### Compare to certain value (absolute)

Compares the metric against a fixed number.

**Example:** trigger when `Number of calls` **is above** `100` in the last hour.

### Compare to last cycle (relative)

Compares the percentage change from the previous window against your threshold. Use it to catch sudden spikes or drops regardless of the baseline.

**Example:** trigger when `Number of calls` **increases by more than** `50%` compared to the previous hour.

The percentage change is calculated as:

```
((currentValue - previousValue) / previousValue) * 100
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If the previous window had zero activity and the current window has activity, the change is treated as an infinite increase and shown as `+∞%`. Rules that trigger on an increase (*increases by more than* or *increases by at least*) fire in this case.

## Evaluation window and frequency

The **window** is how far back each check looks when aggregating the metric. The **frequency** is how often the rule runs. A shorter window can only be paired with faster frequencies:

| Window | Supported frequencies |
| - | - |
| 1 minute | 1 minute |
| 5 minutes | 1 minute, 5 minutes |
| 30 minutes | 5 minutes, 30 minutes |
| 1 hour | 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour |
| 12 hours | 30 minutes, 1 hour, 12 hours |
| 24 hours | 1 hour, 12 hours, 24 hours |
| 3 days | 12 hours, 24 hours |
| 7 days | 24 hours |

> [!TIP]
>
> Pick a frequency that balances responsiveness against noise. Checking every minute catches issues fast but is more likely to trigger on a brief spike.

## Filters

Filters narrow what data feeds the metric. Which filters are available depends on the metric.

| Filter | Applies to | What it does |
| - | - | - |
| Agents | All metrics except Concurrency used, API error count, and QA not passed | Restrict the metric to specific agents, and optionally specific agent versions. The picker matches the metric's channel: chat metrics list chat agents, call metrics list voice agents. |
| Environment tags | Same metrics as the Agents filter | Restrict the metric to calls or chats handled by versions carrying the selected [environment tags](/agent/version#environment-tags), such as `prod` or `staging`. Select tags in the **Tags** section of the same agent picker; a tag applies across all agents that use it. |
| Disconnection reason | Number of calls | Count only calls that ended for the selected reasons (for example, User Hangup or Dial No Answer). |
| API error code | API error count | Count only requests that returned the selected HTTP status codes: `400`, `401`, `402`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `422`, `429`, `500`. |
| QA cohort | QA not passed | Choose which [QA cohort](/ai-qa/create-cohort) to watch. Required for this metric. |
| Post Call Extraction | Same metrics as the Agents filter | Filter calls or chats by [Post Call Extraction](/features/post-call-analysis-overview) fields, such as a boolean field `appointment_booked` set to `false`. |

## Notifications

When a rule triggers, Retell notifies every channel you configured. When a later check finds the condition no longer met, the incident resolves and the same channels are notified again.

### Email

Each recipient gets an email whose subject is `[Retell Alert] <rule name>`. The body includes the workspace, the metric, the value that triggered the alert, the threshold that was breached, the trigger time, and a link back to the dashboard. For most metrics it also links to the call history, chat history, or QA results behind the incident; Concurrency used and API error count have no drill-down. When the incident resolves, a follow-up email with subject `[Retell Alert Resolved] <rule name>` confirms it.

### Webhook

Each webhook URL receives a `POST` request. The body wraps the incident under an `alert` object:

```json theme={"dark"}
{
  "event": "alert_triggered",
  "alert": {
    "alert_incident_id": "alert_incident_0b1c2d3e4f5g6h7i8j9k0l1m",
    "org_id": "org_abc123",
    "alert_rule_id": "alert_rule_xyz789abcdef012345678901",
    "name": "High call volume",
    "metric_type": "call_count",
    "filter": {
      "agent": [{ "agent_id": "agent_abc123", "version": [3] }]
    },
    "threshold_type": "absolute",
    "threshold_value": 100,
    "comparator": "gt",
    "frequency": "5m",
    "window": "1h",
    "emails": ["oncall@yourcompany.com"],
    "webhook_urls": ["https://yourcompany.com/hooks/retell-alerts"],
    "current_value": 148,
    "previous_value": null,
    "triggered_timestamp": 1714608475945,
    "resolved_timestamp": null
  }
}
```

Key fields:

* `event` is `alert_triggered` when an incident opens. When it resolves, the same URLs receive a second request with `alert_resolved`.
* `filter` echoes the filters set on the rule. An environment-tag filter appears as `agent_tag`, for example `"agent_tag": { "type": "enum", "op": "in", "value": ["prod", "staging"] }`.
* `comparator` is one of `gt`, `lt`, `ge`, `le` (the symbol forms `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` are also accepted).
* `current_value` is the aggregated value that triggered the rule. `previous_value` is populated only for relative thresholds.
* For `total_call_cost` and `total_chat_cost`, `current_value`, `previous_value`, and `threshold_value` are in **cents** (the dashboard displays them as dollars).
* `triggered_timestamp` and `resolved_timestamp` are Unix timestamps in milliseconds. `resolved_timestamp` is `null` while the incident is active.

Each request carries an `X-Retell-Signature` header. Verify it before trusting the payload. Alert webhooks use the same HMAC-SHA256 scheme as other Retell webhooks, so the [webhook verification steps and code](/features/secure-webhook) apply here too. Retell sends each request once and waits up to **10 seconds** for a response; it does not retry, so acknowledge quickly and do heavy work asynchronously.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Always verify the webhook signature in production so you only act on requests that genuinely come from Retell.

## Alert history

Each time a rule's condition is met, Retell opens an **incident** and sends notifications. Incidents are listed under the **Alert History** tab, with the active period, the rule name, the condition, the value that triggered it, and the channels notified.

![Alert History tab listing past alert incidents in a table with columns for active period, alert name, condition, triggered value (for example '0 → 2 (+Infinity%)'), and notification channel.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/GWDpUspWhecmEo9X/images/alerting/incidents.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=GWDpUspWhecmEo9X\&q=85\&s=410cb741e4a2ed4bfa1557e6ad77caef)

The Alert History tab lists past incidents and the value that triggered each one.

Only one incident stays active per rule at a time. A new incident opens only after the previous one resolves.

## Limits

As of October 2026:

* Up to **20 alert rules** per workspace. Creating a 21st returns a `400` error.
* Up to **100 agents** in a single rule's agent filter.

## FAQ

> [accordion] How often are alerts evaluated?
>
> The system checks for due rules every minute and runs each one on its own configured frequency (1 minute to 24 hours). A rule with a 5-minute frequency is evaluated roughly every 5 minutes, not every minute.

> [accordion] Will I get repeated notifications for the same issue?
>
> No. A notification is sent once when a new incident opens, and once more when it resolves. You won't get repeat notifications while the condition persists.

> [accordion] What happens when I edit a rule?
>
> Editing a rule resets its evaluation schedule and clears any active incident, so it starts evaluating fresh on the next check. This prevents a stale incident from lingering after you've changed the condition.

> [accordion] What happens if an agent in a rule's filter is deleted?
>
> When you open the rule to edit it, Retell removes any agent that no longer exists from the Agents filter and shows a notice that some agents were removed. Select **Save** to keep the cleaned-up filter. The rule keeps evaluating on its remaining agents; a transient fetch error (not a deletion) leaves the agent in place so it isn't dropped by mistake.

> [accordion] Can I alert across multiple agents at once?
>
> Yes. Select multiple agents in the Agents filter and the metric is aggregated across all of them. Leave the filter empty to include every agent of the metric's channel. A single rule can't mix voice and chat agents; create one rule per channel instead.

> [accordion] Can I alert on chat agents?
>
> Yes. Pick one of the chat metrics (Number of chats, Chat success rate, Chat negative sentiment rate, or Total chat cost) and the rule evaluates chats instead of calls. Filters work the same way: narrow by chat agent, environment tag, or Post Call Extraction fields.


# Analytics dashboard
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/features/analytics-dashboard

Build custom Retell analytics dashboards to track call and chat metrics like success rate, latency, cost, and concurrency, with charts, filters, and breakdowns.

The Analytics dashboard charts your call and chat data so you can see how your agents are performing over time. Open it from the **Analytics** tab, build the charts you care about, then filter and break them down without leaving the page.

![Analytics page in the Retell dashboard with Call Dashboard and Chat Dashboard tabs, the date range picker, Filter and Breakdown controls, and an Add Chart button, above charts for call counts, call duration, call latency, concurrency used, call successful, disconnection reason, user sentiment, and phone inbound versus outbound.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/dashboard-overview.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=2d27d95f915313e9b2d3ef02b807860a)

A call dashboard with number, line, and donut charts.

## When to use it

Reach for the analytics dashboard when you want to see a pattern across many sessions rather than the detail of one:

* **Track performance over time.** Watch success rate, duration, or latency by day or week and see whether a prompt change moved them.
* **Compare agents or versions.** Break a metric down by agent or agent version to see which one performs better.
* **Watch spend.** Chart combined cost by agent or by day to see where your money goes.
* **Report on business outcomes.** Chart any [custom Post Call Extraction](/features/post-call-analysis-create) field, so "booked appointments" sits next to call volume.

It isn't the right tool for everything. To inspect one session's transcript or recording, use [call and chat history](/features/session-history). To be told when a metric crosses a line instead of checking for yourself, set up [alerting](/features/alerting-overview). To follow a call that's still running, use [live monitoring](/features/live-monitoring).

### Example

A clinic runs an appointment-reminder agent. They chart **Call Successful Rate** by day, break it down by agent version, and add a **Call Counts** chart filtered to the `voicemail_reached` disconnection reason. When a new version ships, the two charts show within a day whether more calls are landing in voicemail and whether the success rate followed.

To build or improve a dashboard by describing what you need, use [Conductor for analytics dashboards](/conductor/analytics-dashboards).

## Create a dashboard

Each dashboard is scoped to either call data or chat data, and the scope is fixed once you create it. You can keep up to **10 dashboards** per workspace; creating an 11th fails with "Dashboard limit reached."

**1. Add the dashboard**

Open the overflow menu next to **Add Chart**, choose **Add Dashboard**, then pick **Call** or **Chat**.

![Dashboard overflow menu open with Duplicate and Delete above Add Dashboard, whose submenu offers Call and Chat.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/add-dashboard.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=d48468c06c73da653474e9d12867888c)

Add Dashboard, where the call or chat scope is set for good.

**2. Name it**

Select the tab name and type a new one. Names are how you'll tell tabs apart, so prefer "Outbound sales" over "Dashboard 2".

**3. Arrange the tabs**

Drag tabs to reorder them. **Duplicate** in the overflow menu copies a dashboard with all of its charts, which is the quickest way to build a variant. **Delete** appears once you have more than one dashboard.

## Add a chart

**1. Open the chart editor**

Select **Add Chart**.

**2. Choose the graph type**

Set **Graph Type** to column, bar, line, donut, or number. Line suits trends over time; number suits a single headline figure.

**3. Pick the metric and measurement**

Choose a [metric](#metrics-you-can-chart) under **Call Source Metrics**, then how to measure it. The measurement list changes with the metric: counts offer only **count**, while durations and costs offer **avg**, **median**, **p90**, **sum**, **min**, and **max**. Use **+ Add** to plot more than one metric on the same chart.

**4. Set the time range and grouping**

Pick the chart's own range, or leave it on **Follow dashboard time range** so it moves with the picker at the top. The **Hour / Day / Week / Month** toggle sets the time bucket. Tick **Previous period comparison** to overlay the preceding window.

**5. Narrow it (optional)**

Add filters and up to five breakdowns that apply to this chart only. See [Filters and breakdowns](#filters-and-breakdowns).

**6. Save**

Save the chart. It lands at the end of the dashboard, where you can drag it into place.

![Chart editor showing Graph Type set to Column, Call Source Metrics set to Call Counts, Filter and Breakdown sections with Add buttons, a Last 4 weeks range with an Hour, Day, Week, Month toggle and a Previous period comparison checkbox, and a live preview of the resulting chart.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/chart-editor.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=fce2c285ddc025ab7e3f70f5295b6450)

The chart editor, with a live preview of the chart you're building.

## Metrics you can chart

Which metrics you get depends on whether the dashboard is scoped to calls or chats.

### Call metrics

| Metric | Measurements | What it covers |
| - | - | - |
| Call Counts | count | Number of calls. |
| Call Successful/Unsuccessful | count | Calls split by whether analysis marked them successful. |
| Call Status | count | Calls split by status. |
| Phone Inbound/Outbound | count | Calls split by direction. |
| Disconnection Reason | count | Calls split by why they ended. |
| User Sentiment | count | Calls split by the sentiment analysis assigned. |
| Call Successful Rate | avg | Share of calls marked successful. |
| Call Picked Up Rate | avg | Share of calls answered. |
| Call Transfer Rate | avg | Share of calls transferred. |
| Voicemail Rate | avg | Share of calls that reached [voicemail](/build/handle-voicemail). |
| Call Duration | avg, median, p90, sum, min, max | Length of calls. |
| End to End Latency | avg, median, p90, min, max | Per-call p50 [latency](/reliability/check-actual-latency), aggregated across calls. |
| Concurrency Used | max | Peak [concurrency](/deploy/concurrency) in the period. |
| Combined cost | avg, sum, median, p90, min, max | Total cost of the call. |

### Chat metrics

| Metric | Measurements | What it covers |
| - | - | - |
| Chat Counts | count | Number of chats. |
| Chat Successful/Unsuccessful | count | Chats split by whether analysis marked them successful. |
| Chat Status | count | Chats split by status. |
| User Sentiment | count | Chats split by the sentiment analysis assigned. |
| Chat Successful Rate | avg | Share of chats marked successful. |
| Combined cost | avg, sum, median, p90, min, max | Total cost of the chat. |

## Set the time range

The date range picker at the top of the page sets the window for every chart that follows the dashboard. Pick a preset (**Today**, **Last 7 days**, **Last 4 weeks**, **Last 3 months**, **Week to date**, **Month to date**, **Year to date**, **All time**) or select start and end dates on the calendar, then **Apply**. Each end of the range carries its own time and timezone, so buckets line up with your working day. Future dates are disabled.

![Date range picker open on the analytics dashboard showing presets from Today to All time down the left, two month calendars with a selected range, and start and end time fields each with a UTC-07 timezone selector, above Cancel and Apply buttons.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/date-range.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=0b7e9af211209109d65791a636304f85)

The dashboard date range, with presets, a calendar, and per-end timezones.

A chart can override that window with its own range: **Today**, **Last 1 week**, **Last 4 weeks**, **Last 3 months**, **Week to date**, **Month to date**, **Year to date**, or **All time**.

The range is saved with the dashboard, so each dashboard keeps its own window. A relative preset like **Last 4 weeks** or **Month to date** rolls forward, so a saved dashboard always shows the most recent window rather than the dates you first picked. Changing the range puts the header into its unsaved state, the same as a filter change (see [Filters and breakdowns](#filters-and-breakdowns)).

## Filters and breakdowns

Filters and breakdowns set in the header apply to every chart on the dashboard. Charts can add their own on top.

The filter list is split across four tabs. **Base** holds the built-in fields; **Post Call Extraction**, **Metadata**, and **Dynamic Variables** hold whatever your agents produce.

On a call dashboard, Base offers agent, call ID, batch call ID, type, duration, from number, to number, user sentiment, disconnection reason, call status, call successful, end-to-end latency, and combined cost. A chat dashboard offers agent, chat ID, chat status, chat successful, combined cost, and user sentiment.

![Filter panel open on the analytics dashboard with tabs for Base, Post Call Extraction, Metadata, and Dynamic Variables, and base filters listed for agent, call ID, batch call ID, type, duration, from, to, user sentiment, disconnection reason, call status, call successful, and E2E latency.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/filter.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=f2f92afb29ad16d3b188f4a967414205)

Filters, grouped into base fields and everything your agents produce.

**Breakdowns** group every chart by one or more dimensions: agent, agent version, disconnection reason, call status, call successful, call type, and Post Call Extraction fields. Chat dashboards offer agent, agent version, disconnection reason, chat status, chat successful, and Post Chat Extraction fields.

![Breakdown menu open on the analytics dashboard listing Agent, Agent Version, Disconnection Reason, Call Status, Call Successful, Call Type, and Post Call Extraction Field.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/breakdown.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=2487694a69a5748a40bbb0981a1753a9)

Breakdowns split each chart by a dimension such as agent or version.

Filter, breakdown, and date-range changes aren't saved for you. When you change one, **Save** and **Cancel** replace the usual controls in the header: save to keep the state for next time, cancel to revert to the last saved state. Moving and resizing charts saves on its own.

![Analytics dashboard after adding an agent breakdown, with Cancel and Save buttons shown in the header where Add Chart normally sits.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ/images/analytics/save-cancel.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=2HwuM2BExfFOy7pJ\&q=85\&s=675d27c85d7b3961a82addac1ae6d43f)

Changing a filter or breakdown puts the header into its unsaved state.

### Per-chart filters and breakdowns

Each chart can carry its own filters and up to five breakdowns, set in the chart editor. Chart filters are merged with the dashboard filters rather than replacing them, so both apply. Use them to narrow one chart without touching the rest of the dashboard.

Any field from your [custom Post Call Extraction](/features/post-call-analysis-create) can drive a chart, which is how you track business-specific outcomes next to the standard metrics.

## Chart types and layout

Five chart types are available: **column** for comparing categories, **bar** for the same comparison horizontally, **line** for trends over time, **donut** for proportions, and **number** for a single figure.

Arrange charts directly on the dashboard, without opening the editor:

* Drag a chart to move it within a row or into another row. A row holds up to five charts.
* Drag the divider between two charts to change their widths.
