## FAQ

> [accordion] Does a Retell agent sound like a real person?
>
> Yes. Retell agents use natural-sounding voices and handle turn-taking and interruptions the way a person would, so they don't talk over callers. Pick a voice from the [platform voices](/build/platform-voices), and turn on [expressive mode](/build/expressive-mode) for more natural pacing.

> [accordion] Is Retell HIPAA compliant?
>
> Yes, with a signed BAA before you send protected health information. Retell is also SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2 certified and GDPR compliant. See [compliance](/general/compliance).

> [accordion] What happens when the agent can't handle a call?
>
> It [transfers the call](/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call) to a person, either right away or after briefing them with a warm transfer.

> [accordion] Can I keep my existing phone numbers?
>
> Yes. Connect your provider with [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony), or [buy a number](/deploy/purchase-number) from Retell.

## How does a voice agent work?

Every Retell agent runs on four layers:

> [card] Telephony
>
> The call arrives by phone number, SIP trunk, or web.

> [card] Speech to text
>
> The caller's audio is transcribed as they talk.

> [card] LLM
>
> The model picks the reply, using your prompt and tools.

> [card] Text to speech
>
> The reply streams back to the caller as audio.

> [!TIP]
>
> Retell handles turn-taking, interruptions, and background noise between the layers. See the [orchestration overview](/general/orchestration_overview) for how they fit together.


# ChatGPT
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/chatgpt

Install the Retell AI ChatGPT app, connect with OAuth, and build, test, deploy, and monitor voice agents from a ChatGPT conversation.

Install the **Retell AI** app in ChatGPT to build, edit, deploy, test, and monitor [voice agents](/build/choose-agent-type) from a conversation. Interactive widgets open in chat for workspace selection, agent creation, voice preview, testing, deployment, and analytics.

For Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and other MCP clients that use an API key, see the [Retell MCP server](/get-started/mcp-server).

## When to use it

Use the ChatGPT app when you want to:

* Build or edit agents in natural language without opening the Retell dashboard for every change
* Preview voices, run playground chats, and place test calls from the same conversation
* Deploy an agent to a phone number and check call analytics without leaving ChatGPT

Prefer the [MCP server](/get-started/mcp-server) when your client is Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex and you already manage Retell with an API key. Prefer the dashboard when you need full editor controls, conversation-flow graphs, or settings the ChatGPT widgets do not expose.

### Example

A cafe owner asks ChatGPT to create a friendly receptionist that answers menu and hours questions, transfers frustrated callers to a manager, then deploys the agent to their Retell number — all from one chat after connecting Retell AI once.

## Before you start

* A ChatGPT account on a plan that supports plugins and apps. Availability depends on your plan, region, and workspace settings; the app may not be available on the free tier.
* Permission to install plugins or apps. On ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, or Edu, an admin may need to enable **Retell AI** first.
* A Retell account at [retellai.com](https://www.retellai.com) with at least one workspace
* For live test calls and deployment: a [Retell phone number](/deploy/purchase-number), and a destination number in E.164 format such as `+15551234567`

> [!NOTE]
>
> Use your own Retell account, workspaces, agents, and phone numbers. The screenshots use sample or masked values.

## Install Retell AI from ChatGPT

Retell AI is listed in the ChatGPT plugin directory (some accounts still show **Apps**). The steps are the same either way, and existing connections keep working.

**1. Open the ChatGPT directory**

In ChatGPT, open **Settings → Plugins** or **Settings → Apps**, or go to [chatgpt.com/apps](https://chatgpt.com/apps/). Search for **Retell AI**.

![ChatGPT plugin or app directory showing the Retell AI listing](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-1.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=fcf5a077fe0174377c40c38ae69f53c8)

Search the ChatGPT directory for Retell AI.

**2. Install and connect**

Open the **Retell AI** listing and review its capabilities, terms, and privacy policy. Select **Install plugin** if it appears, then select **Connect**.

If **Connect** is greyed out or says **Disabled by admin**, ask a workspace admin to enable Retell AI in **Workspace settings → Plugins** or **Workspace settings → Apps**.

**3. Sign in to Retell**

Complete the Retell sign-in screen. Use the Retell account that owns the workspaces and agents you want to manage from ChatGPT.

**4. Approve access**

Review the requested access and approve it. This lets ChatGPT manage agents, phone number assignments, and call data in your Retell account on your behalf.

## Add Retell AI to a conversation

Installing the app is not enough. Enable it in the chat where you want to use it.

**1. Start a new chat**

Return to ChatGPT and start a new conversation on a supported surface, such as ChatGPT on the web or the desktop app.

**2. Enable Retell AI in the chat**

Select the **+** button next to the message box, then **More**, then **Retell AI**. You can also type `@` and select **Retell AI**.

If Retell AI does not appear in the list, the app is not installed for this account. Repeat the install and connect steps above.

![ChatGPT composer plus menu showing Retell AI under More](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-2.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=f363aad27025e66b922597446f590e7f)

Enable Retell AI from the composer plus menu.

## Select a Retell workspace

Your workspace determines which agents, phone numbers, and call history ChatGPT can see.

* If your account has **one** workspace, Retell selects it automatically.
* If your account has **multiple** workspaces, a workspace selector appears the first time a tool needs one.

**1. Ask ChatGPT to load your workspaces**

In a chat with Retell AI enabled, enter:

```text theme={"dark"}
Show me my Retell workspaces.
```

**2. Choose the workspace**

In the **Select a workspace to continue** widget, open the dropdown, choose the workspace that holds your agents, and confirm. Later actions use this workspace until you change it.

![Retell workspace selector widget in ChatGPT with a workspace chosen](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-3.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=43b5e6e13ea0120587b810a5faa1d79f)

Select the Retell workspace for this conversation.

To change workspaces later, ask ChatGPT to switch the selected Retell workspace and the same selector reopens.

## Review existing agents

**1. Open the agent list**

Ask ChatGPT to list your agents. The **Your Agents** widget shows each agent's name, ID, voice, and language. You can search by name or ID, copy an agent ID, or open the agent in the Retell dashboard.

```text theme={"dark"}
List all of my Retell agents.
```

![Retell Your Agents widget listing agents in the selected workspace](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-4.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=c604a628c7bd49c8196da14ce99ac310)

Browse agents in the selected workspace.

If the list is empty, confirm you selected the intended workspace, then create an agent in the next section.

## Build a voice agent

The build wizard collects the agent summary, voice, optional functions, end-call behavior, and a generated prompt, then creates the agent in Retell.

**1. Start the builder**

Describe the agent you want. For example:

```text theme={"dark"}
Create a customer support agent for my coffee shop. It should be friendly, answer questions about the menu and hours, and transfer to a human if the caller gets frustrated.
```

ChatGPT opens the agent creation widget on the summary step.

![Retell agent creation widget summary step inside ChatGPT](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-5.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=78c44d217b436fd58d8f49d8fda4482e)

Agent creation starts on the summary step.

**2. Review the agent summary**

Confirm the **Agent Name**, description, use cases, target audience, tone, style, and language. Edit any field before you continue.

The ChatGPT builder offers English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. For the full set of languages Retell agents support across providers, see [language support](/build/language-support).

**3. Choose a voice**

Pick a voice from the recommended set or the full catalog, and play the audio preview before confirming.

![Retell voice selection step showing voice cards with audio previews](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-6.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=2eb079a74d369060eca7e8c646968342)

Preview and select a voice for the agent.

**4. Enable optional functions**

Turn on the functions this agent needs. Core options include [Transfer Call](/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call) and Book Calendar Events ([Cal.com](/integrations/cal-com)). Advanced options can include [press digit](/build/single-multi-prompt/press-digit) for IVR navigation, custom API tools, extract variables, agent swap, and [send SMS](/deploy/enable-sms).

Each function you enable gets its own configuration step later in the wizard.

![Retell additional functions step with Transfer Call and Cal.com toggles](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-7.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=bc216082f048997a17c2cc11932a3b7d)

Turn on Transfer Call, Cal.com, and other optional functions.

**5. Set when the call should end**

In **End Call Setup**, describe when the agent should hang up — for example, once the caller's request is handled or the caller says goodbye.

**6. Review the prompt and create the agent**

Review the generated system prompt, adjust it if needed, and create the agent.

On success the widget shows the agent name, ID, voice, and creation time, with a link to open the agent in the Retell dashboard.

![Retell agent created confirmation card with agent ID and next step](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-8.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=c953f062540efb8814fa688d251d1eaf)

Confirm the new agent and open it in the dashboard if needed.

![Retell agent created confirmation card with agent ID and next step](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-9.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=6df1a354505d9f9cbdfe02f4709218ea)

Confirm the new agent and open it in the dashboard if needed.

The success card suggests the next prompt:

```text theme={"dark"}
Deploy my agent to a phone number
```

You can also ask ChatGPT to change the voice, language, instructions, or call handling before deploying.

## Test the agent

Test the conversation flow in chat first, then place a live phone call.

**1. Open the test widget**

Ask ChatGPT to test the agent. For example:

```text theme={"dark"}
Let me test my new agent. Start a conversation as if I am calling about store hours.
```

The **Test Agent** widget opens with a live chat against the agent playground.

**2. Chat with the agent**

Type a caller message and send it, then continue for several turns. If the simulated call ends, select **Restart Conversation** to start over.

**3. Place a real test call**

Under **Real Call Test**, select a **From Phone Number** from your Retell numbers, enter a **To Phone Number** in E.164 format such as `+15551234567`, then select **Call**. Answer the destination phone and speak with the agent.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A live test call requires at least one Retell phone number. If no numbers appear, [purchase a number](/deploy/purchase-number) in the Retell dashboard first.

![Retell Test Agent widget showing a playground chat with the agent](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-10.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=0566a711d890b6cc468077b99093ca61)

Chat with the agent in the playground widget.

After testing, a common follow-up prompt is `Help me improve my agent's responses`.

## Deploy the agent to a phone number

Deployment assigns the agent to inbound and outbound numbers in the selected workspace.

**1. Open the deployment widget**

Ask ChatGPT to deploy the agent:

```text theme={"dark"}
Deploy my agent to a phone number
```

![Retell deploy agent widget listing available inbound and outbound phone numbers](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF/images/chatgpt/screenshot-11.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=p_O04fuvw5F8FsaF\&q=85\&s=7a99577e4001c9d7451a39ff69a1361a)

Choose inbound and outbound numbers for the agent.

**2. Assign inbound and outbound numbers**

Select an inbound number, an outbound number, or both, then confirm. Numbers already assigned to another agent are labeled **In Use**. You can use the same number for both directions, or leave one direction unassigned.

**3. Buy a number if none are available**

If the widget shows **No Phone Numbers Available**, open the [phone numbers](https://dashboard.retellai.com/phoneNumbers) page in the dashboard, add a payment method, and [purchase a number](/deploy/purchase-number). Enter your email and select **Send Link** if you want the dashboard link emailed to you. After buying, select **Refresh** and deploy again.

To confirm later, ask ChatGPT whether the agent is deployed — it reports the inbound and outbound assignments.

## Review call analytics

Once the agent has call history, open analytics from the conversation.

**1. Open the analytics dashboard**

Ask ChatGPT for performance data. For example:

```text theme={"dark"}
Show me call analytics for [agent name] from the last 7 days.
```

The dashboard shows total calls, success rate, average duration, sentiment distribution, and recent calls. You can filter by time range, call type, status, direction, and sentiment.

**2. Open a call transcript and recording**

Select a call in the recent calls table, or ask ChatGPT for the details of the most recent call. The detail view includes the transcript, summary, sentiment, duration, and recording playback when a recording exists.

## Edit an existing agent

Ask ChatGPT to change one part of the agent at a time. A confirmation widget shows the change so you can verify it.

```text theme={"dark"}
Rename my support agent to Bella's Bistro Receptionist.
```

```text theme={"dark"}
Update the prompt to handle complaints: apologize, offer a 10% discount, and escalate to a manager if the caller is still unhappy.
```

```text theme={"dark"}
Add a transfer call function that transfers to +15551234567 with a warm transfer when the caller asks for a manager.
```

```text theme={"dark"}
Change the agent's voice. Show me the available voices so I can preview them.
```

You can also update end-call behavior, Cal.com booking, custom API functions, extract variables, agent swap, SMS, IVR press-digit navigation, and dynamic variables such as business hours or address. For multilingual setup in the dashboard, see [Configure a multilingual agent](/agent/multilingual).

> [!NOTE]
>
> Retell validates transfer destinations and rejects reserved example exchanges such as `555` numbers, so use a real E.164 number. Editing transfer settings does not place a call on its own.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deleting an agent from ChatGPT is permanent for that agent in Retell. Confirm the agent name and ID in the approval prompt before you approve the delete.

## What you can do in ChatGPT

| Task | Example prompt |
| - | - |
| Select or switch workspace | `Show my Retell workspaces and switch to [workspace name].` |
| List agents | `List all of my Retell agents.` |
| Build an agent | `Create a friendly restaurant receptionist that takes reservations.` |
| Preview voices | `Show me the available voices. I want to hear what they sound like.` |
| Edit prompt, voice, or tools | `Update my support agent to transfer to +15551234567 when the caller asks for a manager.` |
| Test in chat | `Let me test this agent before deploying it.` |
| Place a test call | `Call my phone from the agent so I can hear it.` |
| Deploy | `Deploy this agent for inbound calls.` |
| Check deployment | `Is my agent deployed to any phone numbers?` |
| Analytics | `How did my Sales Assistant perform over the last 7 days?` |
| Delete an agent | `Delete the [agent name] agent.` |

## Verify setup

* Retell AI is installed from the ChatGPT directory and connected to the correct Retell account.
* Retell AI is enabled in the current conversation through **+ → More → Retell AI** or an `@` mention.
* The intended workspace is selected.
* An agent can be listed, opened in the builder or editor, and tested in the chat widget.
* If you deployed, the agent is assigned to the intended inbound and outbound numbers.
* If the agent has call history, analytics and transcripts load for it.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Resolution |
| - | - |
| Retell AI is not in the directory | Confirm your ChatGPT plan, region, and workspace allow plugins or apps. On Business, Enterprise, or Edu, ask an admin to enable the app. |
| **Connect** is disabled or says **Disabled by admin** | Ask a workspace admin to enable Retell AI in **Workspace settings → Plugins** or **Apps**. |
| The app is connected but nothing happens in chat | Add Retell AI to the conversation with **+ → More → Retell AI**, or start a new chat and `@` mention it. |
| Sign-in fails or access expires | Reconnect from the ChatGPT directory and complete the Retell authorization again. |
| Wrong Retell account | Disconnect the app, then connect again with the account that owns the target workspace. |
| Multiple workspaces and nothing loads | Complete the workspace selector, or ask ChatGPT to switch workspaces. |
| No agents found | Confirm the selected workspace, then create an agent if the workspace is empty. |
| Voice preview does not play | Allow audio playback in the browser and try another voice. Reopen the voice step if the widget was interrupted. |
| No phone numbers for deployment or test calls | [Purchase a number](/deploy/purchase-number) in the Retell dashboard, then select **Refresh** in the deploy or test widget. |
| Test call does not ring | Use E.164 format with a leading plus and country code, and select a valid **From** number from your Retell account. |
| ChatGPT asks for approval on every change | Expected for write actions such as create, deploy, call, and delete. Approve the action, or adjust app permissions only if your security policy allows it. |
| Analytics are empty | The agent needs completed calls. Place a test call, wait for analysis to finish, then reopen analytics. |
| Widgets do not render | Use ChatGPT on the web or desktop in a supported chat, and start a new conversation with Retell AI enabled. |

## FAQ

> [accordion] Is this the same as the Retell MCP server?
>
> Related, but different setup. The ChatGPT app is a packaged integration with OAuth and inline widgets. The [MCP server](/get-started/mcp-server) connects clients like Cursor and Claude Desktop with your Retell API key and the `https://mcp.retellai.com` endpoint.

> [accordion] Do I need an API key or webhook?
>
> No. ChatGPT connects through OAuth. API keys and webhooks are used by other integrations such as [Slack](/integrations/slack-marketplace) and [Notion](/integrations/notion-marketplace), and by the [MCP server](/get-started/mcp-server).

> [accordion] Why is Retell AI installed but not working in my chat?
>
> Install connects your account; each conversation still needs Retell AI enabled via **+ → More → Retell AI** or an `@` mention. Start a new chat if an older thread does not pick up the app.

> [accordion] How do I switch Retell accounts?
>
> Disconnect Retell AI from the ChatGPT directory or Apps/Plugins settings, then connect again and sign in with the Retell account that owns the workspace you need.

> [accordion] Can I use this on ChatGPT mobile?
>
> Use ChatGPT on the web or desktop for the install flow and interactive widgets. Mobile support depends on OpenAI's app surface and may not render every widget.

* [Transfer Call](/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call) — route callers to a human

# Claude connector
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/claude

Add the Retell AI connector to Claude to build, edit, deploy, test, and analyze voice agents from a chat, with OAuth sign-in and interactive widgets.

The **Retell AI** connector lets you build, edit, deploy, test, and analyze [voice agents](/build/choose-agent-type) from a conversation with Claude. You sign in with your Retell login, and multi-step tasks such as building, deploying, and testing an agent open as interactive widgets inside the chat.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page covers the Retell AI connector in Claude's connectors directory, which signs in with OAuth. For Cursor, Claude Code, Claude Desktop config files, and other MCP clients that use a Retell API key, see the [Retell MCP server](/get-started/mcp-server).

## When to use it

Use the connector when you want to describe an agent in plain language and have Claude set it up, or make quick changes to an existing agent without opening the dashboard.

Use the [dashboard](https://dashboard.retellai.com) instead when you need settings the widgets don't expose, such as [conversation flow](/build/conversation-flow/overview) agents, knowledge bases, [integrations](/integrations/overview), or credentials for custom functions. The connector builds single-prompt agents. It can't edit conversation flow agents.

### Example

A restaurant owner asks Claude for a receptionist agent for Bella's Bistro that takes reservations and answers questions about the menu and opening hours. Claude opens the build wizard with those details filled in, writes the prompt, lets them pick a voice, and creates the agent. They then put it on the restaurant's Retell number and place a test call to their own phone.

## Before you start

* A Retell account at [dashboard.retellai.com](https://dashboard.retellai.com) with at least one workspace.
* A Claude account. On Free, Pro, and Max plans you connect directly. On Team and Enterprise plans, an organization owner adds the connector under **Organization settings > Connectors** first, and then each member connects with their own Retell login. See [Use connectors](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities). The widgets render in Claude on the web and in Claude Desktop.
* To deploy an agent or place a call, a [Retell phone number](/deploy/purchase-number) in the workspace. Outbound calls also require [KYC](/accounts/kyc), which some accounts pass automatically.
* Usage through the connector is billed to your Retell workspace like any other usage. Test calls and test chats cost the same as live ones. See [Testing pricing](/test/testing-pricing).

## Connect Retell AI to Claude

**1. Find the connector**

In Claude, open **Customize > Connectors**, browse the directory, and search for **Retell AI**.

**2. Sign in to Retell**

Select **Connect** and sign in with the email you use for the Retell dashboard. The connector uses OAuth 2.0, so Claude never sees your Retell password.

**3. Pick a workspace**

If your login belongs to one workspace, the connector selects it for you. If it belongs to several, Claude shows the list and asks which one to use. The choice is saved for your login and carries over to new chats. To change it later, ask Claude to switch to another workspace by name.

You don't need to configure anything else. The connector finds your workspaces, agents, and phone numbers on its own.

To disconnect, remove the connector in Claude's connector settings. Claude then has no access to your Retell account until you connect again.

## What you can do

* **Build an agent.** A wizard collects the agent's name, purpose, audience, tone, and language, writes a prompt, lets you pick a voice with audio previews, and adds functions such as [call transfer](/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call), custom API calls, data extraction, agent swap, [SMS](/deploy/enable-sms), and [press digit](/build/single-multi-prompt/press-digit).
* **Edit an agent.** Change the voice, name, language, or prompt. Prompt changes appear side by side with the current prompt before you apply them. You can also set default values for [dynamic variables](/build/dynamic-variables) and add, change, or remove functions.
* **Deploy an agent.** Assign the agent to one of your Retell numbers for inbound calls, outbound calls, or both. The deploy screen shows which agent is on each number today.
* **Test an agent.** Chat with the agent in text, or have it place a real phone call from one of your numbers after you confirm the details.
* **Analyze calls.** Filter call history, open a call's transcript, recording, and analysis, and see call volume, success rate, sentiment, and latency for an agent.

![Retell AI build wizard in Claude with the Build step complete on a Build, Deploy, Test, Iterate progress bar. A card confirms the agent Bella's Bistro Receptionist was created with the voice Leland, and a Next card suggests deploying it to a phone number with a View in Retell Dashboard button.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hQyUQlPI9TMGXA-h/images/claude/build-wizard.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hQyUQlPI9TMGXA-h\&q=85\&s=832396c4ff6adc410864f5658206c267)

The build wizard after Claude creates an agent.

![Retell AI Test Agent widget in Claude showing a text conversation where a caller named Sam asks to book a dental cleaning and the agent asks whether they are a new patient, which days suit them, and for their name, date of birth, and callback number.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hQyUQlPI9TMGXA-h/images/claude/test-chat.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hQyUQlPI9TMGXA-h\&q=85\&s=74dc59fc49048dfa5849218559a2d797)

A text test chat with an agent.

![Retell AI analytics widget in Claude for The Experts Clinic Agent over the last 30 days, showing 4 total calls, a 50.0% success rate, a 1m 38s average duration, 988 ms end-to-end latency, and disconnection reasons split between agent hangup and user hangup.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/hQyUQlPI9TMGXA-h/images/claude/analytics.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=hQyUQlPI9TMGXA-h\&q=85\&s=bd69f1ac1354181b209a2b814b991d4f)

Call analytics for an agent over the last 30 days.

Calendar booking and other connected apps are set up on the **Integrations** page in the dashboard, not through the connector. After you connect a provider there, you can add its functions to any agent in the dashboard. See [Integrations](/integrations/overview).

The connector doesn't take credentials in the chat. It never asks for a Cal.com key or another integration's credentials. For custom functions, you add HTTP headers and query parameters, which often hold API keys, in the dashboard after the agent is created, and the connector refuses a function URL that contains a password, a key-like parameter (in the query or after `#`), a value that looks like an API key, or a webhook secret in its path (Slack, Discord, Zapier, Make, Telegram, IFTTT, Microsoft Teams). It checks when it creates an agent, when it adds or edits a custom function, and before it fills in a widget. A new dynamic variable value that looks like an API key is refused too, and a function with credentials saved in the dashboard can only be moved, from the chat, to another `https://` address on the same host.

## Usage examples

**Build an agent.** "Build me a receptionist agent for a dental clinic. It should answer questions about hours and insurance and transfer billing questions to the front desk."
Claude opens the build wizard with those details filled in and writes a prompt. You pick a voice and review the functions, and the connector creates the agent in your workspace.

**Edit the prompt.** "Show me the prompt for my receptionist agent and make it more concise."
Claude shows the current prompt next to the shorter version. Nothing changes until you apply it.

**Deploy to a number.** "Put my receptionist agent on my Retell number for inbound calls."
The deploy screen lists your numbers and the agent on each one. If another agent already answers the number you pick, you confirm the replacement before it happens.

**Test with a phone call.** "Have my receptionist agent call my phone at +14155551234 so I can hear it."
Claude shows the agent, the number it calls from, and the number it calls, and waits for you to confirm before Retell dials.

**Review calls.** "How did my receptionist agent do this week? Show me the calls that failed."
The analytics view shows call volume, success rate, duration, and latency, and you can open any call's transcript and recording.

## Which actions ask for confirmation?

Three actions take effect outside Claude, so the connector runs them in two steps. The first step returns a preview and changes nothing. The action only runs after you confirm. You confirm a call in the test widget or in the chat, a deletion in the chat, and a number replacement in the deploy widget.

| Action | What the preview shows | What happens when you confirm |
| - | - | - |
| Place an outbound call | The agent, the number it calls from, and the number it calls | Retell dials the number. The person who answers talks to your agent. |
| Delete an agent | The agent's name and any phone numbers routed to it | The agent is deleted permanently, and those numbers are left without an agent. |
| Deploy to a number another agent already uses | The agent on the number today, with each agent's share of calls if the number splits them | Your agent replaces it on that number immediately. |

A confirmation covers only the exact request in its preview, in the same workspace, and works once, even if the same request arrives twice. If anything in the request changes, or the confirmation is older than 2 minutes for a call or 5 minutes for a deletion or replacement, the connector asks again.

The connector checks that a confirmation matches its preview, but it can't tell whether you or Claude sent it. Claude asks for your approval in the chat before it confirms, so read the preview before you approve.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deleting an agent can't be undone. Check the numbers listed in the preview first, because they stop answering with an agent once it is deleted.

### Outbound calls

Outbound calls from the connector are meant for testing an agent, usually by calling your own phone. The connector can't verify that a number belongs to you, so it doesn't limit calls to your own numbers. Instead, every call needs your confirmation of the exact destination, and the checks below apply. The call goes from a Retell number in the selected workspace to the number you give, in E.164 format such as `+14155551234`. Before it shows the preview, the connector checks that:

* Both numbers are valid and different, and the from number belongs to the workspace.
* The destination isn't a premium-rate number (the US and Canada 900 area code and 976 local exchanges, and the international +979 range), a shared-cost or satellite number (+808, +870, +881, +882, +883), or a +1 number outside the US and Canada, such as Jamaica (+1 876) or the Dominican Republic (+1 809). US territories such as Puerto Rico and Guam can be called.

Retell then refuses the call if the destination is on the workspace's do-not-call list, and runs its own checks, including [KYC](/accounts/kyc).

The connector allows 20 outbound calls per hour per Retell login (as of October 2026). To place more, or to call a number the connector refuses, use the [dashboard or the API](/deploy/outbound-call).

You're responsible for having the consent the law requires to call a number with an AI agent. See Retell's [Terms of Service](https://www.retellai.com/legal/terms-of-service).

### AI disclosure

Agents you build through the connector tell callers they're an AI in two ways:

* **At the start of every call.** The agent's opening message is "Hi, this is an AI assistant. How can I help you today?" You can ask Claude for a different opening when you build the agent, or change it in the dashboard later. Keep the disclosure in it, because some jurisdictions require it.
* **When asked.** The **AI Disclosure When Asked** preset in the [Agent Handbook](/build/agent-handbook) is on, the same default as agents built in the dashboard. The agent says it's a virtual assistant whenever a caller asks if they're talking to a person. To review it, open the agent in the dashboard and select **Agent Handbook** in the prompt section.

Agents built in the dashboard keep their own settings when you deploy or test them through the connector.

## What data does the connector use?

The connector runs on Retell's infrastructure and calls the Retell API on your behalf. Retell's [privacy policy](https://www.retellai.com/legal/privacy-policy) applies.

* **Your Retell login.** Sign-in uses OAuth 2.0 through Retell's identity provider. The connector uses the access token to call the Retell API during the session and doesn't store it. It reads your login's name, email address, and whether the email is verified, to send you the dashboard link when you ask and to identify your account in Retell's product analytics (Mixpanel). It caches these for up to 24 hours.
* **Agent configuration.** Names, prompts, voices, phone numbers, and functions are read from and written to the Retell API.
* **OpenAI.** Four tools use OpenAI to write or rewrite prompt text: `generate_prompt`, `refine_prompt`, `preview_agent_prompt_edit`, and `show_prompt_preview`. When generating a prompt they send the agent's name, description, use cases, audience, tone, style, and language. When editing one they send the current prompt and your change request. Anything written in that text, including phone numbers, goes to OpenAI. Call transcripts and recordings aren't sent.
* **Email.** `send_dashboard_link` sends one email to the verified address on your Retell login, up to 3 times an hour. You can't give it another address.
* **Stored by the connector.** Your workspace selection and Claude's OAuth client registration are kept in a database for as long as your connection is active. Unsaved widget drafts and test chat transcripts are held in memory for up to 24 hours, and the counts behind the hourly limits for up to an hour. A used confirmation is remembered until it would have expired.
* **Logs and analytics.** For each tool call, the connector records the tool name, timing, whether it succeeded, the error message if it failed, your login and workspace IDs, and the shape of the input. The shape keeps field names, on and off settings, numbers, and the voice and language. Every other text value, such as prompts, phone numbers, and messages, is replaced by its length. These records go to Retell's logging service (Axiom) and to Mixpanel.
* **Deleting your data.** Remove the connector in Claude to end the connection. To have Retell delete data it holds about you, email [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com). The [privacy policy](https://www.retellai.com/legal/privacy-policy) describes the process.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
| - | - |
| "Authorization with the MCP server failed" when connecting | Sign in with the email you use for the Retell dashboard. If it still fails, remove the connector in Claude and connect again. |
| A tool is missing, or the tools look out of date | Disconnect and reconnect the connector in Claude's settings to refresh the tool list. |
| A widget shows "Waiting for agent data" or stays blank | Ask Claude to open it again and name the agent. |
| "is not a phone number in this Retell workspace" | Calls can only come from numbers in the selected workspace. Ask Claude to list your phone numbers, or [buy a number](/deploy/purchase-number). |
| The call is refused with a verification message | Complete [KYC](/accounts/kyc) from the phone number's page in the dashboard. |
| "cannot be called from the connector" or "outside the US and Canada" | The destination is a premium-rate, satellite, or non-US/Canada +1 number. Place the call from the [dashboard or the API](/deploy/outbound-call). |
| "on the do-not-call list" | The contact is marked do-not-call in your workspace. Remove the flag in the dashboard if you have consent to call them. |
| "reached the connector's outbound call limit" | Wait for the hourly window to reset, or place the call from the dashboard. |
| A confirmation "expired" or "was already used" | Ask Claude to prepare the action again, then confirm the new preview. |
| The dashboard link email didn't arrive | Check your spam folder. If your login's email isn't verified, the connector says so instead of sending. |
| "The dashboard link was already emailed" | The link can be sent 3 times an hour. Use the earlier email, or open the dashboard directly. |
| Changing a custom function's URL is refused | The function has headers or query parameters saved in the dashboard, and the new URL is on a different host, so they would be sent there. Change the URL in the dashboard, where you can update the credentials at the same time. |
| A custom function URL is refused | Remove the key, token, or password from the URL, create the agent, then add it as a header or query parameter in the dashboard. For a webhook whose secret is the URL itself, such as Slack, Discord, Zapier, Make, Telegram, IFTTT or Microsoft Teams, add the whole function in the dashboard. If the message says the URL isn't valid, use the full address, such as `https://api.example.com/lookup`. |
| Claude can't edit an agent's prompt or functions | The agent is a conversation flow agent. Edit it in the dashboard. |

## FAQ

> [accordion] Is this the same as the Retell MCP server?
>
> No. The connector signs in with your Retell login through OAuth and shows widgets in the chat. The [Retell MCP server](/get-started/mcp-server) uses a Retell API key and exposes the Retell API through three generic tools, for clients such as Cursor and Claude Code.

> [accordion] Why does Claude ask which workspace to use?
>
> Your Retell login belongs to more than one workspace, and every tool acts on one of them. Tell Claude which one by name, or ask for the workspace picker. The choice is remembered.

> [accordion] Why does deploying ask me to confirm a replacement?
>
> Another agent is already on the number you picked. The panel shows which one. Confirm to move the number to your agent, or pick a different number.

> [accordion] Can Claude set up Cal.com booking for my agent?
>
> No. Connect Cal.com or another calendar on the dashboard's **Integrations** page, where Retell stores the credentials. You can then add its booking functions to your agents in the dashboard. See [Cal.com](/integrations/cal-com). If an agent still has the older per-agent Cal.com functions, Claude can edit the rest of the agent but can't change or remove those functions. Manage them in the dashboard.

# Retell CLI
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/cli

Install the Retell CLI to manage agents, phone numbers, knowledge bases, and other Retell resources from your terminal with simple commands.

## Overview

The Retell CLI lets you manage Retell resources from your terminal. See the [`@retell-ai/retell-cli` npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@retell-ai/retell-cli) for the full CLI reference. For application code, use a [Retell SDK](/get-started/sdk).

## Get started

**1. Install the CLI**

Requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22 or later.

```bash theme={"dark"}
npm install --global @retell-ai/retell-cli
```

**2. Authenticate**

With a Retell [API key](/accounts/manage-api-keys), run:

```bash theme={"dark"}
retell auth login
```

Enter your API key when prompted.

**3. Run a command**

For example, list your agents:

```bash theme={"dark"}
retell list-agents
```

Run `retell --help` to see all available commands.


# Create voice agent with TypeScript SDK
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/create-agent-with-sdk

Create a Retell AI phone agent with the TypeScript SDK in Node.js: configure its prompt, voice, webhook, call limits, testing, and published version.

Create a Retell voice agent with the TypeScript SDK by creating a Retell LLM response engine and attaching it to a voice configuration. This example builds an after-hours receptionist, returns the resource IDs, and leaves the first agent version as a draft for testing.

## When to use this workflow

Use this workflow when you manage agent configuration in source code or provision agents for multiple customers. If you already have an agent and only need to place calls, use the [create phone call API](/api-references/create-phone-call) instead.

The example creates an after-hours receptionist for a heating company. It collects the caller's name, callback number, address, and reason for calling without promising a price or appointment time.

## Before you start

You need:

* Node.js 18.10 or later.
* A Retell [API key](/accounts/manage-api-keys).
* A voice ID from the [voice library](/build/platform-voices).
* An HTTPS endpoint if you want to receive [call event webhooks](/features/webhook-overview). The webhook is optional in this example.

## Create the agent

**1. Install the SDK and TypeScript runner**

Create a Node.js project and install the dependencies:

```bash theme={"dark"}
npm init -y
npm install retell-sdk
npm install --save-dev tsx
```

**2. Set environment variables**

Export the API key and voice ID you copied from the dashboard. Set the webhook URL only if your endpoint is ready to receive call events.

```bash theme={"dark"}
export RETELL_API_KEY="<your Retell API key>"
export RETELL_VOICE_ID="<your voice ID>"
# Optional: uncomment after your webhook endpoint is ready.
# export RETELL_WEBHOOK_URL="https://example.com/retell/webhook"
```

Keep the API key in your server environment or secret manager. Do not expose it in browser code or commit it to source control.

**3. Create the response engine and agent**

Save this file as `create-agent.ts`:

```typescript theme={"dark"}
import Retell from "retell-sdk";

function requireEnv(name: "RETELL_API_KEY" | "RETELL_VOICE_ID"): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) {
    throw new Error(`Set ${name} before running this script.`);
  }
  return value;
}

const apiKey = requireEnv("RETELL_API_KEY");
const voiceId = requireEnv("RETELL_VOICE_ID");
const webhookUrl = process.env.RETELL_WEBHOOK_URL;

const client = new Retell({ apiKey });

async function main() {
  const llm = await client.llm.create({
    start_speaker: "agent",
    begin_message:
      "Thanks for calling Northstar Heating after hours. How can I help?",
    general_prompt: `
You are the after-hours receptionist for Northstar Heating.

Your job:
- Ask for the caller's full name, callback number, service address, and reason for calling.
- Ask one question at a time.
- Read the details back and ask the caller to confirm them.
- Do not promise pricing, appointment times, or technician availability.
- Tell the caller that the office will follow up during business hours.
- When the caller confirms there is nothing else they need, use the end_call tool.
    `.trim(),
    general_tools: [
      {
        type: "end_call",
        name: "end_call",
        description:
          "End the call after the caller confirms the collected details and has no more questions.",
      },
    ],
  });

  console.log(`Created Retell LLM: ${llm.llm_id}`);

  const agent = await client.agent.create({
    agent_name: "Northstar after-hours receptionist",
    response_engine: {
      type: "retell-llm",
      llm_id: llm.llm_id,
    },
    voice_id: voiceId,
    language: "en-US",
    max_call_duration_ms: 15 * 60 * 1_000,
    end_call_after_silence_ms: 2 * 60 * 1_000,
    ...(webhookUrl ? { webhook_url: webhookUrl } : {}),
  });

  console.log(`Created agent: ${agent.agent_id}`);
  console.log(`Draft version: ${agent.version}`);
}

main().catch((error) => {
  if (error instanceof Retell.APIError) {
    console.error(`Retell API error ${error.status}: ${error.message}`);
  } else {
    console.error(error);
  }
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
```

The example sets English explicitly, caps calls at 15 minutes, and ends a call after 2 minutes of silence. As of July 2026, `max_call_duration_ms` accepts 1 minute to 2 hours, while `end_call_after_silence_ms` has a 10-second minimum and a 10-minute default. Because `model` is omitted, the Retell LLM uses the endpoint's default text model.

If `RETELL_WEBHOOK_URL` is set, the agent-level webhook replaces the account-level webhook for this agent.

**4. Run the script**

Run the TypeScript file:

```bash theme={"dark"}
npx tsx create-agent.ts
```

A successful run prints the Retell LLM ID, agent ID, and draft version:

```text theme={"dark"}
Created Retell LLM: llm_...
Created agent: agent_...
Draft version: 0
```

## Test and publish the agent

Open the new agent in the dashboard and run a [web call test](/test/test-web). A draft can be tested without publishing or assigning a phone number.

When the draft is ready, publish it from the dashboard version panel or call the [publish agent API](/api-references/publish-agent) with the `agent_id` and `version` printed by the script. Published versions are immutable. See [agent versioning](/agent/version) before you attach a version or environment tag to a [phone number](/deploy/purchase-number).

If you configured a webhook, [verify its signature](/features/secure-webhook) before processing call events.

## Common questions

> [accordion] Why does the example make two API calls?
>
> The response engine and voice agent are separate resources. `client.llm.create()` defines what the agent says and which tools it can use. `client.agent.create()` attaches that response engine to voice and call settings.

> [accordion] What happens if agent creation fails after the Retell LLM is created?
>
> The Retell LLM remains available because the two create calls are not atomic. Reuse its `llm_id` on the next attempt, or remove it with the [delete Retell LLM API](/api-references/delete-retell-llm).

> [accordion] Do I need to publish before testing?
>
> No. Test the draft with a browser web call first. Publish it when you are ready to use an immutable version for a phone number or environment tag.


# Global search
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/global-search

Use global search in the Retell AI dashboard to find agents, calls, chats, Conductor conversations, and documentation, then open a result or create an agent.

Global search finds agents, calls, chats, your Conductor conversations, and public Retell Docs from anywhere in the dashboard. Open it from **Search & create** in the sidebar or press **⌘K** on Mac or **Ctrl+K** on Windows and Linux.

## When to use global search

Use search when you know a name, an ID, or a phrase from the content you need. For example, search `reschedule` to find an appointment agent whose prompt handles rescheduling, a matching call transcript, or a Conductor conversation about that workflow.

For date ranges, outcomes, or other session filters, use [Call History or Chat History](/features/session-history).

## Search and open a result

**1. Open search**

Click **Search & create** in the sidebar or use **⌘K** / **Ctrl+K**.

You can also click **Search agents** on the Agents page to start in the **Agents** category, or **Search chats** on Home to start in **Conductor**. These page entry points start with an empty query. The sidebar and keyboard shortcut reopen your previous query and category.

**2. Enter a query**

Type at least 2 characters. Results appear as you type. Choose a category to narrow the results, or **All** to search across categories.

**3. Open a match**

Click a result, or use **↑** / **↓** to highlight one and press **Enter**. Agents open in the builder, calls and chats open their detail panels, and Conductor results reopen the conversation. Retell Docs results open in a new browser tab.

Press **Esc** to close search.

![Global search with voicemail entered and Retell Docs selected. Results include Handle voicemail and IVR, with matching text highlighted in result snippets.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/JY6yKSKuVSbpTsjx/images/global-search-results.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=JY6yKSKuVSbpTsjx\&q=85\&s=fb1ed9c7bc1e7507861893e2143361a8)

Search for voicemail and choose Retell Docs to find related guides.

## What can you search?

| Category | Searchable content |
| - | - |
| **Agents** | Agent names, IDs, and text in prompts and configuration, such as node instructions and tool descriptions. |
| **Calls** | Call IDs, summaries, and transcripts. |
| **Chats** | Chat IDs, summaries, and messages exchanged with your agents. |
| **Conductor** | Titles, conversation IDs, and message text from your own [Conductor conversations](/conductor/overview#manage-your-conversations). |
| **Retell Docs** | Public documentation. |

Workspace results respect your permissions and the workspace you have selected. **Chats** contains conversations with your agents; **Conductor** contains your conversations with the dashboard's AI assistant.

## Recent searches and quick actions

Press **Enter** to submit a query, or open a result, to add the query to **Recent Searches**. Clear the search field to see recent searches, then click one to run it again. **Clear history** removes the recent queries without deleting any resources or conversations.

With the search field empty, **Quick actions** lets you create a voice or chat agent, view your agents, or open Analytics or Settings. The available actions depend on your permissions. See [Build an agent](/build/overview) for configuration guidance.

## Why can't I find a result?

If search shows **No Results Found**, try a more specific keyword, check the spelling, or switch to **All**. For a known agent or conversation, try its full ID.

Call and chat search depends on retained transcripts and summaries, and older conversations may be outside the search window. Use [Call History or Chat History](/features/session-history#browse-and-filter-sessions) to locate a session by its date or ID. Your workspace's storage settings and your access to sensitive data also affect which content is searchable.


# Retell MCP server for AI assistants
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/mcp-server

Use Retell's MCP server to build and manage voice agents from MCP-capable clients like Cursor, Claude Desktop, and Claude Code via Retell APIs.

## Overview

Retell supports the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) so you can build Retell AI voice agents directly from MCP-capable clients (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex-style tools, and more).

If you're already using Retell via REST or SDKs, MCP is simply a different interface to the same core functionality — optimized for agentic workflows in IDEs and assistants.

To manage Retell from Claude with your Retell login and in-chat widgets instead of an API key, see the [Claude connector](/get-started/claude). For ChatGPT, see [ChatGPT](/get-started/chatgpt).

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page covers Retell's own MCP server, which lets your assistant manage your Retell account. To let one of your agents call an external MCP server's tools during a call, see [MCP tools for single and multi-prompt agents](/build/single-multi-prompt/mcp) or the [MCP node](/build/conversation-flow/mcp-node) for conversation flows.

## What can Retell's MCP server do?

Retell's MCP server gives your AI assistant native access to the Retell platform through a single integration. Depending on your API key permissions and what you enable in your MCP client, an assistant can:

* **Agents**: create, update, publish, list, and fetch agent versions.
* **Calls**: create phone/web calls, fetch call details, list calls, delete calls, update call metadata, run QA and review.
* **Phone numbers**: import, provision, list, and fetch phone numbers.
* **Knowledge base**: create KBs, attach sources, remove sources, list KBs.
* **Voices**: list voices, clone voices, search community voices.
* **Chats**: create chats, create chat agents, end chats, update chat metadata.
* **Testing & QA**: create test cases, run tests, list/rerun QA, submit scores.
* **Alerts & webhooks**: create/list alert rules, list incidents, test webhooks.

## How it works

* **Runtime**: MCP clients connect to a hosted (remote) MCP endpoint over Streamable HTTP, authenticate with your Retell API key, then call tools.
* **Tools**: the server lists three tools instead of one tool per API endpoint, so the tool list stays small enough for your assistant's context window. Your assistant uses them in order:
  1. `list_api_endpoints` returns each endpoint's name, HTTP method, path, and summary. It accepts an optional `search` filter.
  2. `get_api_endpoint_schema` returns the JSON input schema for one endpoint, such as `updateAgent`.
  3. `invoke_api_endpoint` checks the arguments against that schema and calls the Retell API.
* **Coverage**: deprecated endpoints aren't available. If a call includes an argument that isn't in the endpoint's schema, the server returns an error that names the argument and doesn't call the Retell API. Values that can take several shapes, such as `response_engine`, are sent to the API as given.

## Prerequisites

* A Retell API key ([get one here](/accounts/manage-api-keys))
* An MCP client (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, etc.)
* Retell MCP server URL: `https://mcp.retellai.com`

**Authentication header format:**

```
Authorization: Bearer <RETELL_API_KEY>
```

## Setup

Most clients support remote MCP over HTTP. Configure:

* **URL**: `https://mcp.retellai.com`
* **Headers**: `Authorization: Bearer <RETELL_API_KEY>`

## Client setup

The exact UI differs by client version, but the configuration concepts are the same: server name, URL/transport, and authentication.

>     }
>   }

> ```

> [tab] Claude Desktop

>       "headers": {

>       }
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```

> [tab] Claude Code

> [tab] Lovable

> [tab] Other MCP clients

> If your client supports remote MCP URLs + headers, configure:
>
> * **URL**: `https://mcp.retellai.com`
> * **Header**: `Authorization: Bearer <RETELL_API_KEY>`

## Prompt examples

Try these prompts in your MCP client to get started:

* "List my agents and summarize what each one does."
* "Create a new agent for inbound sales qualification and publish it."
* "Show me the last 20 calls and flag any with low QA scores."
* "Create a knowledge base and attach these sources, then update my agent to use it."
* "Import this phone number and assign it to my agent."
* "Rerun QA on this call and summarize the failure reasons."

## Security considerations

Connecting an LLM to operational tools introduces new risks. The primary risk class unique to LLM workflows is **prompt injection**: untrusted content (like call transcripts, user messages, or knowledge base documents) can include instructions that try to trick the model into taking unintended actions.

Most MCP clients support **"confirm before running tools"**. Keep that enabled and review tool calls carefully. Clients approve tools by name, and every API call goes through `invoke_api_endpoint`. If you always allow that tool, you allow every endpoint your API key can reach, including delete and publish. Approve each `invoke_api_endpoint` call separately and check its `endpoint` and arguments.

### Recommendations

MCP makes it easy to connect powerful tools to an assistant. Treat MCP like giving a programmatic operator access.

* **Use least privilege**: create keys with the minimum permissions needed.
* **Keep keys out of prompts**: store API keys in client secrets/settings, never paste them into chat.
* **Prefer read-first workflows**: fetch the current resource before you update or delete it.
* **Review destructive actions**: approve an `invoke_api_endpoint` call to a delete or publish endpoint only when you asked for that action.
* **Be careful with PII**: call logs and transcripts may contain sensitive data — avoid sending full transcripts back to the model if you don't need them.
* **Use non-production data when possible**: if you're exploring agent behavior or testing workflows, prefer development/sandbox environments.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
| - | - |
| Tools not showing up | Verify the server URL, auth header, and that the client can reach the endpoint. |
| 401 Unauthorized | Confirm `Authorization: Bearer <RETELL_API_KEY>` and that the key is active. |
| Tool call errors | Re-run with smaller inputs, then inspect the returned error payload (many clients surface structured tool errors). |
| `unknown field(s)` error | The endpoint's schema doesn't include the named argument, so the server didn't call the API. Ask your assistant to fetch the schema with `get_api_endpoint_schema` and retry with only the listed fields. |

## Feedback

If you run into issues or have requests for additional MCP capabilities, reach out to our support team at [support@retellai.com](mailto:support@retellai.com).


# Build your first phone agent in 15 minutes
Source: https://docs.retellai.com/get-started/quick-start

Build your first Retell AI phone agent in 15 minutes: create an account, pick a template, test in the dashboard, deploy to a phone number, and make a call.

**Retell** is a platform for building, testing, and deploying **AI phone agents** that hold natural conversations over the phone.

**1. Create your account**

1. Visit the [Retell Dashboard](https://dashboard.retellai.com)
2. Sign up for a new account

New accounts start with \$10 in free trial credits, no payment method required. You'll only need to add one if you want to purchase a phone number.

**2. Create a new agent**

1. Navigate to the "Agents" tab
2. Click "Create an agent"
3. Choose **Single prompt** for your first version. Use **Conversational flow** when you need tighter execution control or less context per node; see [Choose an agent type](/build/choose-agent-type).
4. Choose how to start: click **Build from scratch** to build everything yourself, pick a ready-made template like Receptionist or Insurance Verification Caller, or click **Generate from prompt** (marked Suggested) to let [Conductor](/conductor/create-agent) draft an agent from a plain-English description of your use case

![Create agent dialog: pick a Single prompt or Conversational flow type, then choose Build from scratch, the suggested Generate from prompt option, or a ready-made template like Insurance Verification Caller.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/MoqZ2YN1eciIk62m/images/create-agent-templates.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=MoqZ2YN1eciIk62m\&q=85\&s=2502d0beee48e4743dbfb0477e4ccb2d)

**3. Test your agent**

1. Click the "Test" button to start a web call with your agent
2. Allow microphone access when your browser prompts for it, then talk to your agent like a real caller

This step is free and doesn't need a phone number or payment method. You can test a draft agent this way as many times as you want before publishing it.

![Test Audio panel with Run Test and a notice that call transfer is not supported in Webcall.](https://mintcdn.com/retellai/Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k/images/agent-settings-test-playground.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Mg1hiS-BnevMo90k\&q=85\&s=65e24197fa12818ede79b02ae8bed91a)

Use Run Test in the Test Audio panel for a browser test call.

**4. Deploy to a phone number**

1. Go to the "Phone Numbers" tab

Retell-managed numbers are US and Canada only: \$2 per month for normal phone numbers, \$5 per month for toll-free phone numbers. If you need a number from another country or want to bring your own telephony provider, see [custom telephony](/deploy/custom-telephony) instead.

* Receive incoming calls
* Make outbound calls

> No. Web call testing (step 3) works on a draft, unpublished agent with no payment method or phone number required. You only need a number once you want to make or receive real phone calls.
